## §G GOAL
Browser WebGPU node compositor: typed graph → compiled pass plan → live multi-branch preview, dark pro-tool UI, agent-drivable via 1 semantic command bus. Phase 0 + Phase 1 of `docs/vgpu-visual-node-compositor-implementation-handoff.md` only.

## §C CONSTRAINTS

### stack (locked)
- React 19 + TypeScript strict + Vite. pnpm.
- graph UI: `@xyflow/react`. presentation & gesture only.
- GPU: `vgpu` (vercel-labs), exact pinned version.
- state: `zustand` + `immer`. selective subscriptions.
- panes: `react-resizable-panels`. persisted layout.
- shader editor: CodeMirror 6 (⊥ Monaco — bundle size, theming to tokens).
- primitives: Radix UI, fully restyled.
- style: CSS vars + CSS modules. ⊥ Tailwind.
- validation: `zod`.
- test: `vitest` (unit + `vgpu/mock`), Dawn headless node render, `playwright` browser.
- persist: versioned JSON, ext `.loom.json`.

### point model — unified pointset (TD POP analog), Phase 2/3
ONE data model. mesh = points + topology. particles = points w/o topology. ⊥ SOP/POP split.
- storage = structure-of-arrays: 1 buffer per attribute. kills WGSL alignment pain; op binds only what it touches.
- arbitrary named attributes day 1. WGSL structs CODE-GENERATED from attribute schema.
- kernel ABI: `fn process(p: Point, ctx) -> Point`. `Point` codegen'd. versioned (`contractVersion`), fusion-ready.
- per-point RNG = `hash(seed, pointId, frame)`. `pointId` = identity, ⊥ slot index.
- GPU-driven lifecycle from start via scan/prefix-sum COMPACTION, ⊥ atomics — atomics ⊥ deterministic, would break V45 + headless parity. cost = 2-3 extra passes, nothing else.
- render spine: sprites → instances → mesh.
- TOP↔POP bridges: `TextureToAttribute` (P3a), splat-to-texture (P3b), audio/pointer via resolver seam (V61). one instrument, ⊥ two apps.

slices:
- P3a (late Phase 2, beside audio-reactive): pointset core, SoA buffers, attribute codegen, custom per-point WGSL kernel node, sprite render, viewer + attribute spreadsheet, `TextureToAttribute`. flagship demo = audio-driven particles.
- P3b: neighbors (flocking, SPH) — kernel ABI reserves the slot. indirect instancing, trails, splat-to-texture.
- P3c: handoff §35.6 3D scene.

gates:
- P3a exit: audio-reactive 100k particles @ 60fps 1080p · seed-identical browser vs headless · agent builds a variant via patch + verifies via `render_preview` + `read_points`.
- P3b exit: flocking 50k + indirect instancing + trails, 10-min stable resource count.

TOP RISK: attribute→WGSL codegen = new center of gravity. own task, heavily tested, headless.
⊥ a side effect of writing the first node.

### example projects — executable specs, ⊥ demos

regression fixture, and documents the concept it proves. an example that ⊥ load = a
release blocker, ⊥ a docs chore.

buildable w/ what exists (18 nodes + Feedback + CustomWGSL):
- **E1 Feedback Echo** — Noise → Over → Output, w/ Feedback → Transform → Blur → Level
  closing the loop. proves: explicit temporal boundary, fade+transform inside loop,
  branch preview, reset, ping-pong stability over 10 min (T49 gate).
- **E2 Reaction-Diffusion** — Feedback → CustomWGSL (Gray-Scott kernel) → Feedback.
  proves: iterative sim via render feedback, seeded init (V45), pause|step|reset,
  rgba16float precision path, determinism browser vs headless (V47).
- **E3 Animated Noise Field** — Noise (perlin4d, t4d ← time) → Level → Displace ← Noise.
  proves: time reaches shader via `FrameEvaluationInput` ⊥ wall clock (V44), fan-out
  rendered once (V6), 4D noise as the TD animation idiom.
- **E4 Bloom** — Threshold → Blur → Add ← source. proves: multi-branch converge,
  HDR rgba16float intermediate, per-node format override (V51).
- **E5 Kaleidoscope** — Transform → Tile/mirror → Transform. proves: extend modes,
  resolution override (V50), cheap chain @ high res.
- **E6 Displacement Stack** — Noise → Level → Transform → Displace. proves: `data` vs
  `linear` space discipline (V56/V57) — displacement input ⊥ color-converted.

later, when deps land: media mixer (needs image/video nodes), particle trails +
audio-reactive (P3a), 3D scene (P3c), agent-built visual (§35.7, agent gate).

### three libraries, three verbs (TD: OP Create dialog | Palette | example projects)
- **node library** — a TYPE. verb = ADD. already exists.
- **component library** — a reusable subgraph (TD Palette / `.tox`). verb = INSTANTIATE into the
  current graph, linked or detached, at a pinned version (V79, V84). shipped set + user-saved.
- **example library** — a whole PROJECT. verb = OPEN, which REPLACES the open document.

⊥ merge into one browser. the verbs differ, and merging puts a DESTRUCTIVE action (open
replaces your work) one click from an additive one. examples ! confirm when the document
is dirty; add/instantiate ! never confirm — they are undoable.

shipped components (handoff §31.4, buildable w/ current catalogue):
FeedbackEcho · Bloom · DisplacementStack · MediaGrade · Kaleidoscope.

### latency-compensated person masking

`MatteCut` is a starter component with one picture input and an alpha-masked output.
Movie File In, Webcam In, and Screen In can feed it. Its internal Matte shares that
input with Cache; the Cache tap reads `op('matte1').chan.cacheFrames`. That channel
counts encoded render occurrences from the actually sampled input to the next encode,
including the live effect-to-compute submission offset. Project frame indices can skip
or wrap and must not select cached render history. `delaySeconds` measures input age,
including inference latency; completion timestamps are used only for inference rate.

The component publishes model, smoothing, history length, and cache scale. It defaults
to MediaPipe, smoothing 1, 24 half-scale history frames. Smoothing below 1 deliberately
blends different masks and therefore cannot match one source frame exactly. Before a
first result, or when the matching frame is unavailable, the output is transparent.
Cache supports tap 0 for the current completed write pass; `strictHistory` explicitly
rejects unavailable history with transparency. Its existing nonstrict warmup/clamping
policy remains the default. Input texture provenance is invalidated on allocation,
resize, and clear. The component uses the normal authoring commands and save format.

### media needs a resource kind that ⊥ exist yet
`ResourceDescriptor` = target | pingPong | sampler | buffer | bufferPair. **⊥ way to
carry a texture the CPU supplies.** ∀ current resource is GPU-allocated & GPU-written;
a decoded frame comes from outside. ∴ media is blocked on plan-IR work, ⊥ on node work —
worth knowing before anyone starts w/ the node.

```ts
interface ExternalTextureResourceDescriptor {
  kind: "externalTexture";
  id: string;
  size: readonly [number, number];
  format: TextureFormat;
  /** Who supplies frames. The runtime uploads; the plan ⊥ carry pixels (V63 clone-safe). */
  sourceId: string;
}
```
`sourceId` ⊥ the pixels: the plan stays structured-clone-safe (V63) ∴ worker-movable. the
runtime holds a registry `sourceId → MediaSource` and uploads on frame-ready.

### media as NODES (TD Movie File In / Movie File Out TOP)
recording belongs ∈ the GRAPH, ⊥ a global "record" button. TD makes it a node ∴ TOPOLOGY
decides what is recorded: an intermediate branch, several outputs at once, a pass you are
debugging — ⊥ only whatever the single main output happens to be.

- **MovieFileIn** — ONE node for STILL, SEQUENCE and VIDEO, as TD's Movie File In TOP is.
  ⊥ a separate ImageIn: the param set overlaps almost entirely (file, color space, alpha,
  filter/wrap, native res) and 2 nodes would mean choosing the wrong one before you know
  what the file is. a still simply has no timeline — playback params HIDE when the loaded
  asset has 1 frame, ⊥ sit there inert (V90: ⊥ show a control that does nothing).
  **NOTHING loads a file today** — the catalogue is entirely procedural, so this is the
  first node that reads from disk and the first real consumer of `AssetReference`.
  image | video | sequence → texture. play/pause/seek/loop/rate, in|out
  points, native res, current time, duration, frame-ready event. asset by `AssetReference`,
  ⊥ a raw path (V10). decode behind a media-source abstraction: `HTMLVideoElement` first,
  WebCodecs later where it measurably wins.
  Browser image source extent is independent of output extent: upload the whole decoded
  image, then fit it into the Common output resolution. Project limits constrain output,
  ⊥ crop an oversized source at origin. Common **Image fit** defaults Fit (whole image,
  aspect preserved, transparent margins); Fill crops centrally; Stretch fills and changes
  aspect. File inputs keep project resolution by default; loading a file never overwrites
  Common. Sources beyond the physical device texture limit report an explicit error.
  Movie **Audio** enables embedded soundtrack playback on the SAME video element and
  transport; Volume controls monitoring. Default off preserves existing silent projects.
  Still images have no audio; offline rendering and export do not monitor to speakers.
  In realtime free run the playing element is the clock: the playhead adopts its position
  and `playbackRate` equals Speed (§V1027). Under the timeline lock the frame stays master:
  no correction within one frame, then whole 1% rate steps up to ±5%, and one seek only
  past 0.25 s of drift (§T1549b). A driven Speed integrates in free run (§B187). Cues, scrubs, trim edits and laps align explicitly;
  known collapsed windows and Hold Last pause. Native position precision must not
  retrigger a held seek every frame.
- **DeviceIn** (TD Video Device In TOP) — webcam | capture device → texture. SEPARATE node
  from MovieFileIn, as TD keeps them: the param sets barely overlap (device pick, resolution
  negotiation vs file + playback), and V122's hide-what-⊥-apply would hide most of either.
  rides the SAME `externalTexture` + media-source registry (T229) — a webcam is another
  `MediaSource`, ⊥ a subsystem.
  what a FILE never has to handle, and ∀ of it is normal ⊥ exceptional:
  permission denied · no device · device unplugged mid-stream · another app takes the camera ·
  tab backgrounded · resolution ⊥ what you asked for.
- **Screen In** — browser tab | window | screen → texture through the SAME external
  media-source registry. Inspector Share opens `getDisplayMedia` directly from the user
  gesture; project restoration never opens the picker. Capture is video-only, session-owned,
  and live/non-reproducible. Stop, browser-ended sharing, node mute/bypass/removal, project
  replacement and page exit release every capture track. Re-share keeps the current source
  until a replacement is ready; refusal reports explicitly. Intrinsic size changes resize
  source storage at the backend's frame prelude; Common output resolution stays independent,
  including nested component instances. Decoded frames alone advance the upload identity;
  no extra animation loop or CPU pixel copy.
- **MovieFileOut** — a texture input → an encoded file. rides T111's WebCodecs mp4 +
  exact-frame capture. IS A SINK (V25) ∴ ⊥ pruned; recording is its side effect.

both are Phase 2 (media pipeline, doc §33) — but the SHAPE is decided now, because
"recording is a node" changes who owns the export interface, and retrofitting a global
recorder into a node model is a rewrite.

### node catalog guideline
TD TOP family = reference vocabulary for core node set — naming, param names, default behavior.
map where it maps, ⊥ clone. POP/SOP families → later phase, same approach.
per-node parity notes ∈ node manifest `description`, ⊥ ∈ spec.

Variant retention: a definition may declare `retainedParameterKeys` for known settings
intentionally kept while its effective schema omits them. Compiler recognizes only these
dormant keys; it does not resolve or expose them. Matte derives this list from its model
schemas, preserving Backend, Input Size and RVM detail pins across model switches.
Unrelated undeclared keys still warn.

### decided (was open, confirmed 2026-08-29)
- baseline: Chrome/Edge ≥ 128 desktop. min capability Tier B (rgba16float + compute + storage buffers). timestamp query optional. mobile excluded v1.
- headless: seam + CI parity test. ⊥ render queue v1.
- agent authority: graph edit | shader edit | param set = free + undoable, ⊥ confirm. local file | network | upload | export | recording | component install | project delete = capability grant + confirm.
- save: single `.loom.json` + external `AssetReference`. unresolved → relink flow. bundle → Phase 2.

### locked — owner interview 2026-08-29
- color: `space` ∈ `texture2d` port type. linear working space, decode @ load, encode+tonemap @ output only.
- param modulation: resolver invariant AND `ParameterValue` envelope `{kind:"static",value}` | reserved bound — both land now, before ∀ `.loom.json` ∈ wild. envelope passthrough lane fixes closed-union anti-V10.
- perform mode: full multi-window output = COMMITTED Phase 2 deliverable (multi display, VJ). presentation seam designed now, ⊥ prep-only.
- revision contention: param-only carve-out. value-only edits on disjoint entities ⊥ conflict w/ structural patch. amends V33.
- workers: renderer-in-worker COMMITTED Phase 2. worker owns device + ∀ surfaces; window transfers `OffscreenCanvas` in = also multi-window transport. v1 main-thread + clone-safe invariant + DOM-free lint + non-rAF loop.
- audio-reactive: early Phase 2 headline. AudioIn (mic|file) → analysis (FFT bands, beat, envelope) → params via resolver. first consumer proving modulation arch. WebMIDI alongside. OSC → Phase 3 (needs bridge).
- expressions: own minimal grammar. jsep-style AST, whitelisted fns, vars only ← `FrameEvaluationInput` + node ctx. deterministic + sandboxed by construction. v1 = arithmetic only, 1 evaluator module.
- autosave: IndexedDB ring. 2s debounce after last mutation. keep last 20 + 1 per 10min pinned, pins capped 48 (~8h; ⊥ multi-day session fills quota). restore-on-launch prompt. manual save still writes `.loom.json`. `serialize.ts` = sole serializer, shared w/ manual save.
- recording: first realtime export = WebCodecs → mp4 (`VideoEncoder`, exact-frame capture ← render loop). ⊥ MediaRecorder stopgap. Chrome ≥128 guarantees WebCodecs.

### open ? — ⊥ blocking Phase 0/1
- extension trust: declarative graph + manifest + WGSL only, ⊥ 3rd-party JS. ?
- 3D scope: doc §36.6 option 1 — procedural + loaded geometry → texture graph. ?
- when deterministic media seek + stateful-sim checkpoints enter roadmap. ?
- perform mode display-selection UX: single fullscreen toggle vs true multi-window. ?

### kernel ABI
```wgsl
fn process(p: Point, ctx: KernelContext) -> Point
```
`Point` struct codegen'd from attribute schema. `ctx` carries frame input + `pointId`.
`NodeDefinition.contractVersion` pins ABI; mismatch → diagnostic, ⊥ silent run.

### type: component (COMP) — subgraph behind a stable interface
```ts
interface GraphComponentDefinition {
  componentId: ComponentId;
  version: number;
  name: string;
  graph: GraphDocument;              // internal network
  inputs: ExposedPort[];             // internal port → external port
  outputs: ExposedPort[];
  parameters: PublishedParameter[];  // internal params → component param page
  migrations?: ComponentMigration[];
  description?: string;
  capabilities?: CapabilityRequirement[];  // what the internal network needs (V38)
}

interface ExposedPort { externalId: PortId; label: string; nodeId: NodeId; portId: PortId; }

/** One component param drives N internal targets — TD binds a custom par to many. */
interface PublishedParameter {
  key: string;                       // name on the component's param page
  definition: ParameterDefinition;   // label, range, unit, default — re-authored, ⊥ copied
  targets: ReadonlyArray<{ nodeId: NodeId; key: string }>;
}
```
instance stores `componentId` + `version` + own param values + overrides.
⊥ duplicate internal graph unless detached.

### parent scope
child reads owning component's params via resolver (V61): `parent.<key>`.
resolves ∀ nesting depth by walking up instance chain. ⊥ arbitrary cross-node reads —
`parent` = lexical, ⊥ a graph edge.

### type: context menu (right-click) — data, ⊥ hardcoded
```ts
interface MenuTarget {
  surface: "canvas" | "node" | "port" | "edge" | "parameter";
  nodeId?: NodeId; portId?: PortId; edgeId?: EdgeId; parameterKey?: string;
}
interface MenuItem {
  command: CommandName;   // ⊥ inline handler — same path as hotkey + palette (V29, V52)
  input?: unknown;
  label: string;
  when?: string;
  submenu?: MenuItem[];
}
```
ONE menu root per surface, target resolved from event on open. ⊥ Radix root per node —
dense graph cost. keys rendered ← keymap (V55), ⊥ literal "⌘Z" strings.

### parameter modes — TD parity (verified vs docs.derivative.ca)
TD: ∀ parameter has a MODE. click the param NAME to expand → 4 square mode buttons.
grey=Constant · blue=Expression · green=Export(CHOP-driven) · purple=Bind(bi-directional).
right-click = popup menu. ctrl/cmd+E = edit the expression.

**THE DETAIL THAT MATTERS**: an inactive mode that HAS a value shows a small square ∈ the
button's lower-left corner. ∴ **each mode retains its own value independently** — switching
to Constant ⊥ destroys the expression. that is why the indicator exists, and it is what
makes mode-switching safe to experiment with.

```ts
type ParameterBinding =
  | { kind: "static"; value: ParameterValue }
  | { kind: "expression"; source: string }            // OUR grammar (V71), ⊥ Python
  | { kind: "bind"; ref: string }                     // another param | `parent.<key>`
  | { kind: "driven"; channel: string };              // TD Export analog — audio|MIDI|LFO, Phase 2

interface ParameterSlot {
  mode: ParameterBinding["kind"];
  /** EVERY mode's last value, kept. mode switch ⊥ destructive. */
  bindings: Partial<Record<ParameterBinding["kind"], ParameterBinding>>;
}
```
∀ parameter TYPE takes ∀ mode — number, vector, color, bool, enum, string alike. ⊥ a
number-only feature: TD drives menus + toggles from expressions & that is half its power.

### Composite node + individual blend nodes — BOTH, sharing one implementation
TD ships a Composite TOP w/ an Operation menu AND standalone Add/Multiply/etc. keep both:
- **Composite** — variadic inputs + an `operation` ENUM. flexible: change the blend w/o
  rewiring, drive the mode by expression (V107), reach a mode you ⊥ have a node for.
- **Over/Add/Multiply/Screen/Difference** — fixed operation. a graph reading `Multiply`
  says what it does at a glance; `Composite` makes you open it. when you KNOW the op, the
  named node is the better documentation.

**⊥ two implementations of the blend math.** blend fns live ∈ 1 WGSL module; Composite
selects @ compile time; a named node binds a fixed selection of the SAME fn. else Over ∈
Composite and the Over node drift & only one gets the bug fix.

`operation` is `compileTime: true` — it changes the SHADER, ⊥ a uniform. specialise per
mode (the shader cache already keys on constants) ⊥ branch per pixel: a per-pixel switch
on a value that changes ~never is the wrong trade, and V5's uniform-only fast path stays
meaningful only if mode changes are honestly classified as structural.

### variadic inputs (1+n) — the mechanism exists, ⊥ node uses it
`PortDefinition.variadic` is ∈ the contract, honored by the patch layer (V14), the
compiler (`CompiledInputBinding` is an ARRAY per port), and the canvas. **⊥ production
node declares one** — only test fixtures. same shape as feedback before T152: every layer
built, nothing reaching it.

Composite (Over/Add/Multiply/Screen/Difference) is the obvious first consumer — TD's
Composite TOP is multi-input. Also: Switch, Merge, and any "combine N of these" op.

**THE GAP THAT MATTERS**: edges into one port currently arrive in EDGE-ID order — i.e.
creation order — and `GraphEdge` carries no ordering field. For Over, **layer order IS the
operation**. Wiring a third layer would land it wherever its id sorted, and reordering
would mean deleting and rewiring. ∴ a variadic port needs an EXPLICIT order before any node
can use one.

### node NAMES are identifiers, ⊥ decoration (TD: noise1, noise2, null1)
prerequisite for expressions & binds: `op('noise1').par.period` only works because a name
is UNIQUE within its network. ∴ names must land BEFORE reference syntax, ⊥ after.

- ∀ node has a `name`, unique within its graph. auto-numbered on collision: `noise1`,
  `noise2` — created from the definition type, lowercased.
- rename to a taken name → auto-suffix, ⊥ reject. the user's intent is the WORD; the
  number is bookkeeping.
- `name` (identifier, unique, referenceable) ≠ a comment (free text, ⊥ unique). today's
  `GraphNode.label` conflates them — it is display-only & unconstrained. `label` BECOMES
  the name; a separate comment field arrives when someone wants one.
- rename ! rewrite references that named it, or the rename silently breaks a bind (V110).
  ∴ rename is a graph-wide patch, ⊥ a node-local one.

**Null node** — TD `null1` idiom: 1 in, 1 out, passes through untouched. exists to be a
STABLE REFERENCE POINT: reference `null1` & rewire upstream freely w/o touching any
reference. cheap (⊥ pass emitted — compiler passes the binding through), and the standard
place to park a bookmark ∈ a big graph.

### pulse parameters (TD Pulse) — momentary triggers
TD: `Pulse` is a parameter TYPE, ⊥ a per-node feature. Feedback TOP has Reset; Timer has
Start/Stop. ∴ ANY node can declare one and the mechanism is written once.

```ts
interface PulseParameter extends ParameterBase { type: "pulse"; }
```
- momentary: it FIRES, it ⊥ hold. never serialized as "on" — a pulse ∈ a saved doc that
  re-fires on load would reset your work every time you opened it.
- mutates RUNTIME state, ⊥ document state ∴ audited (V31) but **⊥ undoable**: undo restores
  a document, and a cleared feedback buffer is ⊥ ∈ the document. saying so beats a
  disabled undo that silently does nothing.
- takes ∀ mode (V107) — an EXPRESSION firing a pulse is how an automated reset happens
  (TD's whole idiom: pulse on a beat, on a threshold, on a frame count).
- TD also pairs a HOLD toggle w/ the momentary pulse (Feedback TOP has both). support both:
  `reset` (hold ∈ reset) + `resetPulse` (fire once).

a node declaring `stateful.reset === true` (V46, already ∈ the contract) SHOULD expose one
— that field has been declaring the capability w/ nothing to trigger it.
consumers: Feedback (clear), Noise (reseed), accumulator (clear), point sim (reset),
MovieFileIn (re-fetch).

### compound parameters are COMPONENT-ADDRESSABLE (TD: colorr/colorg/colorb, tx/ty/tz)
TD has ⊥ "a color parameter" — it has `colorr`, `colorg`, `colorb`, each a first-class
parameter w/ its OWN mode. the swatch is a convenience ON TOP. same for `tx`/`ty`/`tz`.
that is what makes a single channel drivable while the others stay constant.

ours: the MANIFEST keeps one declaration (`color`, `t`) — verbose 4-way manifests would
be worse — but the SLOT is per component:
```
color  → color.r  color.g  color.b  color.a
t      → t.x      t.y      t.z      (t.w for size 4)
```
∀ component gets its own `ParameterSlot` ∴ its own mode, expression, bind, value.
resolver reassembles components → the compound value the shader wants.
component names: r g b a · x y z w.

### type: per-node output resolution override (TD Common page)
```ts
type NodeResolutionOverride =
  | { mode: "auto" }                                   // node's own ResolutionPolicy — DEFAULT
  | { mode: "project" }                                // project output resolution
  | { mode: "input"; input?: PortId }                  // inherit named input
  | { mode: "scale"; factor: number; input?: PortId }  // 1/8 1/4 1/2 2x 4x 8x
  | { mode: "fixed"; width: number; height: number };  // custom
```
lives on `GraphNode.resolution?`. absent → definition policy. instance state, ⊥ definition state.

TD Output Resolution menu = Use Input | Eighth | Quarter | Half | 2X | 4X | 8X |
Fit Resolution | Limit Resolution | Custom. our `scale` covers eighth..8x, `fixed` = custom.
MISSING: `fit` (fit w/h, keep aspect) + `limit` (clamp w/h). both real, both useful —
`limit` = safety valve. → wave 2 barrier (union growth, tracks E+G reading it now).

### type: per-node pixel format override (TD Common page)
```ts
type NodeFormatOverride =
  | { mode: "auto" }                          // node's own FormatPolicy — DEFAULT
  | { mode: "project" }                       // project workingFormat
  | { mode: "input"; input?: PortId }         // Use Input
  | { mode: "fixed"; format: TextureFormat }; // rgba8unorm | rgba16float | r32float
```
lives on `GraphNode.format?`. depth ⊥ selectable — color outputs only.
`rgba8unorm-srgb` landed @ barrier. `TEXTURE_FORMATS` const = single source, type derived from it.

### Common processing channels and alpha inspection (2026-10-03)

`GraphNode.channelMask?` stores R/G/B/A processing flags; absent/all true means the
unchanged node policy and adds no pass or target. Disabled channels preserve the first
connected texture input (declared port order, then variadic order); generators use
`(0,0,0,1)` for disabled channels. This changes actual output through commands and
validated patches. Components apply masks at exposed output boundaries, preserving
internal consumers; drilled edits are instance overrides. Opted-in output masking adds
one pass and target per texture output. Preserve encoded/linear sampled-space meaning.

Default editor previews/viewer show bounded straight-alpha coverage over a checkerboard
in linear light. Explicit RGB shows raw colour. Backend presentation defaults raw RGB;
editor RGBA inspection is explicit. Canvas remains opaque; display never changes graph
or export payloads. Producer alpha outside [0,1] displays RGB; an Output transform's
existing alpha clamp remains authoritative. This supersedes T1196's old RGB-default
recommendation at the owner's request. Details and evidence:
`docs/channels-components-and-connections-2026-10-03.md`.

Drilled parameter controls read instance-effective compiler values, including nested
instance pages, and write the published owner through the existing command path.
Common occupied-input moves swap wires; Alt-drop replaces. HTML drag destinations
remain stable while live document order changes. MatteCut exposes Cutout plus Mask;
existing output address `out` remains stable.

### module: `src/editor/keymap` — bindings as data
```ts
type KeyContext = "global" | "graph" | "inspector" | "viewer" | "text";

interface KeyBinding {
  id: string;              // stable, survives rebinding
  keys: string;            // "mod+z", "shift+h", "g d" (chord)
  context: KeyContext;     // narrowest wins; "text" swallows editing keys
  command: CommandName;    // bus command — ⊥ inline handler
  input?: unknown;         // static args, or resolved from selection
  when?: string;           // guard: "hasSelection", "nodeHovered"
  label: string;           // shown in palette, menus, tooltips
}

interface Keymap {
  defaults: KeyBinding[];
  overrides: Record<string, string | null>;  // id → keys, null = unbound
}
```
`mod` = Cmd @ macOS, Ctrl elsewhere. overrides ∈ localStorage, ⊥ ∈ project doc.

### custom WGSL node contract v1
```wgsl
@group(0) @binding(0) var inputSampler: sampler;
@group(0) @binding(1) var inputTexture: texture_2d<f32>;

// Shared frame block — the runtime fills it from FrameEvaluationInput every frame.
// TIME LIVES HERE AND NOWHERE ELSE (V44).
@group(0) @binding(3) var<uniform> frameU: SharedFrame;

struct Params { amount: f32 };
@group(0) @binding(2) var<uniform> params: Params;

@fragment
fn fs(@location(0) uv: vec2f) -> @location(0) vec4f {
  return textureSample(inputTexture, inputSampler, uv);
}
```
`Params` ⊥ carries `time`. per-pass uniform block written @ compile + on param change
(V5, V21) ∴ structurally ⊥ carry a per-frame clock — a `time` field there = a value that
silently never advances. `frameU.time` = its only home.

binding is GATED, ⊥ unconditional: runtime binds by NAME and hard-errors on a name the
shader ⊥ declare (`VGPU-RING1-UNSUPPORTED`). `compile()` scans the source and binds only
what it asked for — a kernel declaring neither block (E2 Gray-Scott) ! still compile.

## §V INVARIANTS

V1: domain graph = truth. React Flow node array ⊥ execution source.
V2: React component ⊥ encode GPU command. WebGPU calls only ∈ `src/runtime/`.
V3: `vgpu` import only ∈ `src/runtime/backend/vgpu/`. lint-enforced.
V4: current-frame graph = DAG. cycle legal ⟺ ∀ path in cycle crosses explicit temporal node.
V5: uniform-value param change → update uniform only. ⊥ recompile.
V6: output w/ N consumers → rendered 1× per frame, texture reused ∀ N.
V7: preview GPU→GPU. readback ⊥ in playback loop — export/inspect/test only.
V8: ⊥ render-target alloc inside frame loop. effects/targets/samplers/buffers created outside.
V9: shader compile fail → last valid plan retained + output flagged stale. ⊥ blank frame.
V10: ∀ serialized doc has `schemaVersion` + per-node `definitionVersion`. unknown node preserved as placeholder, ⊥ dropped.
V11: ∀ node definition runs headless. ⊥ import React or @xyflow.
V12: optional GPU feature discovered via capability report before use. ⊥ assumed.
V13: connect requires exact `PortType` match. ⊥ implicit color-space/format/scalar/resolution conversion. conversion = visible node.
V14: input port accepts ≤ 1 incoming edge unless declared variadic. output fan-out unbounded.
V14b: an EDGE is a valid drop target for a connection. release over the line → the drag takes that edge's TARGET and replaces it. the line is a big target; the port is a 7px dot (V99) — requiring the dot when the wire is right there is asking for precision the task ⊥ need.
V14c: edge hit area ! be generous (~10px each side of the stroke, invisible), same principle as V99. a 1px stroke is ⊥ a target. NOTE the ~10px is a CURSOR tolerance ∈ SCREEN space. a NODE dropped on an edge (V14d) needs a different unit — a band through the node's middle, ¼ height either side, ∈ GRAPH space — & someone will otherwise "correct" it to 10px.
V14d: dropping a NODE on an edge splices it, & the hit test runs ∈ GRAPH space (both the node box & the wire are graph-space facts, unlike a cursor) ∴ identical @ any zoom. a BAND, ⊥ the whole rectangle: rect-vs-curve silently rewires a graph whenever a node is parked near a wire passing behind it, which is far worse than a gesture needing a 2nd try. REFUSE when the node is already an end of the edge, when ⊥ port pair fits (V13), or when the splice would close a loop (V4).
V14e: the drag-onto-edge gesture is SYMMETRIC — a drag begun @ an INPUT takes the edge's SOURCE, mirroring V14b's target case. both ends are draggable & a 1-way gesture reads as a bug.
V14a: dropping a connection on an OCCUPIED input REPLACES the existing edge — 1 patch, 1 undo group (V32, V34). ⊥ silently refuse: the user's intent is unambiguous and refusing makes them hunt for the old edge to delete first.
V15: ∀ semantic edit undoable. continuous drag coalesced → 1 history entry, live values still applied.
V16: per-frame metrics & preview pixels ⊥ enter document store. UI metric refresh ≤ 10 Hz.

### cooking — TD's model, Notch's stateless/stateful split (T249-T256)
TD: cook needs BOTH a REQUEST (downstream | param reference | viewer) & a REASON (input
cooked | param changed | time-dependent | expression resolves ≠). PULL, ⊥ push. cook graph =
wires ∪ PARAMETER REFERENCES. escape hatches @ both ends (Cook Type, Cooking Flag).
Notch: push-traverse active tree from Root ∀ frame, ⊥ dirty mechanism, per-node manual
"static" switches. worse — but 3 ideas better than TD's:
 1. STATELESS vs STATEFUL as a per-node property (the thing TD lacks & we need most)
 2. a frozen node ! COMPUTE ONCE before it may serve cache; clears on reset
 3. CPU+GPU ms together per node, category rollups
TD's own failure worth ⊥ inheriting: dependency system ⊥ total; when it misses it shows a
STALE value as FRESH. documented (`Dependency.modified()` exists for this) & unroot-caused
∈ the field. ∴ our gate is built BEFORE the feature, ⊥ after.

LAYERING — 3 rows, ⊥ 1: compile = does node EXIST. build = which GPU objects REUSED
(carry-over, already built). cook = does this pass RUN THIS FRAME. cooking is only row 3.
unit = NODE ⊥ pass (Blur's 2 passes share a node-private scratch).

V174: ∈ the inspector, PARAMETERS come first & COMMON is a separate TAB (TD's page model) — ⊥ both stacked on 1 page. common is chrome you set once; parameters are the work. prime real estate goes to the work.
V175: a Ramp is N STOPS, ⊥ 2 colours. add|remove|move a stop, position per stop. 2-colour is the degenerate case of the general thing, & shipping only the degenerate case means every gradient anyone actually wants is impossible.
### jitter ∈ `time * k` — ⊥ rounding, it's the CLOCK (B21)
`liveClock` accumulates WALL deltas (clamped, epoch 0 — both already right). but rAF deltas
jitter ~16.6ms ± several ∴ `time` advances NON-UNIFORMLY ∴ `time * 0.15` on a translate
steps unevenly. spatially straight, temporally ragged. ⊥ f32, ⊥ JS rounding — f64 on CPU,
& they already start @ 0 which is the real f32 mitigation.
TD's answer: 2 clocks. `absTime.seconds` = wall. timeline time = frame/fps, UNIFORM BY
CONSTRUCTION. animation uses the timeline one.
TRADE, stated: timeline time means dropped frames SLOW the animation (TD behaves this way);
wall time means dropped frames SKIP it (Notch's "frame-rate independence" = "visually
similar", ⊥ identical). ⊥ 1 right answer ∴ ship both & DEFAULT to smooth.

V202: the frame loop follows the VISIBLE surface. when a perform window is open, IT hosts the scheduler. Chrome clamps rAF to ~1Hz ∈ a non-foreground tab & suspends it entirely after a while ∴ an editor tab backgrounded while a perform window shows output means THE SHOW FREEZES. that is a real failure mode for a TD replacement, ⊥ a test artefact. background timers are throttled too ∴ the robust answers are the perform window's own context, or the worker + OffscreenCanvas already committed for Phase 2.
V203: when rAF cadence COLLAPSES while playing, SAY SO. compare wall time to frame count (cheap) & surface "throttled by the browser". a frozen picture w/ ⊥ explanation is indistinguishable from a bug — & it generated ~6 "nothing animates" reports before anyone worked out what it was.
V209: a heal-on-any-edit path is a LATCH waiting for the edit rate to drop. T258's dirty-preview retry runs @ `backend.compile`, & today EVERY edit lands there ∴ any knob turn heals a dirty preview. wire the classifier & only STRUCTURAL edits land there — a preview that went dirty ∈ a race stays black through any amount of knob-turning. ∴ a recovery path ! be driven by something that happens UNCONDITIONALLY (frame entry), ⊥ by a path an optimisation is about to make conditional. same species as B24's retry gated on a condition only true before the 1st compile.
V210: the compile gate has SEVERAL independent structural triggers & the document revision is only ONE. an input producing ⊥ document edit is INVISIBLE to a document-keyed gate. the enumeration, so it is ⊥ rediscovered 1 at a time:
 (a) SINK SET — opening|closing a preview. ⊥ document edit @ all ∴ nothing to classify. a revision-keyed gate stops materializing a sink the moment someone opens a preview.
 (b) BACKEND CAPABILITIES on device recovery — a plan compiled against tier-B needs recompiling if the recovered adapter differs. covered today: the recovery path rebuilds from the retained plan.
 (c) COMPONENT CATALOGUE edits (V82) — editing a component's INTERNAL graph changes what flattening produces WITHOUT touching the host document. live-ness depends on how component edits reach the store; ⊥ assumed either way, ! be checked.
 (d) `project.setSettings` (T272) — settings are COMPILE INPUT. presumably a document revision, but presumption is the failure mode this invariant exists for.
V218: prefer the EXACT claim; when a range assertion FAILS, ask whether the exact value is derivable before loosening it. T299 asserted "≥4 distinct lit intensities" on a sphere of axis-aligned boxes & got 3 — because two-sided lambert reads |x·L|, |y·L|, |z·L| & `abs` collapses the ± face pairs. the range was the WRONG assertion & the device said so. companion to V147: a range assertion TOLERATES the bug, & a failing one is often the geometry teaching the stronger claim.
V219: a per-shape `vertexCount` would make SHAPE structural. all shapes draw the same 36 verts & shorter ones collapse their tail into ZERO-AREA triangles ∴ switching shape is 1 integer upload & V5 holds. the naive version is correct & silently costs a recompile per shape change.

V585: **an ASYNC node takes the ANALYZE SHAPE — GPU half inside the plan, CPU half outside it.** `compileGraph` is SYNCHRONOUS & PURE ∴ a node's `compile()` cannot await, allocate ∨ read ambient state. the GPU half is an ORDINARY pass reading an **`external` scratch texture** someone else fills (the seam webcam/movie/text already use — ⊥ new resource kind, ⊥ new GPU→CPU route); the CPU half is fire-and-forget w/ an `inFlight` guard & a synchronous `latest` map. **PENDING never makes the plan structural** — a node w/ ⊥ result renders its texture's LAST CONTENTS, which the backend contract already specifies. & an inference node ! **⊥** declare `sink: true` (Analyze does ∵ it has ⊥ outputs) ∴ ordinary pruning applies & a disconnected model node costs zero & DOWNLOADS NOTHING (T384,V25,V335)
V586: **`frame.mode` is the reproducibility seam & branching on it is ⊥ a V44 violation** — V44 forbids `Date.now`/`performance.now`/rAF & REQUIRES consuming `FrameEvaluationInput`; `mode` IS that input. ∴ **offline BLOCKS** (TD's non-realtime flag exactly, & both offline drivers ALREADY `await` per frame ∴ free) while **live uses the latest result & exposes its AGE**. both modes produce the IDENTICAL plan — only the fill policy differs — so V47's "same graph + same compiler" stays literally true. & the offline CACHE KEY is free: `(document revision, frameIndex, seed)`, ⊥ input bytes, ∵ hashing bytes needs the readback we are avoiding (T384,V44,V47,V329)

E34's bounce carries its first-leg verdict as a **parked position + a derived distance**, ⊥ as carried flags — & its author judged that GENUINELY BETTER than the flag version. compile against the BASELINE, ⊥ against the machine you have (T641,V309)

V615: **2 SEAMS CAN PASS EACH OTHER WITHOUT TOUCHING, & an invariant can promise a loop the catalogue cannot close.** V144 exists for image→parameter→image; `analyze` publishes a MEASURED channel; the value graph processes VALUE PORTS; & **⊥ door connects them** — analyze has ⊥ outputs, the driven envelope is unity-gain, expressions cannot see channels. ∴ **every value-processing node ∈ the catalogue is unreachable from the one node whose output most wants processing.** an invariant w/ ⊥ example is ⊥ merely undemonstrated — it may be UNBUILDABLE, & only trying reveals which (T408,V144,V505)
V616: **a WRAPPING parameter as a feedback TARGET flips the loop's SIGN @ the wrap ∴ negative feedback becomes POSITIVE.** measured on E14: error→palette-PHASE tap, phase −0.02 → settled meter 0.51→0.94 ∵ background WRAPS into ramp's white stops ∴ early builds saturated to a WHITE FRAME in 5 frames. loop was correctly signed EVERYWHERE except across the seam @ 0. ∴ ∀ driven param that WRAPS (phase, hue, angle, any `fract`) & sits ∈ a feedback path → its usable range ! be BOUNDED OFF the wrap (E14: bias +0.03, clamp floor 0.005) & bound ! be GATED, ⊥ a comment. corollary: a stability argument computed from LOCAL gain is silent about this — gain says ~0.7 & decays, wrap says diverges|V510

V622: **preview SLOT aspect FOLLOWS the project's configured resolution — OWNER'S CALL, made w/ costs on the table.** ⚠ REVERSES this row's first decision; measurement below stands, conclusion does ⊥. owner, after seeing the numbers: "make it the default then anyway… follow the configured resolution and thus aspect derived from that… it's fine if we need to manually update or resize them on change. that's what happens in TD too." ∴ manual re-author on aspect change is ACCEPTED COST, ⊥ a bug. **measured cost, unchanged & still true**: 24 of 27 examples are 16:9 & ⊥ move; 3 square projects re-author (E2 3 nodes, E12 1, E24 **28**); @ portrait 9:16 slot = 313px ∴ 25 of 27 violate, 203 overlapping pairs. **∴ §V621 still binds: aspect ! travel as an ARGUMENT from the document's OWN settings (`previewAspectOf`), ⊥ as a constant 2 files agree on** — that is what keeps a user doc's reflow derived ⊥ imposed|T663,T668,V389,V621,V437
V623: **a BLEND whose operand SATURATES deletes its other input — & the deletion is INVISIBLE ∵ downstream still receives a valid field.** E32: `dish1 = screen(coast1, shape1)` & `bowl1`'s background is WHITE ∴ `screen(1, anything) = 1`. measured on the outskirts: **median 0.9989, p90 = p99 = p999 = 0.9989** — chemistry map is ONE VALUE across the whole outskirts, & `terrain1`'s drift is erased THERE by a compositing choice, ⊥ by anything about Gray-Scott. ∴ the "static & homogenic outskirts" the owner saw was a prescribed disturbance ALREADY WIRED & THROWN AWAY. **∴ ∀ blend feeding a field a SIMULATION reads → check the operand's saturating value (`screen`→1, `multiply`→0, `min`/`max`→rails) ∨ a whole region silently loses its input; & gate a driving field by its SPREAD (p90≠p999), ⊥ by its presence**|V554,T657
V624: **⊥ ship a DEAD parameter — wire it ∨ remove it.** a param that drives ⊥ (a value chain w/ ⊥ consumer, a `speed` on a node w/ ⊥ time axis) is a LIE ∈ the document: a reader takes it as intent & an agent takes it as wiring. both E35 cases: `valuemath15`×9→`valuemath16`+1 drives NOTHING while Corona's IDENTICAL pair drives its 3rd renderPoints' `sizePixels`; `noise1` is perlin2d w/ `speed 0.12` & **a 2D noise has ⊥ time axis (T518)** ∴ speed is inert. ∴ decide on PIXELS: wire it & keep it if it earns its place, ELSE delete the param — shipping it dead teaches wrong EITHER way. corollary: an unfinished-intent pair is EVIDENCE (identical precedent ∈ a sibling example) ⊥ licence to invent|T518,B115,V471,T660
V625: **a SAW drives a WALKED angle; a ROTATION wants a SINE @ the same frequency.** a saw's wrap is CONTINUOUS once you take its cosine (an angle the herd walks) & DISCONTINUOUS as a rotation — it SNAPS BACK once a lap. ∴ same clock, same period, different reader ∴ ⊥ re-use the driver, re-shape it|T671,V481

E32: `displace` between `state1` & the reaction, w/ `pack1` repainting b from `dish1` AFTER the reaction ∴ the field moves & its parameters do ⊥. ⚠ COST, measured: advection eats COVERAGE — @ weight 0.006 dark fraction → 71% & the pasture visibly SHRANK ∵ flow moves V faster than a low-feed regime regrows it ∴ 0.0025 chosen against that; the weight is the density knob|T671,V623,V554 ⟶ **CONFIRMED IN THE WILD & EXTENDED (T734).** ⚠**E24 ALREADY HAD A NODE ∈ THIS SLOT DOING THE WRONG THING**: `wind1`, a `transform` w/ `r: 0.02` between `state` & `rd` — **a RIGID ROTATION applied 17–24× PER FRAME**, precisely what this row says turns a lattice & leaves it a lattice. swapping it for ADVECTION (`displace` from a slow 2-channel perlin, `mono` OFF) **beats the rotation on motion @ EVERY age & multiplies live spot count 2–4×** (f1800: motion .0462 → **.0624**, spots 238 → **907**). **& the COST curve TURNS OVER**: on E2 (substeps 20 ∴ E32's .0025/frame is **.000125** here) dark rises MONOTONICALLY as recorded, **but MOTION PEAKS ~.00025 & FALLS above ~.0005** — past that **the flow REMOVES THE MATERIAL THAT WAS DOING THE MOVING** ∴ the weight has a measurable OPTIMUM, ⊥ only a ceiling

V630: **ALPHA out of [0,1] @ a SINK is a CATALOGUE-WIDE fault class, & "feedback + additive points" is ⊥ the predicate.** measured across 25 shipped: **10** ship a sink whose alpha leaves [0,1]; E12-Fluid & E31-Corona are CLEAN despite having BOTH feedback & additive points ∴ lead's predicate was wrong. real predicate = **sink alpha leaves [0,1]**, & **goes NEGATIVE** for the flicker. mechanism ⊥ unbounded accumulation but a NEGATIVE-GAIN OSCILLATOR: additive passes floor alpha ≈6.02, Screen's alpha map `L ↦ A+L−A·L` has slope `1−A` = −5.02, feedback 0.62 closes it @ gain **−3.11** (measured −3.13) ∴ `M_{n+1} = 6.02 − 3.112·M_n` reproduces every frame. V667: **a CROSS-CUTTING TYPE change (a new port kind, a new enum member) reddens EVERY consumer until ALL are updated ∴ ∈ a SHARED tree it ! be done in ONE push, ⊥ incrementally.** T704's `projector` port kind mid-thread left **9 typecheck errors** across `ports.ts`, `port-compat.ts`, `reference-lines.tsx`, `search.ts`, `ui/ports.ts` & a test ∴ **⊥ other worker could claim a green typecheck**, & 3 stopped to prove the errors were ⊥ theirs. an exhaustive `switch` ∨ `satisfies Record<Kind,…>` is a FEATURE (§T675 made a new payload kind a typecheck failure ON PURPOSE) — & the SAME property makes the intermediate state EXPENSIVE for everyone else. ∴ thread it in one sitting, ∨ work it ∈ a worktree & land it whole|V479,B123,T675,T704

V670: **RELEASING a windowed file means COMMITTING your change — ⊥ merely CEASING TO EDIT.** T710 handed back `documents.ts` w/ its 465-line E13 hunk & its `look-baselines.json` row still UNCOMMITTED while it moved on to the md & tests ∴ the next holder (T711) could ⊥ `git commit -- <paths>` w/o **landing another worker's in-flight rebuild on their behalf** — §B133's exact hazard, & the §V494 pathspec rule forbids the index-staging workaround. ∴ a window CLOSES w/ a commit; if follow-up files remain, commit the WINDOWED file & continue outside it. corollary: a worker holding uncommitted edits ∈ a CONTESTED file blocks EVERY successor, ⊥ just the file|V494,B133,V643,T710,T711
V671: **a NEGATIVE result requires a PASSING CONTROL — a broken instrument reporting "absent" is INDISTINGUISHABLE from a real absence.** T715's 1st WebNN probe returned `navigator.gpu: undefined` from Playwright's Chromium ∈ ALL 3 configs INCLUDING headed w/ `--enable-unsafe-webgpu` — & **we KNOW WebGPU works ∵ the app runs on it** ∴ the CONTROL FAILED ∴ the negative was ⊥ evidence & the agent nearly reported it. re-run ∈ real Chrome 151 w/ the control PASSING (`navigator.gpu` object, adapter vendor `apple`, architecture `metal-3`): **`navigator.ml` = `undefined`** ∴ **WebNN is ⊥ PRESENT on the owner's machine — ⊥ flag-off-but-detectable, the ENTRY POINT does ⊥ EXIST.** ∴ ∀ "X is unavailable" claim ! carry a sibling "Y IS available" measured the SAME WAY|V461,V650,T715,T381
V672: **a capability label ! be LICENSED BY USE, ⊥ by SELECTION — & PAIRING the name w/ a MEASURED NUMBER makes it unable to lie about SPEED even where it cannot see the DEVICE.** @ detection time a path is CHOSEN but ⊥ TAKEN ∴ a bare "WebGPU" claims a path ⊥ yet exercised & "WebGPU · — ms" is a label w/ its evidence MISSING. ∴ the backend label appears ONLY after a completed inference; before that the node reports its STATE ("Acquiring model — 142 MB of 380 MB" | "Waiting for first result" | "Model unavailable — showing a flat depth map"). **self-correcting property**: ask transformers.js for `webnn-npu`, let it silently fall back INSIDE WebNN, & the label "WebNN" stays TRUE (we DID take that path) while **the LATENCY exposes the fallback**|V469,T715,T381
V673: **`memo` does ⊥ protect against CONTEXT — a context value re-renders EVERY consumer straight THROUGH `memo`.** T714: `NodeView` was memoized, its payload deliberately `{nodeId}`, & its projection reference-stable — all correct, all useless, ∵ it ALSO called `useGraphCanvas()`. ∴ **a memoized component's real dependency set is its props PLUS every context it reads**, & a context value rebuilt per revision defeats the whole memo strategy silently — the code looks right & the property is untrue (§V480's shape, one level up). ∴ ∀ context value shared by many consumers ! be reference-stable per member: read mutable state through a REF, & keep a derived collection's object when its MEMBERSHIP does ⊥ move|V480,T519,T714
V674: **a COUNTING gate ! subscribe to EXACTLY what the real component subscribes to.** T714's wrapper is `memo`'d **AND** calls `useGraphCanvas()` ∴ it re-renders under the 2 conditions `NodeView` does — **a wrapper that skipped the context would go QUIET during the very failure it exists to catch**. & it counts the thing that SCALES: renders on a 6-node vs a 60-node graph, asserting the DIFFERENCE does ⊥ grow (red-first **305 vs 35** = N+1 per edit, visible ∈ the numbers; after **0 and 0**), ⊥ a wall-clock threshold generous enough to survive noise & therefore generous enough to survive the regression returning|V666,V669,V649,T714
V675: **a feedback loop closing on the FINISHED FRAME smears EVERYTHING the frame contains ∴ a SELECTIVE trail closes on a SIDE BRANCH composited back.** E34 is the catalogue's 1st SELECTIVE loop (a luminance THRESHOLD decides what ENTERS it) & the 1st that does ⊥ close the way §V471.5 describes: it closes on `smear1`, a side branch added into the bloom's composite, ∵ closing on the output would trail the terrain, the chrome & the beams alike. ∴ **§V471.5 describes the DEFAULT, ⊥ the only shape** — & the roster ∈ `temporal.test.ts` is an EXPLICIT list, so adding a loop REDDENS it BY DESIGN (the gate working, ⊥ a sweep)|V471,T711,V631
V676: **an EXEMPTION silences a gate ∴ use one only when the GATE is wrong, NEVER when the PROSE is.** T716's md named `materialUnlit` ∈ a table describing a MUTATION, & E33's graph genuinely lacks the type ∴ a `DELIBERATE` entry would be **a gate declining to check a TRUE claim** — the prose gets rephrased instead. corollary from the same pass: when a rebuilt example inherits a measured table from the OLD form, **KEEP it w/ its ORIGINAL commit stamp & say WHAT it was measured on** — re-deriving produces a 3rd set of numbers for ONE invariant & makes the record worse, ⊥ better (§V641's stamp is what makes that legible)|V641,V643,T716,V640
V677: **⊥ MUTATE A SHARED SOURCE FILE TO TEST — mutate the GENERATED ARTIFACT the gate actually READS, & RESTORE BY REGENERATING.** T711's 1st mutation attempt was a `perl -i` on `documents.ts` **while 2 other workers had live hunks in it**, & it was a NO-OP BY LUCK: a shell expansion ate `${LIDAR_RANGE}` from BOTH pattern & replacement ∴ it substituted a string matching nothing. had it matched, it would have written into a contended file. **∴ the safe form is also the BETTER INSTRUMENT**: these gates read the `examples/` DIRECTORY via `listExamples()`, ⊥ the source ∴ mutating the SHIPPED `.loom.json` hits EXACTLY the surface the gates see & never touches a contended file. **restore is the GENERATOR, never a checkout** (§GOD-RULE). verify the tree clean after each pass|V666,V494,B133,T711 ⟶ **STRONGER FORM, used by T721: an ISOLATED `git worktree` — files copied in, `node_modules` symlinked, mutated THERE, worktree removed.** it needs ⊥ discipline about who else is typing & **the shared tree is never WRITTEN AT ALL** ∴ prefer it for SOURCE-level mutation; mutate-the-generated-artifact stays right for gates that read `examples/`
V678: **§V653 DEMONSTRATED, ⊥ argued: `liveness.test.ts` stayed GREEN under ALL TEN deliberate breakages** — including every ray drawn to full range, & 240 bounce legs (the green-spaghetti frame). @ 192×108 w/ a 10% band a look baseline **does ⊥ see structural damage this large** ∴ **a green baseline row means "about the same picture", ⊥ "this example is intact" — it is ⊥ a STRUCTURE gate & ⊥ cite it as one.** the claims are what catch structure; the baseline catches DRIFT|V653,V643,V666,T711
V681: **⊥ STILL-FRAME instrument can see MOTION damage — & most of ours are still-frame.** T716's most informative mutation (`z = 1 − 2u` → an INDEPENDENT sphere direction) **renders a PIXEL-IDENTICAL still frame** & re-deals EVERY tile in motion; ONLY the claim that names the correspondence sees it — ⊥ the rendered legibility gate, ⊥ the baseline, nothing else. same class as §V678's ten breakages surviving `liveness`. ∴ a property about CORRESPONDENCE ACROSS FRAMES (a tile keeping its identity, a marker holding its place, a beam matching its mark) ! be asserted STRUCTURALLY ∨ across FRAME PAIRS — a single rendered frame is evidence about a MOMENT, ⊥ about a MOTION|V678,V653,V666,T716,T711
V682: **a MULTI-RED can PROVE SHARING — if a mutation to a SHARED resolver reddens only ONE consumer, the consumers are ⊥ actually sharing.** T721's N5 mutated `resolveScalarMap` & reddened `points.test.ts`'s renderPoints `sizePixels` claim, `scene-pipeline.test.ts`'s geometry-map refusal, AND the new gate — **3 tests across 2 nodes** ∴ the resolver PROVED it is shared. had it reddened only the new gate, the 2 nodes would ⊥ actually answer "what may drive a size" the same way & **§V109 would be a COMMENT rather than a FACT**. ∴ §V666's "reddens it alone" is the rule for an ISOLATED claim; for a SHARED mechanism the multi-red IS the evidence — & either way the author ! be able to NAME which it is|V666,V109,T721
V683: **a UNIT TEST PINS THE CONVENTION ITS AUTHOR CHOSE ∴ it CANNOT DETECT THAT THE CONVENTION IS WRONG — only DOMAIN TRUTH can, & here only LOOKING did.** T704: the projector's LENS-SHIFT SIGN was INVERTED — positive `shiftY` slid the image **DOWN**. **EVERY unit test PASSED**, ∵ they pinned the author's chosen sign; Dawn gates were blind ∵ they use shift 0. the FIRST RENDERED E36 FRAME put the beams BELOW the cornice they were aimed past. ∴ for any parameter w/ an OUTSIDE convention (a projectionist's up/right, a photographer's f-stop, a musician's bar) the gate ! assert against **the DOMAIN's direction, named**, ⊥ against the implementation's own choice — & §V383 stands: LOOK at the first frame|V383,V681,V666,T704
V684: **the `text` node CANNOT appear ∈ a BASELINED example until the harness has a FONT story.** §V403: `registerSyntheticMediaSources` deliberately does ⊥ fake `text` — "black is the honest output of a machine w/ ⊥ font stack" — ∴ a text-bearing document renders **BLACK ∈ every offline gate** & its §V643 baseline would enshrine that black. ∴ E38 uses an ANALYTIC emblem (ramp/circle/noise composite), ⊥ `text`. **& this EXPLAINS §T728's list**: `text` is unused by any example ⊥ from neglect but ∵ it is UNGATEABLE — a node's absence from the catalogue can be a CONSEQUENCE, ⊥ an oversight, & is worth checking before treating coverage as a to-do|V403,T728,V643
V685: **a BACKTICK ∈ a WGSL COMMENT TERMINATES the TypeScript template literal — & it has bitten TWICE TODAY, 2 different workers.** T676's `RELIEF_LIFT_KERNEL` & T724's E33 kernels: writing `` `like this` `` in prose silently turns a kernel into a SYNTAX ERROR, & the error is `ERR_INVALID_TYPESCRIPT_SYNTAX` **pointing at a line of PROSE** ∴ it reads as unrelated. **EVERY WGSL constant ∈ `documents.ts` is exposed & NOTHING catches it before the regenerator runs** — & the tree is UNIMPORTABLE meanwhile, which the owner sees ∵ their dev server runs on this checkout. ∴ GATE IT (T729)|T676,T724,V670
V686: **a RECOVER-FROM-HISTORY splice needs an ANCHORED search & an assertion on the SPAN LENGTH.** T724's 1st apply script used a bare `pre.index('node(\n  "body",')` which matched a DIFFERENT example thousands of lines earlier & spliced a huge span into E33. it failed LOUDLY on a duplicate `const` ∴ caught ∈ seconds — but the ⊥-loud version of that mistake lands silently ∈ a 900-line file ⊥ one reviews line by line. ∴ anchor on something UNIQUE & assert the extracted span's LENGTH before writing|V494,V677,T724
V687: **an example whose SUBJECT IS CHANGE has ⊥ NULL STATE THAT LOOKS LIKE ANYTHING — if its performer does ⊥ move, it opens BLACK & reads as BROKEN.** a frame-difference probe rendered PURE BLACK ∵ `noise` has ⊥ intrinsic time axis (T518/§V624) & a static `t.z` differenced against a 6-frame-old copy is IDENTICALLY ZERO. ∴ for a motion example the UNDERSTUDY'S OWN MOTION is LOAD-BEARING, ⊥ decoration — & it is §V681's shape exactly: the claim is about CORRESPONDENCE ACROSS FRAMES ∴ assert across a frame PAIR, never from a still|V681,T518,V624,V411
V688: **polar/log-polar warp is EXPRESSIBLE TODAY ∈ 6 nodes — the lead's "most versatile missing primitive" hypothesis is REFUTED, by render.** `ramp(circular)` → `transform(s.x = 1/aspect, aspectcorrect off)` = θ aspect-corrected (`ramp(circular)` computes `atan2` ∈ **uv** space ∴ rays are ELLIPTICALLY spaced on 16:9 & the fix is exactly `atan2(dv, du·aspect)`); `circle(distance)` → `level(black=−k, white=0)` = ρ UNCLAMPED; `reorder` → `remap(extend:"repeat")`. ⚠**do ⊥ use `ramp(radial)` for ρ** — it is `clamp(length(uv−0.5)·2,0,1)` ∴ all 4 CORNERS (~20% of a 16:9 frame) pin to ONE FLAT VALUE, rendered & visibly dead. & RGB split (2 `transform` + 2 `reorder`), frame-difference (`cache`+`difference`+`level`), halftone, mosaic, luma key are ALL expressible. **feedback-with-transform ships TWICE already** (E1 fade+transform; E29 scale ABOVE ONE) ∴ a polar example ! ⊥ be a tunnel ∨ it collides w/ E29|T728,V624
V689: **a THRESHOLD chosen NEAR THE THING YOU ARE MEASURING turns ONE property into TWO — & can report the direction BACKWARDS.** T713's 1st sign test counted echo pixels above a BRIGHT threshold & said mid-focus had MORE area than either extreme — **exactly what an INVERTED SIGN looks like** — but a defocused mark is BIGGER **AND** DIMMER ∴ a bright gate measures the two TOGETHER & the area claim was contaminated by the brightness one. w/ a gate just clear of the BACKGROUND (area is the claim ∴ it ! ⊥ sit near the mark's own PEAK) the domain assertion PASSES: focus-near 17,102 px & focus-far 17,102 px, both above 14,591 for focus INSIDE the population ∴ **BOTH SIDES GROW, which is the property**. sibling of §V649 (percentage w/o population): **place the gate away from the QUANTITY YOU ARE ⊥ CLAIMING**|V649,V683,V666,T713
V690: **ADDING AN EXAMPLE TOUCHES 6 FILES + 2 CONDITIONAL — measured from `66653f7`, ⊥ recalled.** `src/examples/documents.ts` · generated `examples/E<N>-<Name>.loom.json` · hand-written `examples/E<N>-<Name>.md` · 1 row ∈ `examples/README.md` · 1 row ∈ `src/examples/look-baselines.json` (§V643, DELIBERATE) · 1 entry ∈ the HARD-CODED list ∈ `src/examples/runner.test.ts`. CONDITIONAL: `src/examples/temporal.test.ts` IF the graph closes a Feedback loop (its roster is explicit ∴ it reddens BY DESIGN), & a dedicated `*.gpu.test.ts` for a pixel claim. **BOTH REGISTRIES ARE DISCOVERY-DRIVEN & DELIBERATELY NEED ⊥ EDIT** — `catalogue.ts` `readdirSync`, `example-catalogue.ts` `import.meta.glob`. regenerators (neither wrapped ∈ a package script): `node --import ./src/tooling/alias-hooks.ts src/examples/build-examples.ts --only <N>` & the same for `measure-look-baselines.ts`|V643,T698,T730,V670
V691: **a CACHE keyed on a value that is CONSTANT ACROSS THE POPULATION is STRUCTURALLY BLIND.** `compileNow`'s plan cache compares by `graph.revision` ALONE & **all 29 shipped examples ship `revision: 1`** ∴ the comparison can NEVER distinguish any pair of them. it is masked today by render-before-effect ordering & the bus swap — masking, ⊥ correctness. ∴ before trusting a cache key, MEASURE ITS DISTRIBUTION over the real population; a key w/ ⊥ variance is ⊥ a key|B140,V649,T726
V692: **a REF read INSIDE a `.then` AFTER an `await` is ⊥ ∈ lockstep w/ the value it mirrors, whatever the comment says.** `use-frame-loop.ts:554` reads `documentBoundaryRef` after `await backend.compile`; its comment claims it "changes in lockstep w/ `compiled`" & it does ⊥ — any re-render producing `documentBoundary:false` WHILE the boundary compile is ∈ FLIGHT (the preview-sink store publishes on the graph pane's rAF tick, well inside a real compile) LOSES `resetTemporalHistory` + `seek(0)` for that load. **INTERMITTENT BY CONSTRUCTION ∴ the best remaining candidate for a genuine PIXEL leak, & ⊥ current gate can see it**|B141,V480,T726
V693: **an AUTO-RANGING plot whose WINDOW IS SHORTER THAN THE SIGNAL'S PERIOD rescales CONSTANTLY — & it is a CLIFF, ⊥ a slope.** measured, synthetic sine, frequency swept: window/period 0.022–0.30 → **~200 refits/min**; 0.50 → 142; **1.00 & above → ZERO**. ∴ the moment ONE PERIOD FITS ∈ the window the refits stop entirely. §T352's docblock states its own assumption in prose — *"a sliding window over a periodic signal varies by a fraction of a percent, so half is far outside the noise"* — **TRUE ONLY WHEN A PERIOD FITS ∈ THE WINDOW**, & nothing enforced that (§V478's shape). ∴ either the window CONTAINS a period, ∨ the range is HELD|V478,T352,T459,T735
V694: **a positive `blacklevel` IS A SUBTRACTION, `rgba16float` does ⊥ CLAMP, & `Level` is ROUTINELY REACHED FOR AS A THRESHOLD.** ⚠**WIDENED — the feedback loop was ⊥ the point, it only COMPOUNDS it every frame.** measured OUTSIDE a loop: `haze1` w/ `blacklevel 0.68` as a bloom threshold — "keep only the highlights" — sends every pixel below 0.68, which is NEARLY ALL OF THEM, negative as far as **−2.1** ∴ **the bloom SUBTRACTED everywhere it was ⊥ blooming**; fixing it took the frame's range **0.1147 → 0.9703**. E1's docstring ("crushes the dimmest survivors to zero") is TRUE ∈ unorm & FALSE ∈ the format we ship (§V478). ∴ **the NON-NEGATIVE way to threshold a bloom is `gamma1` BELOW 1** — `signedPow(c, 1/gamma)` crushes midtones & keeps highlights **w/o ever crossing zero**. ⚠ **the catalogue is ACCIDENTALLY SAFE & nobody wrote down why**: every shipped bloom uses blacklevel 0 ∨ 0.01, & E34's `poolbase` uses **−0.1 DELIBERATELY to LIFT** (§V644)|V478,V644,V698,V699
V695: **RAMP STOPS ARE DISPLAY SPACE & DECODE TO LINEAR ∴ a palette that looks BALANCED as authored numbers plays back WARM-OVER-BLACK.** measured: a dark cool stop `[0.05,0.36,0.55]` lands @ linear `[0.004,0.106,0.267]` & reads as BLACK — the decode costs a dark cool colour most of its LUMINANCE while barely touching a bright warm one. ∴ balance a palette by its LINEAR luminance, ⊥ by how its stops look ∈ the picker; the cool half ! be LIFTED until it carries comparable LIGHT. sibling of §V618 (the same encode, one layer up)|V618,V471,T-VJ
V696: **RANGE-CHECKING a gain/bias pair against its target means MEASURING the target, ⊥ ESTIMATING it — & the error is an ORDER OF MAGNITUDE, twice.** a `whitelevel 0.3` & later `0.045` were written against a frame-difference field whose measured max is **0.058**; the second mapped the field's MEDIAN to 0.86 & blew the frame WHITE. ∴ instrument the source's PERCENTILES before fitting anything to it — §V471's amended rule is only as good as the number you fit against|V471,V545,T-VJ
V697: **a PORTALED surface falls back to the GLOBAL keymap context ∴ DESTRUCTIVE GLOBAL bindings fire from INSIDE it — & a `<button>` is the ONE target shape the text-context rule CANNOT SEE.** T732 documented its strip's `stopPropagation` as stopping `tab` re-opening the browser on itself; **the mutation written to PROVE that DECLINED TO FAIL.** measured instead: the popover is PORTALED ∴ the keymap falls back to `environment.context`, which `app.tsx` sets to **`"global"`, ⊥ `"graph"`** — graph bindings cannot fire from in there AT ALL. **but GLOBAL ones can, & `mod+z` is `graph.undo`** ∴ the real hazard is **browsing categories w/ the keyboard SILENTLY UNDOING the user's last edit** — §V53's classic bug arriving through the one target the text-context rule misses. ∴ the gate is a NODE COUNT, ∵ the damage is to the DOCUMENT|V53,V78,V666,T732
V698: **an OPERATION'S ALGEBRAIC PROPERTY is a DETECTOR — use it before hunting.** T-VJ chased a contrast-floor failure through 3 wrong guesses (probe averaging, blur size, source distribution), each making it WORSE, then instrumented the per-stage histogram: `paint1` range **0.5454** → `burn1` range **0.1147**. **`burn1` is an ADD, & an ADD CANNOT REDUCE RANGE** ∴ one input was NEGATIVE — & that single fact named the fault immediately. ∴ when a pipeline's output violates a property its OPERATOR GUARANTEES, the violation LOCATES the fault; instrument per STAGE & compare against what each stage is ALLOWED to do|V666,V694,V649
V699: **`blur.size` is ∈ PIXELS while the liveness/contrast floor is measured @ 192×108 ∴ a halo that is a 2.7% glow @ 1280 is an 18%-OF-WIDTH WASH @ probe size.** §V627's resolution trap arriving through the BLOOM rather than through point density. ∴ ∀ pixel-denominated parameter ! be read against the resolution the GATE measures at, ⊥ only the one the owner SEES|V627,V643,V694
V700: **a UNIT gate proves a builder EXISTS; a BROWSER gate proves it carries the RIGHT INPUT; NEITHER ALONE IS SUFFICIENT.** T720's 3rd mutation is the finding — a builder of the **WRONG SHAPE** (`clickedNodeIds` sending `nodeIds` where the command reads `nodeId`) leaves the seam gate **GREEN** & the e2e **RED**, while removing the builder entirely reddens BOTH. ∴ presence & correctness are DIFFERENT CLAIMS needing DIFFERENT INSTRUMENTS — §V656's shape (right count, wrong order) one level up. & the near-miss worth keeping: the 1st e2e draft called `fitAll` before the right-click, `fitAll` → `focusGraph` CLICKS THE PANE & CLEARS THE SELECTION ∴ the test degenerated into the other case & **would have passed for the wrong reason** — caught by running it RED & reading WHY it was red, ⊥ by it going green|V656,V666,V634,T720
V701: **a gate that resolves its async on a MICROTASK never opens the window a REAL `await` opens ∴ it cannot see a race that lives ∈ that window.** §T519's `document-boundary.test.tsx` stayed **GREEN under all 3 of B141's mutations** ∵ it resolves `compile` on a microtask — **that is WHY B141 outlived the fix that was supposed to cover it**. ∴ a gate for a race ! OWN the window: defer the async explicitly & **assert 2 operations were genuinely OUTSTANDING TOGETHER** before claiming anything. & the jsdom limit was ⊥ fatal: the production TRIGGER needs rAF, the PROPERTY does ⊥ — drive the second compile by another real path & say so|V666,V681,T519,T733
V702: **LATCH OWED WORK @ SCHEDULE TIME, ⊥ @ RESOLVE TIME — a REF IS ⊥ A SNAPSHOT.** B141 read `documentBoundaryRef` inside a `.then` & got whatever the NEWEST render said; the mutation proving the placement matters: latching @ RESOLVE time instead of SCHEDULE time **still reddens the claim** ∴ the latch alone is ⊥ the fix, its PLACEMENT is. general: when an async result must act on the state that CAUSED it, capture that state where the work is SCHEDULED & treat it as a DEBT to discharge, ⊥ a flag to re-read|V692,V480,B141,T733
V703: **an invariant a READER ! REMEMBER is weaker than one a GATE CAN SEE — turn it into a gate wherever the shape allows.** E40 asserts STRUCTURALLY that **⊥ node on its feedback path carries a positive `blacklevel`** ∴ §V694 stops being prose someone has to recall & becomes a red test. cf §T675 (a new payload kind is a TYPECHECK failure until it declares an orbit) & §T721's `satisfies` table. ∴ when filing a §V, ask what SHAPE would make it enforceable, & say so ∈ the row|V694,V478,T675,T721
V704: **a property that is a CONJUNCTION cannot be SNIFFED FROM A SIGNATURE — DECLARE it.** `plotPeriodFollowsInputs` is "clockless **AND** stateless **AND** repeats-with-input", & ⊥ predicate over a `valueEvaluate` signature reveals that: `valueStep` reads `frame`, `channelIn` reads an AMBIENT BAG, `valueSwitch` may select a DIFFERENT INPUT moment to moment — **all 3 take a value input & NONE propagates a period**. ∴ declare it per node, & make ABSENT the safe default. general: when a capability is the conjunction of things that ⊥ appear ∈ the type, inference will be CONFIDENTLY WRONG on the counterexamples|V478,V109,T735
V705: **assert EXHAUSTIVENESS over the WHOLE UNION, ⊥ over the members CURRENTLY IN USE — a registry walk is BLIND to declared-but-unused kinds.** T712's table is `satisfies Record<PortKind, NodeFamily>` & its test asserts over the FULL union ∴ the 7 declared-but-unused kinds are covered & **the first `buffer`-output node would have arrived TINTED**; a walk over the 8 kinds in use would have said NOTHING about them. verified by DELETING a member & watching `tsc` NAME it. cf §T675 (a new payload kind is a typecheck failure until it declares an orbit) & §T721|V487,T675,T721,T712
V706: **when a published SHAPE does ⊥ fit your abstraction, GENERALISE YOUR OWN — ⊥ reshape shapes you do ⊥ own.** T719 wave 1: `FullscreenHolder` carries **2 slots** (T551 added `app` beside `current`) & `state-queries` holds `{ sources }`, never null, backing several QUERIES ⊥ one command. rather than reshape 2 published shapes w/ foreign call sites, the primitive became **`sharedForBus(bus, key, create)` — keyed on IDENTITY, ⊥ field layout** — w/ `commandHolder` a thin wrapper & **⊥ consumer's shape changed**. ⚠**the TELL that it is the right seam: wave 2's STORES want EXACTLY the same primitive** ∴ wave 2 is a CONTINUATION ⊥ a 2nd mechanism|V487,V109,T719
V707: **a mutation that catches NOTHING reveals a HOLE, ⊥ a safe area.** T719's completeness check ran ONE direction (a module still on the old holder). asking *"what would M4 catch?"* & finding it caught **nothing** exposed the other direction — **a module CONVERTED but MISSING FROM THE TABLE looks perfectly fine to the 1st check**. ∴ a completeness claim needs BOTH directions, & the way to find the missing one is to ask what each mutation would catch & disbelieve any that catches nothing. & 2 more from the same gate: **assert the PRECONDITION that the 2 module instances really are DISTINCT** (∨ a change ∈ module caching silently makes it one instance compared against ITSELF — green forever & blind), & **compare the OBJECTS, ⊥ the key STRINGS** (strings only prove someone TYPED 17 different things)|V666,V656,V700,T719 ⟶ **3rd instance (T727): its 1st E38 mutation was a NO-OP** — ∈ a §T401 PROCESSOR kernel `p.position` **IS** the upstream's position ∴ `fieldAt(p.position)` cannot express "sample where the mote is" & the mutation COULD ⊥ REDDEN. **that ⊥-reddening is the ONLY reason it discovered the gate it had just written was WORTHLESS**; the real mutation needed `p.position + p.drift` ⟶ **4th & 5th instances, T719 wave 2, BOTH on its own gate**: the no-op-unsubscribe mutation initially PASSED ∵ the probe called `begin(PROBE_NODE)` TWICE & the 2nd is an IDEMPOTENT no-op ∴ the assertion held whether ∨ ⊥ unsubscribe worked — `mutate` now ! produce genuinely DIFFERENT state; & a bad probe patched `{exposure: 2}` where the field is `exposureStops` ∴ the "mutation" mutated NOTHING & the store CORRECTLY declined to notify. **the gate caught its own probe, ⊥ review**
V708: **a GUARD'S SCOPE decides WHICH INSTANCES IT CAN SEE — & a scope chosen from the MECHANISM YOU ARE REASONING ABOUT can exclude the instance that MATTERS.** E40's §V694 guard, 1st draft, scoped to the ACCUMULATOR'S FEED PATH: it **reddened on `gain1` — HARMLESS, contained by Lookup's clamp-by-indexing — & stayed GREEN on `under1`, the HARMFUL one**, which fed `lay1` directly & would have thinned the wake over ANY footage w/ real blacks. **it caught the benign instance & missed the real one, & looked correct doing it.** restated over the WHOLE GRAPH it catches all 3 positive cases & still PERMITS a negative black level (a LIFT, legitimate — §V644) — & **that permissive case is exercised AS A MUTATION rather than assumed**, ∵ a guard scoped to make the current file pass is ⊥ a guard|V694,V666,V461,V703
V709: **2 changes that ARRIVE TOGETHER ! EACH be measured against THE OTHER ALONE — beating the BASELINE JOINTLY establishes NEITHER.** T734: the predecessor's weather+advection candidate beat SHIPPED E2 comfortably & that was TRUE; **what was never run is WEATHER vs ADVECTION-ALONE, ∵ advection-alone was ⊥ on its table** — the 2 arrived together. run properly, flattening the front **RAISES tile CV @ 7 of 8 ages** (lap mean 0.353 vs 0.277, **+28%**) & raises dark fraction @ ALL 8; motion is a wash (0.213 vs 0.226) ∴ **the front buys 6% of motion & costs 22% of composition**; & the slow swing it was ADDED FOR is IDENTICAL either way (dark 20.8 pts vs 21.1) ∵ **the advection ALONE already produces a swing of that size**. ∴ a joint candidate hides which half is carrying it, & the §V666 mutation on the wrong half **reddens NEITHER instrument** — which is §V707's tell|V666,V707,V626,T734
V710: **a MULTIPLY-based "weather" walks the chemistry DOWN, & down is the DENSEST regime — it moves a region TOWARD the owner's complaint, ⊥ away.** §V554's CORRECTED band: 0.00–0.30 is **DENSE LABYRINTH**. ∴ a front that multiplies does ⊥ walk a region OUT of the lattice into interesting territory — it walks it into **the most screen-filling regime there is**. measured on BOTH documents independently: E24 advect-only in-disc CV 0.430/0.237/0.307 vs advect+weather 0.300/0.232/0.249, w/ spot count **462/907/470 → 1120/2472/1631 — 3× the spots, finer, flatter, more even**. ∴ if weather is ever wanted here it ! push the coordinate **UP** toward the sparse/dying end, ⊥ down — & §V554 says >0.90 is DEAD, so the usable window is NARROW|V554,V626,V623,T734
V711: **`target` is a WGSL RESERVED KEYWORD — Dawn refuses the WHOLE MODULE, by name.** ⊥ recorded anywhere before T727 hit it, & cheap to trip ∵ it is the obvious identifier for exactly the thing a point kernel computes|V685,T727
V712: **§V678 DEMONSTRATED AGAIN & HARDER: giving EVERY ribbon THE WRONG OWNER moves the look instrument's range 0.4129 → 0.4125** — straight through the 10% band. & on E38: **6,528 members become 8,302, 3,573 slots CHANGE SIDES, & the look range reads 0.8953 for BOTH to FOUR DECIMALS.** ∴ **a look baseline cannot see a TOTAL RE-ASSIGNMENT of which element is which.** the CLAIMS caught both; the baseline caught NEITHER ∴ ⊥ cite a green look row as evidence about STRUCTURE ∨ CORRESPONDENCE|V678,V681,V643,T727
V713: **RUNNING e2e AGAINST THE SHARED DEV SERVER IS NON-DETERMINISTIC while other workers edit the tree** — 4 failures then 1 on CONSECUTIVE IDENTICAL runs. ∴ the standard for e2e ∈ this tree is **`git archive HEAD` into a temp dir + an ISOLATED server + your own files on top**, ⊥ only for attribution but for EVERY run. (& it is how 3 workers have now proven "⊥ mine" by measurement rather than adjacency)|V620,V646,T719
V714: ⚠**`git commit --amend` ALWAYS REWRITES **HEAD**, whatever pathspec you give it — & ∈ a shared tree HEAD MAY ⊥ BE YOURS.** ⚠**LEAD ERRATUM on this row's 1st draft**: I wrote that amend "reads the shared index" & produced a SECOND commit. **FALSE.** verified: `b018aa7^ = 1c8cbd4^ = 9ec501a`, `tree(1c8cbd4) = tree(b018aa7)`, `git diff` EMPTY ∴ **`b018aa7` IS `1c8cbd4` w/ its MESSAGE REPLACED** — ⊥ a 2nd commit, & `1c8cbd4` is **ORPHANED**, reachable only via reflog. **a pathspec selects CONTENT, NEVER WHICH COMMIT ∴ it cannot protect you.** ⚠**& the DAMAGE is ⊥ attribution — it is the REASONING RECORD**: ∈ this project the commit MESSAGE is where the reasoning lives, & the rewrite erased a 4-mutation §V666 table (incl the *same object, lost subscribers* row that is the ENTIRE argument for the 2nd gate), a self-correction, & 2 §V707 self-catches. **& it is the WORST of the 9 sweep routes ∵ it FAILED SILENTLY**: the amend SUCCEEDED & produced a well-formed commit carrying the amender's message — the other 8 left evidence AT THE POINT OF THE MISTAKE. ∴ **⊥ `--amend` ∈ this tree, ever** — & preserve an orphan w/ a LIGHTWEIGHT TAG (`gc.reflogExpireUnreachable` = **30 days**), which is additive & reversible|V494,B145,V670
V715: **work that ! happen AFTER an await is LATCHED AS A DEBT (§V702); work that ! happen BEFORE it is MOVED EARLIER — ⊥ latched.** §B143's fix is §V702's COMPLEMENT & the distinction is the point: B141's boundary work ran after `await backend.compile` ∴ a ref could move under it ∴ it had to be OWED. B143's had to be gone BEFORE the compile installs ∴ the answer is a DOOR THAT OPENS EARLY ENOUGH — a commit-time effect — & **⊥ supersession risk exists ∵ nothing is deferred: a React effect cannot be outrun by a promise scheduled ∈ the SAME COMMIT**. ⊥ new mechanism was added beside §V702's; the existing block MOVED|V702,V701,B143
V716: **a TOLERANCE on a QUANTISED measurement ! be expressed ∈ QUANTA — a precision-digit tolerance landing BETWEEN lattice points is MARGINAL BY CONSTRUCTION.** §B144: a value on a `k/255` lattice (1 count = 0.00392) against a prediction of **36.43 counts**, gated by `toBeCloseTo(…,2)` = ±0.005 = **1.28 counts** ∴ it admits exactly 2 lattice points & rejects their neighbours by 0.0006 → **~50% flake**. ∴ (a) compute the QUANTUM & size the window in it; (b) **widen by WINDOW, ⊥ by PRECISION DIGIT** — a digit is a 10× jump & the next one down (±0.05) would have stopped refuting the hypothesis the gate exists to test; (c) a flake that is marginal-by-construction reads as "statistical" & is ⊥ — **the tell is the failures landing on ADJACENT LATTICE POINTS rather than scattering**|V649,V666,B144
V717: **a BASELINE SAMPLED AT EARLY FRAMES CANNOT SEE A LATE-ONSET FAILURE — & §V643's rows are sampled @ f60–f180.** T734 measured it: **the look baseline's motion row moved 5% while the picture's LATE-AGE motion moved 10×**, ∵ the instrument looks BEFORE the collapse. & the collapse IS the owner's complaint — E2's composition dies @ **f600** & holds for the next fifty seconds. ∴ **a baseline row is evidence about the OPENING of a document, ⊥ about its BEHAVIOUR**; a fault that arrives after the sampling window is invisible to it BY CONSTRUCTION. 3rd distinct blindness recorded for the same instrument: §V678 (structural damage), §V712 (correspondence), & now ONSET|V678,V712,V643,T734
V718: **a MEAN OF CONSECUTIVE DIFFERENCES TELESCOPES TO THE ENDPOINTS — it CANNOT see whether the step is CONSTANT.** §B144's assertion: every gain step is 10 dB ∴ `slopes[i] = means[i−1] − means[i]` & their mean is EXACTLY `(first − last)/4` ∴ it depends **only on the 2 endpoints**, while the comment claimed it pinned *"a FIXED step per 10 dB"*. the per-step values genuinely VARY (0.1127–0.1654 on `low`, ~10 FFT bins @ 23.4 Hz) & that variation is PRINTED & never ASSERTED. ∴ **CONSTANCY needs its OWN assertion & cannot be smuggled into an average** — & a comment describing what a statistic MEANS ! be checked against what it COMPUTES|V666,V649,B144
V719: **a tolerance set INSIDE the statistic's own OBSERVED RANGE is the original error one size down.** §B144's 1st patch shipped ±0.01 & passed 32/32 — then a control run produced **0.13034, which is 0.0125 from the prediction & OUTSIDE that window**. widened to ±0.015 to cover the observed spread w/ margin, & **falsified in BOTH directions** (a predicted span of 60 ∨ 80 dB still reddens 4/4) ∴ the widening did ⊥ buy green by giving up discrimination. **the author reported nearly repeating the mistake rather than landing the number that passed its own runs**|V716,V666,B144
V720: **`vec3f` & `vec4f` cost THE SAME — 16 bytes each — ∵ WGSL ALIGNS A VEC3 TO 16.** ∴ ∀ "a 3-component form is cheaper" argument about an attribute is FALSE HERE, & a choice framed as a cost trade is really a CAPABILITY choice w/ ⊥ price attached. the lead framed §T723 as "quaternion vs direction is what decides it" & the measurement removed the decision's premise entirely|V588,T723
V721: **a READ path ! have ⊥ ROUTE TO THE NETWORK — make the expensive path UNREACHABLE BY CONSTRUCTION, ⊥ by discipline.** §T383: `refresh` reads the cache & CANNOT open a connection; `acquire` is the ONLY thing that can ∴ **placing a node cannot spend 94 MB** no matter what calls it. & 2 siblings from the same design: **a TRUNCATED download is a FAILURE, ⊥ a smaller model** (caching it poisons the machine & surfaces far away as a parse error naming nothing); & the network cost is paid on an EXPLICIT press, never on a placement|V585,T383
