T1581b|.|**INSTANCE AN ARBITRARY MESH AT POINTS (engine wish from §T1561b's capability survey, shaderloom-f1 2026-10-05; extends §T1361b).** today geometry mode "instances" / `renderInstances` draws quad, box or octahedron only (`render-instances.ts`, `scene.ts`), with one scalar scale, an orient quaternion and a tint; Material·WGSL is refused on instances (§T1361b) and instances write no normal/albedo/shadow output. wanted: a mesh wired as the instance shape, a per-instance transform (position, orientation, non-uniform scale), Material·WGSL and the G-buffer outputs. the workaround in use: duplicated parts in one GLB, each with a part index, placed per frame by a point kernel (the furnace rig-kernel idiom; sentinel-bot carries 540 ring copies that way). **WANTED BY THE OWNER (relayed by shaderloom-f1, 2026-10-05): "we should support mesh instancing though". IN BUILD. THE CONSUMER'S SHAPE (sentinel-bot):** (1) the instance SHAPE is a mesh pointset (a Mesh File In selection with its triangle topology), drawn once per point of the points input; quad, box and octahedron stay. (2) per instance: position (vec3f), orient (unit quaternion, as today's Map slot), scale as a scalar AND per-axis vec3f, tint (vec4f), one free vec4f passed to the material untouched. (3) Material·WGSL allowed on these draws, the mesh's own vertex attributes intact (normal turned by orient; uv, color, surface, emissive as the file has them), and SurfaceIn carries the instance's free vec4f and the vertex's OBJECT-LOCAL position, so procedural detail sticks to the part. (4) the same citizenship as surface geometry: depth, normal, albedo and shadow outputs; casts and receives shadows from directional and point lights. (5) counted pointsets draw only live instances; the Group predicate culls per instance. (6) size: 2,000–4,000 instances of one ~700-triangle mesh per draw, plus single large parts; one shape per geometry node is enough. **RESEARCH IN (`docs/td-notch-mechanisms-2026-10-05.md`, `fa759eab`):** TD maps each instance attribute from its own source and channel, writes the transform order as a formula, has pivot, rotate-to-vector plus up, an active channel, colour mode, texture index and four custom attributes read in a GLSL MAT; it has no quaternion or matrix instance input until 2026.20000 (keep Loom's quaternion, add rotate-to-vector as the convenience). Notch keeps per-clone state as flat GPU buffers and effectors are an ordered stack of per-clone kernels — Loom's pointset plus kernel chain is that model. take: a SHAPE INDEX per instance (variant pick and kill through one channel); lights as instance data (§T1589b); one sentence on Copy POP ("real copies when you must deform after") vs instancing. the object transform (§T1588b) is designed in the same doc. **BUILD ORDER RULED 2026-10-05 (owner: "order seems good"): §T1588b + §T1581b first, then §T1586b, then §T1587b and §T1589b, then §T1590b and §T1591b; each design-first with the TD/Notch comparison.** **DESIGN LANDED `3106f8f4` (`docs/mesh-instancing-design-2026-10-05.md`, with §T1588b; D1–D17, slices A–G, follow-ups F1–F17). RULED BY THE LEAD 2026-10-05, pending the consumer's review:** O1 Geometry · Instances · Shape: Mesh with a `mesh` input (no new Instancer node); O2 `Frame` on Mesh File In (World | Object | Part, default World, decided at decode); O3 a mesh instance's scale defaults to 1 — a dependent default through `parametersFor` if the inspector, presets and schema guardrails take it, else a distinct `instanceScale` (default 1) with the 0.05 size hidden for Mesh; never the 0.05 trap; O4 RESOLVE ONCE, DRAW MANY — a compute pass writes one record per instance (3×4 `Object · Instance` rows, tint, uv, the material's fields) that every pass reads; a culled instance is a zero matrix; O5 the Geometry owns that pass (fallback: the Render); O6 `model` always present on surface draws; O7 authored Orient stays refused (Rotate + Forward); O8 custom attributes are the material's `struct Instance`, bound by name; O9 `SurfaceIn` grows on every draw; O10 the shape index is a channel now, several shapes per node later; O11 names as proposed, the existing "Scale" label becomes "Size" (key unchanged); O12 Parent and Look At by name with a Null node; O13 the object transform on primitives/Points/Beam is slice G, refused by name until then; O14, O15 as recommended; O16 build order A (object transform) → B (instancing slice 1, a true prefix) → C … G. one chain: `world = Object · Instance_i · v`, both levels scale → turn → translate, TD's order. **CONSUMER REVIEW 2026-10-05 (shaderloom-f1): no objection; BUILD STARTED (slice A, then B, then the quat module).** folded in: Rotate stays AFTER Look At in the object's own frame, the turn convention stated once (right-handed, X toward Y about +Z) and pinned by a test; Group moves into slice B (four shapes on one pointset); the Frame: Part refusal names the parts; F9 (a `// @use quat` module for kernels) right after slice B; the consumer will instance the HULL too (one point per robot), so slice B is its critical path. measured-frame threshold from the consumer: about 3,150 instances / 2.3 M triangles per pass; over ~6 ms with one point-light shadow moves F1 up. follow-ups F1–F17 → §T1592b. **SLICES A + B AND THE QUAT MODULE LANDED `0fed14ef` (squash of 83261420, 2c9594dc, 77212df8, 0f3563b1) + `2126da9d` (E13 keeps its gutter: every Geometry is one port row taller).** as built: `meshFileIn (frame: object|part) → geometry.mesh` (new input "Shape Mesh", needs only `position`), any pointset → `geometry.points`, `geometry { mode: instances, shape: mesh }`; per instance `instanceTranslate` (a mapped vec3f replaces `position`; the constant still adds), `orient` (Map, unit quaternion x y z w), `scale` (label "Size", defaults to 1 on a mesh instance through `parametersFor`), `tint` (× the mesh's colour), `group` (a rejected instance is drawn in no pass); one resolve pass per Geometry (`<node>:instances:resolve`) writes a 3×4 record every draw in every Render reads; mesh instances take the surface branch (lit models, Material·WGSL, Normal/Albedo/Shadow layers, depth sweeps, shadows cast and received from directional and point lights); counted pointsets draw their live count; glass on mesh instances refuses by name; the primitives' three generators are byte-identical. Mesh File In `frame` = world | object | part with the measured `frameOrigin`; the Part refusal names the parts. `SurfaceIn` gains `local`, `localNormal`, `instanceId`. `// @use quat` (`quatAxisAngle`, `quatMul`, `quatRotate`, `quatFromFrame`, `quatLookAt`, `quatFromTo`, `quatSlerp`) — a Point Kernel did not resolve `// @use` at all before this (`kernelSharedModules`, refusals `node.points.module`). MEASURED (GPU timestamps, Dawn/Metal, 1920×1080 rgba16float, 4,000 × a 716-triangle ring, median of 40): colour 2.9 ms; colour + Depth + Normal + Albedo + one directional shadow 7.1 ms; colour + one point-light shadow 9.1 ms; the same with the G-buffer 12.5 ms — over the consumer's 6 ms line, so the shadow sweeps are the cost (§T1598b, then F1). RULED: the always-visible Shape Mesh socket stays for now (§T1599b makes a socket appear only when it applies); until slice G the Transform group is INACTIVE and ignored on primitives, points and beams, never a per-frame refusal; next slices in the consumer's order: E (custom attributes), D, C, F, G. narrow-run note: every surface shader's text now carries `model`/`modelNormal`; the full examples GPU suite passed after slice A, a sample of five + three example GPU files after slice B and the merge. **FIRST CONSUMER USE (`878bf2d6`), three measured costs that reorder the work:** (1) A REJECTED INSTANCE STILL COSTS THE WHOLE MESH — 631 instances of a 152,490-vertex hull with 630 rejected by Group: 400 ms a frame (5 ms with a pointset per piece); the zero-matrix record still runs the vertex stage; the workaround is one kernel and pointset per piece (11 kernels where one would do). (2) the eyes' point-light shadow costs ~15 fps at 1280×720 in the app (41–44 fps with everything; 54–57 with no casting light; 60 with no shadow and a one-piece claw). (3) PIECE COUNT costs as much as triangles: dropping eight small instanced Geometries (3,440 triangles × 10 in all) was worth ~5 fps with shadows on while the header's GPU figure did not move (8–9 ms GPU, 24 ms frame) — pass and submit overhead per Geometry. NEW ORDER (consumer + lead): slice E → F1 compaction (a rejected or dead instance costs nothing) + §T1598b + a profile of what one more instanced Geometry costs → then D, C, F, G. Group's description warns until F1. **SLICE E LANDED `662b092f`:** a Material·WGSL declares `struct Instance { field: type, // @default … }` and reads `s.instance.<field>`; each field binds the points' attribute of the same name and type, or through the Geometry's `instanceAttributes` text (`glow = heat`, `glow = pick.z`); field types f32, vec2f, vec3f, vec4f, u32, vec4u; an unbound field reads its default; refusals `node.scene.instanceAttribute` name both sides, all at once. `s.instance` exists only when the source declares the struct, so every existing material's text is unchanged. three f32 fields cost ~0.1–0.2 ms on the lit draw at 4,000 × 716 triangles. ruling 2 landed with it: the Transform group is inactive and ignored on primitive instances, points and beams. T1640b|.|**A UNIFORM VALUE CANNOT CARRY AN ARRAY OF ROWS, SO GENERATORS UNROLL (the root the §B260 audit found under the Ramp, Grid Warp, the curve table and the Render's lights).** `UniformValue = number | boolean | readonly number[]` (`src/runtime/backend/plan.ts:21`): a pass's uniforms are named scalars and one flat vector each, so a table of rows becomes numbered members (`g0..g31`, `c0..c63`, `light{i}…`) and, in the Render, numbered CODE. the Ramp's docblock says so. wanted: a typed table as a uniform value (an array of structs with a run-time count beside it, written as one buffer region), or a small data-buffer resource a node can own, so a generator indexes rows in a loop; the three table nodes moved onto it; §V1029's gate then holds them flat. the lights do not wait for this (they take a storage buffer, §T1623b). the seam ruled for the lights (§T1623b slice 2: values for a region of a buffer, carried by the plan and written like a uniform block's) is this row's mechanism; the Ramp, Grid Warp and the curve table move onto it after the lights.|T1635b,B260,V1029
T1649b|.|**A BOARD THAT TAKES ONE COLUMN OR TWO BY THE WIDTH IT IS GIVEN, AND AN "ALL" VIEW ACROSS PANELS (owner, 2026-10-06, relayed by shaderloom-f1).** owner: *"i still would like an 'All' tab where we see all of them at once … and where there is space definitely 2 columns"*. the consumer built `panel_all` by hand: a second 16-column board repeating every member of its three Panels (a member on two Panels works; the banks join both by name), shipped with Phone off. what is asked of the app: (a) a board whose sections flow into one, two or more columns by the width of the surface showing it (desk pane, phone upright, phone sideways), so a project does not lay the same controls out twice; (b) an All view across the document's Panels on the desk and on the phone, made by the app, not authored. design first, with §T1610b's open items (pages are automatic from labels; a page with few columns has very large cells sideways; pages are derived on the phone only): what a board's authored grid means once the surface may re-flow it, and what stays where the author put it. ALSO THE OWNER, 2026-10-06 (relayed): *"the sliders for the controls could be a tiny bit less high on both app pane and on mobile. just a smidge too chunky"*. a board's row is as tall as its column is wide, so the column count is the only handle a project has on a control's height: the consumer went from eight columns to ten (`4bb29f77`) to make every control a little lower, re-gridding three boards. wanted in the same design: A ROW HEIGHT THAT IS NOT TIED TO THE COLUMN WIDTH (a number on the board, or a density the surface chooses), so "a little lower" is a value and not a re-layout.|T1607b,T1610b,T1517b,T1561b
T1648b|.|**A PRESET IS REMOVED AND RENAMED WHERE IT IS STORED, AND A BANK'S STRIP SAYS WHAT IT IS (owner, 2026-10-06, relayed by shaderloom-f1).** owner: *"how do we remove presets set in the controls?"* today: select the bank node, Inspector, Presets bank, Delete beside each; the board's strip has Store and no Delete, and the owner had made presets from the strip's Store. wanted on the DESK board's strip: delete and rename beside Store (one undoable command each; a deleted preset that a cue or a morph names says so before it goes), and a caption for the strip (the bank's role, by `surfaceNameOf`) so a row of names reads as what it is. the PHONE keeps its rule: it recalls, it never stores or deletes.|T1619b,T1517b,T1561b
T1647b|.|**PHONE: SCROLLING WITHOUT MOVING A SLIDER, SECOND ATTEMPT, DECIDED IN THE OWNER'S HAND (§T1609b failed on a real phone, 2026-10-06).** owner: *"also still pretty hard to not screw with the sliders when scrolling on mobile"*. §T1607b made the WHOLE WIDTH of every slider hot (relative drag from anywhere after 12 px along it), reasoned from Chromium's rules and WebKit's source and never held in a hand; a thumb's scroll starts on a slider nearly every time and often sideways enough to be taken. candidates, each an established answer: (K) THE KNOB ONLY — a slider follows a touch that starts on its thumb, as a native iOS slider does, and the rest of the track scrolls; (H) HOLD TO GRAB — a control follows only after the finger rests on it for a moment, a moving finger always scrolls; (L) A LOCK — the page is in scroll mode or play mode by one switch that is always in reach; (G) A GUTTER — a strip of every board is never a control (the consumer's layout stopgap, made the page's own). a design from reading has failed once, so THIS ROW IS DECIDED BY TRYING: the candidates are built behind one setting on the phone page, the owner tries each on the phone in one sitting, one stays and the rest are deleted with the setting. acceptance is the owner's word, then the touch-emulated spec for the chosen rule. also here: `phone-touch.spec.ts` reads the consumer's live Panels (edited twice by the consumer's session for its own layout changes) — it gets a frozen fixture of its own, as the bore test did. **BUILT AND ON MAIN FOR THE OWNER TO TRY: the frozen fixture `df5ee75d`, the trial `35845323` (the worker's runs: `phone-page.test.ts` 145, the seven phone test files 245, the touch spec 23 of 23 twice, the gates 3,607; the lead's verification of the landing is recorded with the next entry).** ONE CORE: a slider, fader or pad takes a touch after 12 px of travel its way, then moves by the travel; a MODE only says what must be true before that. ONE TRIAL CONTROL at the right end of the phone's tab bar, two lines, "Touch K" and "Rows 36", each the phone's own picker, kept per phone in `localStorage` (`loom.phone.trial`); every line of it is marked "T1647b trial … deleted when the owner has chosen". THE MODES: K THE KNOB ONLY (default) — the touch must land on the knob, drawn 56 px wide (about 9 mm, the thumb target of Parhi, Karlson and Bederson 2006) and kept whole at both ends; the rest of the track scrolls; a pad follows only from its puck and scrolls from everywhere else, so it needs no rail. H HOLD TO GRAB — the finger rests 200 ms within 8 px and the outline arrives; a finger that moves sooner is let go for that touch. L A LOCK — a Play / Scroll switch at the left end of the tab bar; in Scroll the board takes no touch and is dimmed; starts in Play each visit. G A STRIP — 56 px down the right or the left edge that always scrolls, the board inset beside it. A as §T1607b, to compare. K+G and K+H (a 100 ms rest) as one table row each. ROWS: 32, 36 or 44 px, default 36 (§B269). IN EMULATION every mode keeps its own promise: a board three screens tall flicked top to bottom and back from sliders, with flicks that start fast or hesitant, on the knob or beside it, wrote nothing; in K a drag from 4 px outside the drawn knob does nothing and a drag from the knob moves by travel with no jump. NOTHING HERE HAS BEEN HELD IN A HAND: whether a real thumb lands on a 56 px knob while scrolling, rests 200 ms, or wanders is the whole question and the owner's sitting answers it; iOS Safari in every mode is unverified. known rough edges: the trial control takes 72 px of the tab bar (a fourth tab's name elides at 375 px); in K the knob's outline is drawn over the caption's chip. the numbered recipe went to the owner 2026-10-06.|T1609b,T1607b,T1610b,T1561b
T1646b|.|**A COMPILED NODE HAS NO WAY TO RAISE A PROBLEM ON ONE FRAME AND NOT THE NEXT (found by §T1589b slice 2; the same gap §T1641b's inventory named: per-frame warnings have no reader).** a diagnostic that depends on a VALUE (a Light's Type driven to Spot in Single mode, a Range driven to zero, a count driven past a capacity) can only be said by the structural compile, which runs on a revision; `compileFrame` drops every recompiled node's diagnostics and only the value graph's own source is per-frame. wanted: a per-frame problem carrier for compiled nodes (a seam in `frame-compile.ts` and the app's frame loop, read by the Problems registry and by the headless harness), rate-limited so a value crossing a threshold every frame does not flood, with the rule for when a value-dependent problem appears and clears. the first use goes away with §T1623b slice 3 (a named Light becomes a row and a spot is a kind); the always-walked-rows warning of §T1623b is the second and stays. a third case (§T1652b's lane, 2026-10-06): a finding that a value causes two or more hops away through channels (a clamp far downstream of a slider) is no longer said at the write, since the values lane does not resolve the whole downstream of a channel; it is said at the next structural revision. the per-frame carrier would say it at once. **2026-10-06, from §T1652b's lane boundary (`802f9326`):** a frameless finding such as `parameter.expression.clamped` on a node that reads the written value through ANOTHER node's channel is now said at the next structural revision, not on the write.|T1589b,T1641b,T1623b
T1645b|.|**A NOTICE STILL RESIZES THE PANES: WHERE "OUTPUT STALE" LIVES (left by §B265; the owner's call).** since §B265 a notice takes its room from the foot of the window and no pane's top edge moves, but pane HEIGHTS still change when one toggles (the canvas 784 ↔ 815 px; the bottom dock's tab strip moves about 31 px), and "Output stale" toggles on every add-a-node-then-wire-it cycle. two ways to remove the twitch, neither built: (a) a permanently reserved one-line status row at the foot (31 px always spent, nothing ever moves); (b) "Output stale" as a chip in a row that already exists, as the shader pane does for its own stale mark (`dock-panes.tsx`, `.shaderStale`), the strip kept for notices that hold a decision — §T1121 chose the full sentence in the strip on purpose. also here: the node library's "compatible with … clear" banner pushes its list down a row when a wire is picked up; and the wire snap's first-connection frames (7 in 0.72 s) because the snap plays over the node's first compile.|B265,T1121,T1639b
T1644b|.|**THE WIRE SNAP: WHAT §T1639b PROPOSES AND DID NOT BUILD.** (1) THE NODE NUDGE: in the reference the target node is pushed about 10 px away from the wire at the snap, peaking at 130 ms and back by 400 ms; left out because it moves the node's box (§V389) — the owner's ruling, and if yes, as a transform on a visual layer that the box gates do not read. (2) a "this input is fed" mark: a hollow dot for an unfed input and a filled one for a fed input (Loom's analogue of the reference's dot fill), no tick and no new row chrome. (3) the nearest ACCEPTING port wins the range: today the library picks the closest handle whatever it is, so a nearer refusing port shadows a farther accepting one; needs hit-testing beside the library. (4) the strike: the reference's first arc on entering range is larger. (5) the snap for connections made ELSEWHERE (an agent, the Connections panel, undo and redo): only hand gestures on the canvas play it. (6) Escape cancels a pulled wire. (7) the look checked in Safari and Firefox, above 100 % zoom, inside a component dive, and with a finger on a real device.|T1639b,V389
T1638b|.|**A POINTSET'S `swap` SPLITS THE RENDER'S RUN: N GEOMETRIES ARE N DEVICE PASSES IN THE LAST TARGET DRAWN (found by §T1587b slice 2, on §T1604b's ground; derived and counted, not changed).** each pointset's `swap` is emitted after its last reader, which puts it between two Geometries' draws, and a swap ends a run (`renderPassRuns`). ten Geometries of ten pointsets: the shadow cube is one run of 61 draws, but the lit target (or the Normal layer when it is drawn last) is ten runs of one. moving the swaps after the Render's last draw would make the counted cases 2 and 5 device passes instead of 11 and 14. wanted: the swaps of pointsets a Render reads hoisted past its last draw (say what a later reader in the same frame then sees), with `render-pass-runs.test.ts` counting it. with §T1615b (3), the same class: a dispatch landing inside a run. also (§T1589b slice 1): in `encodeSegmented` a swap counts as work a dispatch would overtake, so every kernel in a frame costs one more encoder and one more submit — on the consumer four more dispatches were six more submits. same fix: the swaps hoisted, and counted.|T1604b,T1615b,T1587b
T1587b|.|**SWEEP / EXTRUDE ALONG A CURVE INTO A LIT SURFACE (proposed by shaderloom-f1, same doc).** a profile (ring, square, strip, custom) swept along a curve (§T1586b) into surface geometry with G-buffer writes: radial segments, radius, per-point scale, caps, twist. Notch: Spline Extruder ("useful for making tubes and tunnels"); TD has Sweep on the CPU only and no Sweep POP. consumer: the sentinel tunnel is geometry inside the Render (an extruded bore plus instanced modules), not a raymarched pass composited by depth, because neither product gives a raymarched pass the scene's lights and shadows. 3rd in the ruled build order, with §T1589b. note from §T1586b's design: a sweep of several strips cannot be one `grid:` claim (it would join each tube's end to the next tube's start); it needs a mesh claim or a sheet-aware grid. **DESIGN LANDED `a1da5a8b` (`docs/sweep-design-2026-10-05.md`), RULED BY THE LEAD as recommended, pending the consumer's review:** D1 the swept surface is a GRID CLAIM WITH SHEETS, `grid:{cols}x{rows}x{sheets}` — a kernel after the sweep keeps a correctly lit surface (the grid path works its normal out from the points), one strip is a plain `grid:` claim that needs no Render change, and many tubes are ONE Geometry (measured: 35,200 vertices as one Geometry 0.26 / 0.42 / 0.67 ms with no / directional / point shadow, as forty Geometries 1.76 / 3.95 / 12.65 ms); D2 the grid continues a `uv` attribute past a wrapped seam; D3 no interim mesh-claim form; D4 the grid's own normal is the only lit normal; D6 a mapped radius multiplies the authored one; D9 → §B255. node `pointSweep` ("Sweep", kind `sweep`): ports `points` (Path: strips with `position` and `orient` from Curve Frames) and optional `profile`; `profile` Ring | Square | Strip | Custom, `sides`, `smooth`, `radius`, `caps`, `facing`, `uvAlong` (Stretch | Metres | Points), `uvLength`; no twist on the Sweep (Curve Frames owns the frame); one dispatch, one thread per vertex. slices: 1 a sweep of one strip (no Render change; the tunnel's bore) and 3 caps + custom profile — IN BUILD; 2 sheets in the claim and the Render reading them (cables, a tentacle's skin) after the Render's shadow work. CONSUMER REVIEW (shaderloom-f1): no objection. a kernel AFTER the sweep is the shape wanted, not a displacement input (the relief is branching per vertex and writes a tag the material reads); the kernel must stay free to write `position` (the deck clamp is not a move along the normal) and the surface lit by normals derived after it. one strip for the bore with the deck as a second Geometry is better (the deck wants its own material). the repeated 115 m tail is acceptable if it is an exact copy BY DISTANCE (the relief hashes a plate by `bay mod 600`, lamps by station mod 15). slice 2 is wanted sooner: pipes as real swept tubes a claw can take hold of, cables, more than one kind of place. **SLICES 1 AND 3 LANDED `40a5bef0`, `404bf652`, `aa6c7e65` (gates 57 files / 3537):** `pointSweep` ("Sweep", kind `sweep`): one strip in, a plain `grid:` claim out, drawn by the existing Surface path; profiles Ring, Square, Strip and Custom (from the first strip of a `profile` input); `sides`, `smooth`, `radius` (a mapped f32 multiplies), `caps`, `facing`, `uvAlong`, `uvLength`; publishes `position`, `normal`, `uv` and every attribute of the path point except its frame; several strips are refused by name until slice 2. PROOFS: a straight path with a Ring equals the `pointTube` generator's vertices TO THE BIT and its lit, Normal and Depth outputs byte for byte, with a shadow cast and received; a kernel after the sweep that clamps the tube to a plane reads the plane's normal exactly; a cap covers exactly its outline's pixels. THE CONSUMER'S BORE from stock nodes (`point-sweep-bore.gpu.test.ts`, all 196,608 vertices against the project's kernel-bent grid): 0.11 mm on the 766 inner rings with the path taken from the project's formula, 2.7 mm on the first ring (a strip's end has one chord for its tangent, C13); through a Catmull-Rom Curve with control points every 1.2 m, 2.3 mm. measured pass: 0.02–0.06 ms at 200,000 vertices, 0.22–0.46 ms at 1,000,000. BUILDING IT CORRECTED THE DESIGN: a grid Surface is lit on BOTH sides (`abs(N · L)`), so Facing decides the `normal` attribute and the Normal output, not whether a tunnel is lit from inside; the sentinel tunnel is endless and periodic in z, not a loop (C10 is not its need); its centre line needs ~900 control points against the table's 64, so it is wired from the formula and a camera cannot ride it on the CPU (C12). for the consumer: one period is 960 m of z but 1,058.257 m of curve, so rows by Distance drift 7.4 mm a period — take rows by Count / Even Parameter, and carry z as a path attribute for the relief's hashes. follow-ups: C11 a Custom outline by length; C12 a longer typed table or a CPU reader for a formula path; C13 the tangent at a strip's two ends; C14 a port that can say "one strip with a frame". found, not fixed: the Render's fragment stage stands +Z in for a normal shorter than 1e-6 before normalising, so a grid with cells under ~0.5 mm reads +Z. **C13 AND THE BORE TEST'S DECOUPLING LANDED `caf7b640`, `1db5dff2`, `f40e58e9` (verified on main: typecheck, `curve.test`, `point-curve-frames.test`, `effective-schema-closure` 115; on Dawn `point-curve-frames`, `point-sweep-bore`, `point-sweep-render` 51 — the last on the Render as §T1604b left it; the worker ran 7 Dawn files 138, the 26 catalogue walkers, the gates 3539, the build).** (1) `point-sweep-bore.gpu.test.ts` reads a FROZEN copy of the bore (`point-sweep-bore.fixture.ts`: the centre line, the row rule and the kernel text, copied 2026-10-06 from sentinel-bot's `path.ts` at `1bc118e6` and `tunnel.ts` at `14b66ed2`, checked byte-equal and at 4,001 distances at copy time); it no longer imports `src/projects/sentinel-bot/**`, so the consumer can change its tunnel without turning an engine test red. (2) C13: Curve Frames aims an OPEN strip's two ends by their two nearest segments, `d + (d − e) × h ÷ (h + g)` (for even spacing `(−3p0 + 4p1 − p2) ÷ 2h`). the bore's first ring 2.7482 mm → 0.0144 mm, last ring 0.7261 → 0.0396 mm, worst inner ring 0.1139 mm unchanged to the last digit. THE WALK'S PROGRAM IS NOT TOUCHED: two passes after it (FIND, one invocation per strip; WRITE, one per 64 slots) rewrite only the slots in an end run, because two shader programs can round one expression differently on this device; the walk's nine frozen fingerprints are unchanged and on versus off are the same words at every interior slot. RULED BY THE LEAD AS BUILT: it is a parameter, `extrapolateEnds`, ON by default (a parabola through an L-shaped path leans its end back 18°, so a path of straight legs with a corner beside its end wants the chord; Houdini's Orientation Along Curve has the same toggle); Fixed Up ends use the method's own rule; an end is a RUN (every repeat of the end point is rewritten, or a sweep's padded rings tilt against the last real ring); two-point strips, closed strips and a straight end keep the chord exactly. cost, measured on Dawn: 0.02–0.05 ms without repeats, about 0.3 ms per million repeated slots (0.6 with the three vectors), beside a walk of 1.1–3.4 ms. ONE FIGURE WORSE: the tunnel's repeated part against its first part at the wall, 0.8 mm → 1.1 mm at an end ring (an aimed end counts a point's rounding twice, and the rounding is large at 1,000 m). fourteen mutations red-verified. **SLICE 2 (SHEETS) LANDED `83a45644` (design re-read), `671ee9e3`, `6346235f`, `a1e6d2b0` (verified on main beside the Rope: typecheck; `grid-sheets`, `point-sweep`, `codegen`, `topology`, `point-topology`, `point-rope`, `kernel-steps`, `generated-text` 224; on Dawn `point-sweep-sheets`, the three one-strip sweep files, `scene-preview`, `point-rope`, `render-pass-runs` 105; the 26 catalogue walkers 444; the gates 57 files / 3547).** THE CLAIM: `grid:{cols}x{rows}x{sheets}` with the wrap flags after it; slot = `(sheet × rows + row) × cols + col`; `cols`, `rows`, both wraps and the caps are ONE sheet's and no cell joins two sheets; one sheet is written without the third number, so every shipped claim is the string it was. `ctx.dim` describes one sheet and gains `sheet` and `sheets`; the Topology node has a Sheets parameter; the preview tile and Render Surface draw sheets. THE DRAW: ONE vertex-pulled draw of `sheets × cells × 6` vertices in every pass that draws the Geometry — no index buffer, no join triangles. ONE emitter a program; the sheeted text is a branch taken only for more than one sheet, and one-sheet programs are pinned by fingerprints recorded from main before the branch existed (17, all green). NO BIT MOVED IN THE VARIANT: N straight strips equal N `pointTube` generators' vertices to the bit and lit, Normal and Depth byte for byte with a shadow cast and received; the same against N one-strip sweeps at 1.2 m offsets, under a casting point light, and for closed strips. T1589b|.|**LIGHTS FROM A POINTSET: A MANY-LIGHT PATH INSIDE THE RENDER (proposed by shaderloom-f1, same doc; do not fork from §T1402b's deferred fixtures).** Notch clones lights and culls them on the GPU ("Lights are generated and culled on the GPU, allowing them to be cloned"); TD stays forward with a per-object light mask. wanted: position, colour, intensity, range and cone from point attributes; a deferred or clustered many-light path inside the Render; include and exclude lists; shadows for a chosen few. the furnace's project-code lamp pass (§T1402b) is the prototype and is switched over when this lands. 3rd in the ruled build order, with §T1587b. consumer's critical path (shaderloom-f1): lights BEFORE sweep within this tier — the tunnel bore can be a kernel-bent grid surface today, a lamp every few metres has no stock path. consumer data point (`60683bbe`): sentinel-bot is at the forward limit with FOUR lights (three lamps of a tunnel that has one every 12.8 m, plus the eyes); the lamp plates beyond those glow and light nothing. **DESIGN LANDED `98c5f06c` (`docs/lights-from-pointset-design-2026-10-06.md`), RULED BY THE LEAD as recommended (L1–L12), the consumer's review asked for (C1–C6).** THE METHOD IS CLUSTERED FORWARD: a compute pass per Render sorts the lights into a grid (about 144 screen tiles by 24 exponential depth slices, 3,456 cells) and the lit shader walks only its pixel's cell; a cell is a BITMASK, one bit per light slot, not a list — a list has a length and drops lights silently past it (Notch documents 64 per tile), a bitmask's only limit is the pointset's capacity, known at compile and refused by name. WHY NOT DEFERRED (the furnace's shape): the G-buffer is single-sample, so every silhouette would be aliased in exactly the lamps' light (the consumer renders MSAA with no temporal pass); additive geometry, primitive instances, points and beams write no G-buffer layer; it holds no material model; the lists would need a geometry id layer. WHY NOT A PLAIN LOOP: it is the same design with one cell and linear in the count. MEASURED (M3 Max, Dawn on Metal, headless). a raw WebGPU probe, a 240 m tube from inside, 1280×720 rgba16float 4× MSAA, the Render's GGX and falloff, GPU ms for 16 / 64 / 256 / 1,024 lights: unrolled blocks (today) 0.72 / 1.38 / 9.31 / not run; plain loop 0.26 / 0.52 / 1.84 / 7.93; grid with bitmask 0.20 / 0.20 / 0.33 / 0.85 with a build of under a timer step / 0.07 / 0.39; a tiles-only grid walks every lamp of a tunnel (0.46 / 0.66 / 2.23 / 9.11); lists of 64 drop 184 lights in the fullest cell at 1,024. THE CONSUMER'S DOCUMENT TODAY, extra Light nodes added by script, shadows off: 5 lights 6.75 ms GPU, 13 → 7.54, 21 → 10.75, 37 → 24.05 ms and 1.2 s of `backend.compile` — superlinear, cause not found (§B260). the proposed path on the consumer is COMPUTED, not measured: 75 lamps about 0.5–0.8 ms. THE NODE SURFACE: no new node — the LIGHT gains a `points` input and `mode` (Single | Points, compile-time), as a Geometry has Instances; only `position` is read by name, every other per-light value is the Light's own parameter in Map mode (`color`, `intensity`, `range`, `cone` multiply; `position`, `direction` replace; `orient` turns Direction per point); Range defaults to 10 in Points mode and a light with zero intensity or mapped range is off; `litOnly` / `litExclude` name geometries in both modes and govern lighting only (an excluded geometry still casts that light's shadow); Type: Spot in both modes with `cone` and `coneSoftness`, for which `kind` becomes compile-time; a CASTING light is a Light in Single mode (the pointset's kernel dims the stations the named Lights stand in for) and Cast Shadows in Points mode is inactive; limits by name at compile: 1,024 points of capacity a Render (`node.scene.lightCapacity`), seven pointset Lights a Render (`node.scene.lightSources`); one more storage binding on a lit draw (8 of 8 at the baseline at worst); no frame of latency (kernel, resolve, gather, grid and lit draws in one frame); a Render with no pointset Light emits today's plan and text byte for byte. SLICES: 1 point lights from a pointset, culled (twelve acceptance items: analytic pixels under three lights; the grid's picture equals a one-cell grid's byte for byte; a kernel-moved light lights frame f from its frame-f place; E13, E33, E28, E69, E79 plans unchanged; the consumer's frame with 75 lamps measured) — IN BUILD; 2 cone and aim; 3 the lists; 4 every lit draw (`sceneInstancesWgsl`); 5 the furnace switched over, `lamps.ts` deleted. accepted limitations are rows §T1622b–§T1633b (shadow slots for the nearest lights of a pointset is §T1622b). found on the way, to fix in slice 1: `docs/shadow-casters-design-2026-10-05.md` says TouchDesigner's Light Mask is on the material (it is on the Geometry COMP's Render page); the header comment of `src/nodes/shaders/scene-render.wgsl.ts` says a uniform array carries thousands of lights (they are generated members and blocks). NOT CHECKED by the design: neither product was run; Notch's algorithm is known from release notes only; deferred was not prototyped; ortho, SSAA and non-16:9 are designed, not tried. **THE CONSUMER'S ANSWERS (shaderloom-f1, 2026-10-06):** C1 all 75 stations as one Light (the three-lamp window with `near` exists only because a Light node is dear); C2 no lamp casts on its live tier today, three named lamp Lights cast offline, dimmed in the kernel by `1 − near`; C3 Range 24 is fine provided the falloff is windowed to zero at the range (it is); C4 SPOTS — the owner called the lit air under a lamp "a random sphere … not a cone from the actual light source down": Cone about 150 with a high Cone Softness, `orient` from the path's frame (slice 2); C5 leave the motes and the haze; C6 none excluded; sections 3.1–3.5 fit, Map mode per parameter is right. NEW NEED, owner's words relayed: *"the tunnels could use a bit more detail work too, different lights at different positions in the tube and stuff like that"* — wall lamps at shoulder height, beacons at the alarm stations, a ring of lamps round a hall's crown; with §B260 the consumer adds no Light nodes for it and draws them as emissive fixtures until slice 1 is on main. **REVISED BY §B260 AND THE ONE-LIGHT-PATH DESIGN (§T1623b, 2026-10-06):** section 2.5 of the design and ruling L5 are gone (a Single light does NOT keep its block beside the grid: on the Render's text the blocks are 18.7 ms at 64 lights and a loop 1.1–1.25); L4 is reversed (`kind` stays a value; a pointset of directional lights is legal with a warning past a count); the lists (slice 3) have one mechanism; slice 4 (every lit draw) is §T1623b's slice 7; acceptance 8 of slice 1 ("a Render with no pointset Light has the plan it had") holds for slice 1 and ends, by ruling, when named Lights become rows; the design's section 5 figures were taken without a reference pass and stand in shape only. **SLICE 1 LANDED `c5fa6d19` (one squash; main's tree is byte for byte the worker's tested tip; confirmed on main: typecheck; `light-points.test`, the V1029 gate, `scene-light-guard`, `generated-text`, `grid-sheets` 84; on Dawn `light-points`, `scene-light-guard`, `scene-render` 30; the worker ran 14 named files 320, six Dawn files 56, the gates 58 files / 3,580, the 26 catalogue walkers 444, the build).** A LIGHT WITH MODE: POINTS IS N LIGHTS FROM ONE NODE: `points` input, maps on `color`, `intensity`, `range`, `position`; three dispatches in the Render's shadow phase (the Light's resolve, the gather, the grid build) and one loop in the Surface generator. all twelve acceptance items hold (item 10, MSAA, held but no mutation reaches it); 51 mutations, 49 red. BUILT AS THE FIRST SLICE OF THE ONE LIGHT PATH (§T1623b): a 64-byte record carrying kind, shadow slot and source number; `kind` a VALUE (a directional set is N suns, a driven Type stays values-only; `node.scene.lightKind` is gone); a rangeless or directional row sets its bit in every cell; every loop bound is read from the table's four-word header at run time; the lit draw, resolve, gather and build are each ONE STRING at 3, 300 and 1,000 lights. the table is laid out row by row (every `place`, then every `color`, `aim`, `cone`: 0.43–0.46 of the reference against 0.51–0.56 record by record at 1,024 lights with nothing shaded) and the lit draw reads it as `array<vec4u>` (one load a row instead of four: 0.58 against 0.67 at 64). a Render with no pointset Light keeps plan and text: five frozen fingerprints, §B260's 18 digests, the one-sheet pins and §V1029's exact debt sizes hold. `LightPayload` gains an optional `points`. limits by name: 1,024 points of capacity, seven pointset Lights; lit primitive instances, points or beams beside a pointset Light warn `node.scene.lightDraw` until the instances generator's slice. THE CHOICE OF METHOD RE-TAKEN AND HOLDS: a plain loop over the grid with its build is 2.4× at 256 lights and 4.9× at 1,024. NO CLIFF: a row costs 0.0087–0.0095 of the reference from 64 to 1,024. lit text 8.2 thousand characters at every count against 131 thousand for 64 blocks; a new-text lit pipeline 49 ms against 332. `kind` as a value costs the walk a tenth to a fifth where nothing can be culled (0.57–0.61 against 0.49–0.51 with the kind a constant) — the price of the property, and the grid walk can drop the test once always-walked rows have their own region. FOUND: a kernel's swap between two draws of the colour target splits the device pass, and in `encodeSegmented` a swap counts as work a dispatch would overtake, so each kernel costs one more encoder and submit (four more dispatches are six more submits; §T1638b); a Light in Single mode with Points wired keeps the upstream kernel dispatching, read by nothing (§T1599b); the mock device does not parse WGSL — a reserved word as a name (`from`) was caught only on Dawn (§T1643b). T1590b|.|**A PATH FOLLOWER ON THE VALUE GRAPH (proposed by shaderloom-f1, same doc).** a CPU reader of a path (§T1586b) for cameras and rigid objects: position, heading with a look-ahead, bank, heading-flip protection. T1599b|.|**A SOCKET APPEARS ONLY WHEN IT APPLIES (from §T1581b).** the Geometry's "Shape Mesh" input is read only in Instances mode with Shape: Mesh, yet it is drawn on every Geometry and makes each one a port row taller (E13 needed 16 px). §V122 hides parameters that do not apply; ports have no such rule. wanted: a port-level `inactiveWhen` — the node box, the canvas, connect and the layout rule (§V389) all treat a hidden port as absent; decide what happens to an existing wire when its port stops applying (keep it and show it dimmed with a named warning, or refuse the mode change by name), and how TouchDesigner treats an unused input. then the Shape Mesh socket uses it. the same class (§T1589b slice 1): a Light in Single mode with its Points input wired keeps the upstream kernel dispatching every frame, read by nothing — an input a mode does not read must not keep its producer alive.|T1581b,V122,V389,V372
T1608b|.|**ADDITIVE GEOMETRY: ALPHA AND DRAW ORDER DIFFER BY MODE (found fixing §B256, not changed).** (1) an additive billboard, quad or box ADDS ITS ALPHA over a transparent background, an additive Surface adds none — measured: `[0,0,0,0]` becomes `[0,0,0,255]` under a black additive quad, so such a glow composited over another layer cuts a black shape. (2) additive Points, Beams and primitive instances draw in Scenes order, additive Surfaces are deferred to last, so an opaque geometry listed after an additive one and lying behind it paints over the glow (the Blend description now says to list them after what they glow over). wanted: one rule for every mode (light adds colour and no alpha; additive draws after every opaque draw), with the up to 16 examples whose pictures move listed and their claims re-derived.|B256,T1411b,T917
T1611b|.|**PHONE PAGE: SLIDERS AND PADS ARE NOT KEYBOARD-OPERABLE (found building §T1607b, not changed).** a slider on the phone page answers a pointer only; no focus, no arrow keys, no role. a phone page opened on a laptop, or a switch-access user, cannot move one. wanted: `role=slider` with value attributes, focus, arrows and Home/End through the same write path, toggles and buttons as real buttons; assert the wire, not the DOM.|T1607b
T1610b|.|**PHONE PAGE: WHAT §T1607b DECIDED ALONE AND THE OWNER MAY OVERRULE, AND WHAT IT LEFT OUT.** (1) the momentary Button's hold starts 150 ms late and a held finger that slides far enough to scroll lets go; the alternative is an immediate press and no scrolling from buttons — a per-control choice if both are wanted. (2) relative drag is the only response; absolute (jump-to-touch) as a per-control option, as TouchOSC and Lemur offer. (3) a tap on an XY pad no longer jumps the puck. (4) pages are automatic from labels, so the shipped Scene Panel shows All / Scene / Camera with no opt-out. (5) SIDEWAYS: the pager's 52 px row is a seventh of the screen and a page with few columns has very large square cells. (6) no pages for legacy text-layout Panels. (7) pages are derived on the phone only; the desk has no such view. each needs the owner's hands on §T1609b first. (8) the phone's cue list header gives the next cue's name about 24 px at 375 wide ("show" reads "s…"); its inner rows are a fixed 34 px (§B269 left the cue list out). seen by shaderloom-f1 on its Presets panel (`bce42b04`).|T1607b,T1609b
T1609b|.|**PHONE PANEL SCROLLING ON A REAL PHONE — THE OWNER'S LIVE TEST (§T1607b was verified in headless Chromium only).** iOS Safari and Android Chrome are unrun. the questions a device answers: (a) iPhone: while dragging a slider, does a finger that wanders up or down make the page scroll and the slider let go (WebKit's late cancel)? if so the value must stay and a second touch continue from it; (b) a 45° start becomes a scroll or a drag, never both — which, per phone; (c) Android's slop is the platform's, not the emulation's 15 px: does the 12 px take still feel immediate; (d) a drag from the very left edge against Safari's back swipe; (e) the page jumping when Safari's toolbars hide; (f) sideways, whether two navigation rows leave room on Scene. the numbered recipe (18 steps, sentinel's three Panels) was handed to the owner 2026-10-06. **THE OWNER TRIED IT ON A REAL PHONE, 2026-10-06 (relayed by shaderloom-f1): A FAIL.** *"also still pretty hard to not screw with the sliders when scrolling on mobile"*. the direction lock and relative drag of §T1607b are not enough in the hand. the consumer's stopgap is layout: every control on its phone panels takes six columns of eight, leaving the right quarter bare to scroll from. the redesign is §T1647b; this row closes when the owner's hand says so.|T1607b
T1606b|.|**SHADOW CASTERS: WHAT §T1598b LEFT.** (1) a per-light `visible_<light>` list for INSTANCED geometry (weigh after §T1604b: an indirect draw costs ~0.05 ms per device pass today); (2) reach for directional lights (a sphere against the shadow box); (3) a bound from other producers (a grid, a Point Transform, a kernel that declares one) and a tighter shape than a sphere — a floor's sphere holds any light standing on it, so a floor is in all six faces; (4) the pipeline inspector does not show that a draw is skipped this frame. CONSUMER DATA POINT (shaderloom-f1, 2026-10-06, `2bc870d4`): item (3) is what would put the tunnel lamps' shadows back in sentinel-bot's live tier — the robot is 645,000 triangles of kernel-placed instances with nothing to cull by, so every cube face draws all of it (about 3.9 million triangles a light); a bound for kernel-placed instances lets a face skip them. see also §T1620b.|T1598b,T1604b,T1592b
T1605b|.|**THE KALEIDOSCOPE STARTER COMPONENT READS TWO LFOS OF ITS HOST DOCUMENT (found by §T1593b's equivalence check).** its inner `facets` reads `op('driftx1')` and `op('drifty1')`, nodes that exist only in the document the component was saved from; in the two on-nothing documents that embed it those references name nothing. a component that only drifts beside two particular nodes is not a component. wanted: the component owns its two LFOs (or publishes two inputs for them), the starter is regenerated, and a gate fails a starter component whose graph references a name outside itself.|T1593b,T1221
T1620b|.|**A SHADOW-ONLY CASTER: A GEOMETRY THAT IS IN A LIGHT'S LIST BUT NOT IN THE LIT PASS (proposed by shaderloom-f1 from sentinel-bot's live tier, 2026-10-06).** a cube shadow draws the lit geometry itself: the robot's 645,000 triangles six times a light. the other engines let a low-polygon stand-in cast for a dense object (TouchDesigner: a Geometry COMP's Render flag off with a light's Shadow Casters naming it; Notch: per-object Visible / Cast Shadows flags — CHECK both against the docs before designing, neither is read yet). wanted: a Geometry (or a flag on it) that casts and is not drawn in colour, Depth or Normal, and its counterpart, a lit Geometry that does not cast; named in caster lists like any other (§T1598b); a diagnostic when a stand-in casts for nothing that is lit. design note with the TD/Notch comparison first. the consumer can also cut its kit (the ring is 716 triangles, 540 times), which this does not replace.|T1598b,T1606b,T1561b
T1637b|.|**ROPE: MANY SHORT STRANDS ARE THROUGHPUT-BOUND (R18 of §T1585b, measured in slice 1).** a million points as 18,181 strands of 55 cost 1.43–1.50 ms a step against 0.44 ms for a plain kernel over the same points: one invocation a strand walks its points through storage reads and writes. wanted: function-local arrays for strands under a length, so a short strand is solved in registers and written once; measured with a reference pass (§B260).|T1585b
T1636b|.|**THE BACKEND WRITES STEP UNIFORMS BY NAME INTO ANY BLOCK OF A STEPPED DISPATCH, AND NOTHING RESERVES THE NAMES (R19 of §T1585b, found by a test in slice 1).** a member called `iterations`, `substep`, `seed` (and the others the region writer knows) in a stepped dispatch's uniform block is overwritten each step with the region's value; the Rope's own Newton cap was named `iterations` and silently read 1. the Rope has a definition test; every other node that declares kernel steps is unguarded, and a Custom kernel's author can collide without knowing. wanted, as a seam fix and not a per-node test: ONE list of the names the region writer owns, a refusal by name at compile when a definition or an author's Params declares one for another meaning (the Render's `SURFACE_RESERVED_NAMES` is the idiom), and a gate over every definition that declares steps.|T1585b,T1583b
T1635b|.|**GENERATED SHADER TEXT MUST NOT GROW WITH A COUNT THE DOCUMENT DECIDES: THE AUDIT, THE RULE AND ITS GATE (owner, 2026-10-06, on §B260: *"we do the real cure right so it becomes a core fix of the whole app and not an inplace shader trick of a single patch"*).** §B260 is one instance of a shape: N generated blocks, one per document item, combined in one function. THE CURE FOR LIGHTS is one light path (§T1623b: every light is a row in the Render's light table walked by one loop, casting lights included through an indexable shadow resource, so the lit text holds no light and a change of light count recompiles nothing); its design is the last section of `docs/light-cost-investigation-2026-10-06.md`, reviewed before it is built. THE REST OF THE APP: an audit of every generator for text or plan structure that grows with a document count (projectors, environments, layer stacks and N-input compositing, fused effect chains, kernel attributes and steps, instance attributes, Group predicates, preview synthesis), each classed as §B260-shaped, compile-time only, pass-count only or bounded, with the largest count any shipped document reaches — `docs/generated-text-growth-audit-2026-10-06.md`, LANDED `19a69805` (read from the generators, then measured in TEXT through the real `compileGraph` at N = 1, 2, 4, 16; all 112 shipped documents compiled; no GPU run). THE RULE becomes an invariant (§V1029, reserved): counts are data, not text; exceptions are listed with a bound and a reason. THE GATE is on the cause, not a clock: each generator's text derived at several counts, identical or within a declared ledger whose bounds can only go down. also from §B260: the reference-pass timing harness becomes a tool of the test harness. **WHAT THE AUDIT FOUND:** THE §B260 SHAPE EXISTS IN FOUR PLACES, ALL IN `src/nodes/shaders/scene-render.wgsl.ts`, none bounded: R1 the Surface generator's light blocks (PBR 1,956 bytes a light, `fs` 121,482 bytes at 64; largest shipped 13); R2 the instances generator's own copy of the light block (primitive instances, billboards, beams; largest shipped 3); R3 projector blocks appended to the same `lit` in both (1,261 bytes plain, 1,851 with cookie and occlusion; largest shipped 5; their additions sit under two `if`s, which §B260 measured as keeping them out of the cliff); R4 a casting light's shadow lookup inside its block (4,012 bytes directional, 4,140 point; bounded only by 16 sampled textures a stage; largest shipped 6 casting). the largest shipped chain is 14 blocks and 30 `lit +=` in one 38,685-byte `fs` (on-nothing/title), the longest function in any shipped plan. a light-count change today recompiles every lit text of every Render that lists it (worst shipped: sentinel-bot, 4 lit texts, 154 KB). BOUNDED CHAIN: Composite's fold (`acc = blendPixel(acc, sample)` a layer, 139 bytes and a binding each, refused past 8 by `node.compile.tooManyInputs`). ON PURPOSE: `PERLIN_4_CORNERS`, 16 unrolled blocks, a definition constant. EVERYTHING ELSE grows as declarations, independent statements or passes sharing a text (point kernel 426 bytes and 2 functions an attribute; compaction 311; Render geometries 0 text and up to 12 passes each). THE DATA FORM ALREADY EXISTS in the app: the Cache / Echo / Slit Scan ring (one `texture_2d_array` and a uniform), loop regions for substeps and kernel steps — text byte-identical across counts, measured. WHY ROWS GET UNROLLED: `UniformValue = number | boolean | readonly number[]` (`runtime/backend/plan.ts`) cannot carry an array of rows; the Ramp, Grid Warp (`g0..g31`) and the curve table (`c0..c63`) work round it with numbered members (§T1640b). small waste: the shadow matte declares and binds every shadow map though it reads three. THE RULE IS §V1029, as proposed with one addition by the lead (exception (d): a bounded chain of 8 or fewer under a named refusal with a linear-cost measurement on record — Composite; kernel attributes' byte bound counts as a stated count). THE GATE AS FIRST DESIGNED: 106 count axes derived from the registry (15 variadic ports, 23 pointset inputs, 52 compile-time numbers, 16 code parameters), a positive control first (it must class today's `render.lights` as a chain at 1,888 bytes an item), cost a few seconds, no GPU. not read by the audit: `src/runtime/backend/vgpu/**`, document sources and project shaders (author WGSL can write the same shape; the gate does not see it). **THE GATE LANDED `f5fa2e85` (+ `17b6aaac`: the instruction files count 58 gate files; verified on main: typecheck; the new file with `generated-text`, `scene-light-guard`, `gate-list` 47; the worker ran the gates once, 58 files / 3,573).** `src/compiler/generated-text-growth.test.ts`, 26 tests, 2.1–2.5 s under vitest, no GPU: 127 count axes DERIVED over 153 definitions (the five classes plus a sixth the derivation needed, compile-time STRING parameters — Group predicates, Instance Attributes, Mesh File In's Lamps are lists written in strings), 141 ledger rows, all 17 `generatedOnce` generators run under some row; compiled at 1, 2, 4, 15, 16 so the numbers are taken on two unit steps (the second item and the last). `NOT_YET_DATA` (all §T1623b, exact sizes that can only move by an edit): `render.lights` a chain through `lit`, `fs` +1,885 a light (+1,924 for the sixteenth with the stopgap's guard), unbounded; the same in the instances generator +1,823; casting +3,860 directional and +3,835 point, bounded at 16 by `compiler/binding-budget`; `render.projectors` +971 plain and +1,447 with cookie and occlusion. exception (d): Composite's six blend axes, a chain through `acc`, +82 and a binding an input, refused past 8 — MEASUREMENT OWED. Switch is NOT a chain (a `switch` arm carries nothing): statements, bounded at 8. exception (a) has its own derived list: every node's minimal graph is compiled and any function writing one accumulation more than 8 times outside a loop must be named — it finds only `perlin4`, 16 times (the next largest in the catalogue is 6). the Rope's only axis is flat; sheets is a branch. WHAT THE GATE CANNOT SEE: author WGSL and the document sources that build it with loops of their own; cost (it asserts form, never time); a value carried through a pointer argument or an array write; one node's count as a literal in another node's text; a fixed chain only a non-default mode emits. T1619b|.|**RESET A CONTROL, OR ALL OF THEM, TO WHAT WAS SAVED — ON THE DESK AND ON THE PHONE (owner, 2026-10-06, relayed by shaderloom-f1).** owner: *"ways to reset controls individually or all according to what was saved or something should be something useful accessible on both phone and browser"*. what exists: a Presets bank on a Panel is drawn on both, so "all" can be authored today as a preset holding every control's shipped value (sentinel-bot does, `2bc870d4`: three banks `presets_robot|scene|lights`, one preset `saved` each; `panels.test.ts` moves every control and recalls). what does not exist: (a) ONE control back to its saved value, by a gesture that cannot be made by accident now that touch is relative (§T1607b): a double tap, a long press, or a small reset mark on the control; (b) "saved" as a thing the document knows without an author writing a preset: the value in the file as last saved, or a snapshot taken by a "Set as default" action — a preset written by hand goes stale the moment a slider's shipped value changes; (c) a Panel-level "Reset all" that needs no bank. decide which "saved" it is first; (a) and (c) follow from it. acceptance on both surfaces: move a slider, reset it, it reads the saved value and ONE write went out; a scroll or a drag never resets. **DESIGN LANDED `59d90319` (`docs/control-reset-design-2026-10-06.md`); three questions go to the owner, the lead builds on the recommendations unless overruled.** WHICH "SAVED": a DEFAULT stored on the control in the document and moved only by "Set as default" on the desk — what TouchDesigner custom parameters, TouchOSC (`Default`, `Default Pull`), Open Stage Control and Notch keep. it starts as the value in the file through a one-time definition `migrate` (Slider, Toggle, XY Pad to definition version 2; no `SCHEMA_VERSION` bump), and `parametersFor` makes the inspector's existing "Reset to default" mean the same number. the alternative, the file as opened, already exists as `parameter.revert` (§T1184) but MOVES BY ITSELF: performed values are written on every save and autosave, so a reload or a crash mid-show makes wherever the sliders were the new "saved". (the row's first text was wrong about TouchOSC: it has no double-tap-to-default property; the built-in double-tap reset is Open Stage Control's `doubleTap`.) GESTURES, one rule: nothing resets from one press. PHONE: a DOUBLE TAP on a slider or pad (each tap ends in `pointerup` inside the control within 300 ms, under 10 px of travel, never taken by the control, not on a page still scrolling; the second within 300 ms and 32 px; fires on the second lift); a toggle has no gesture (a tap is its reset; a dot shows when it is off its default); Button, bank, cue list and Layer do not reset. DESK: right-click opens a short `control` menu (Reset, Set as default, Reset all on this Panel, Set all as default on this Panel) — not double-click, which the owner removed from number fields (§T1033) and which would write two moves first on a desk slider; one keymap entry and palette entries. SEEN: a tick on the track (a ring on the pad) at the default, brighter while the value is away; on the phone a dot on a Panel's tab. RESET ALL: phone, a ↺ in the tab bar with a count opens a sheet that asks once (a phone has no undo), the shown Panel only; desk, a ↺ in the Controls tab header, one undo group, no question. Set as default is desk only: no phone write can reach it. THE WRITE: two DOMAIN commands, `control.reset` and `control.setDefault`, `{ nodeIds } | { all: true }`, one patch, one undo group, one audit entry each, registered where `preset.recall` is so the headless server has them; the phone sends one POST `{ handle, values: { reset: true }, phase: "commit" }`; the snapshot gains each control's default. SLICES: S1 the default and the two commands (definition shape changes; E81 and E82 are the shipped examples with controls; presets skip the default keys); S2 the desk; S3 the phone's wire; S4 the phone page (`phone-touch.spec.ts`; the real-phone check joins §T1609b). FOUND: "Reset to default" on a Slider's Value gives 0.5 whatever its range (§T1184's pattern on controls; S1's `parametersFor` fixes it); `resetValue` in `src/ui/controls/drag-math.ts` has had no production caller since §T1033. what is left out is §T1634b; a defect found on the way is §B261. NOT STARTED: waits for a building slot behind §B260. **THE OWNER ASKED AGAIN, 2026-10-06 (relayed by shaderloom-f1):** *"resetting in the controls is not visible for me anywhere … i have to reload right now if i screw something up. want to be able reset individual controls or all page or all"*. the three design questions went to the owner and are unanswered; by standing instruction the lead builds on the recommendations (DEFAULT as the saved value; a double tap on the phone; Reset all asks first on the phone). also from the consumer: its reset presets were named `saved` and did not read as a reset (renamed `reset_robot`, `reset_all`), and a bank's strip on a board says nothing about what the bank is (§T1648b). S1 IN BUILD. **S1 LANDED `b533dfc2` (verified on main: typecheck; `control-default-commands`, `presets/commands`, `controls`, `bus`, `parameter-controls`, the consumer's `panels.test.ts` 87; `phone-touch.spec.ts` 9 of 9; the 26 catalogue walkers 447; `pnpm test:first-import` 282; the gates 60 files / 3,608; the worker ran 41 named files 763, the two examples' claims on Dawn 20, the build).** Slider, Toggle and XY Pad store `defaultValue`, `defaultOn`, `defaultX`, `defaultY` (definition version 2 with a `migrate`: default := stored value; no `SCHEMA_VERSION` bump); `parametersFor` makes the stored default the value key's schema default, so the inspector's "Reset to default" on a Slider goes to the slider's own default instead of 0.5. TWO DOMAIN COMMANDS in `src/domain/commands/control-default-commands.ts`, registered by `createDomainBus`: `control.reset` and `control.setDefault`, `{ nodeIds } | { all: true }` parsed by the bus, a Panel's id naming its members; one patch, one audit entry, one undo group, split from a drag's transaction; a driven key is left alone and named; nothing to change is refused by name. `control.fromParameter` writes the default, so a control made from a parameter is born at it. `controls.ts` exports `controlDefaultState(node)` (defaults, current, away, driven) for S2 and S3; "away" is further than 1/10000 of the range. §B261 FIXED IN THE SAME FEW LINES: one table, `CONTROL_STATE_KEYS` read through `presetHolds` — a whole-control preset holds only what a hand moves, a key named outright is still stored, a default is never stored and never recalled. TO KNOW: a code-built document's builder now writes version-2 controls, and a control whose source authors NO default reads 0.5 clamped into its range — sentinel-bot's source must author its defaults (its committed file, version 1, migrates correctly when opened); S2 makes a missing default a refusal by name and a gate, not a silent 0.5. node migration runs on the root graph at load only, so a control inside a saved component definition is not migrated (Ramp v2 has the same limit). the "which keys are the value" table still exists in four other places (`control-widget.tsx`, `midi-controls.ts`, the phone's `READ_KEYS` and `PHONE_WRITABLE_KEYS`). a whole-Button preset still captures `held` and `presses`. S2 (THE DESK) IN BUILD. **S2, THE DESK, LANDED `4d63f6ff` (+ `91e146bb`; verified on main: typecheck; `control-default-commands`, `control-reset`, the class gate, `menus/schemas`, `bus` 111; headless e2e `control-reset.spec.ts` and `phone-touch.spec.ts` 25; the gates 62 files / 3,629 — after the lead removed a ledger line that was stale at the landing; the worker ran 74 named files 1,318, the catalogue walkers 451, the two examples' claims 40, the build). screenshots from the real app went to the owner.** THE MARK: two notches at a slider's default at the top and bottom of its track (never across the caption or the value), a ring on the pad, a corner dot on a toggle off its default; bright in the text colour while away. ONE CONTROL: a right-click opens the `control` menu (a new menus-as-data surface): Reset, Set as default, Reset all on the Panel, Set all as default on the Panel; a row that could only refuse is greyed with the command's own sentence; on a control's own canvas node the widget gives the control menu and the rest of the node the node menu. RESET ALL: a ↺ with the count in the Controls tab's header, a popover with one sentence and one button, one patch, one undo. `mod+alt+r` resets the selected controls on the canvas. palette: `control.resetAll` and `control.setAllDefaults`. S3 and S4 (the phone) wait for the owner's choice of touch mode (§T1647b).|T1607b,T1610b,T1517b,T1561b

T1657b|.|**A NAMED LIGHT WITH A RANGE THAT COVERS THE PICTURE COSTS MORE AS A ROW THAN IT DID AS A BLOCK (found by §T1623b slice 3; the same pictures to the byte).** 16 lights of Range 30 on the floor: blocks 0.94–1.02 of the reference against rows 1.45–1.48; 64: 4.05–4.30 against 5.70–6.22. a row found through a cell reads four rows and tests a cone it mostly has not; where a light does not reach, a row costs a read and a compare, which is the grid's whole point. one shipped document has such Lights (the consumer's three) and its frame did not move. the cure is the one that worked for the always-walked rows: a cell's rows split by kind, two passes over a cell's words. measure on a document that has many ranged named Lights before building.|T1623b,T1625b

T1651b|.|**A SAMPLE-AND-HOLD VALUE NODE (asked by shaderloom-f1 for sentinel-bot's director, 2026-10-06).** wanted: a value node that takes `value` and a `trigger` (a rising edge, or a count that changed) and publishes the value as it was at the last trigger, until the next. why: a director's decisions (pack size, which place, which gesture) are drawn from expressions that keep moving, and a decision must not change inside a shot; today the only thing that holds is an integer bar count (`valueCount` holds a count, `valueLag` smooths, nothing holds a READING), so every such call is "by bar number only" and cannot read the track's level at the moment the shot began. design note first with what TouchDesigner (Hold CHOP, Trigger CHOP, Logic) and Notch (the Latch / Sample and Hold modifiers) offer, then the node: its state under seek, replay and reset (§V181's rule for stateful value nodes), what it publishes before the first trigger, a vector value. the consumer writes its own test on it.|T1561b,T1591b,V181

T1614b|.|**A RUN INTO A MULTISAMPLED TARGET IS NOT BYTE-IDENTICAL TO ONE PASS PER DRAW, CAUSE UNKNOWN (§T1604b leaves such targets a pass per draw).** grouped, sentinel-bot's colour (rgba16float, 4× MSAA, 640×360) differs on 0 to 8 of 230,400 pixels a frame, each by one unit in the last place of one channel, where two mesh-instanced geometries meet (the claws and the last rings); the stock material shows it too; built scenes of up to 8,192 interpenetrating instanced meshes under three casting lights do not. suspects to test, none tested: the per-pass resolve (one pass per draw resolves after every draw, a run once), a store/load round trip of the multisampled attachment on a tile-based GPU, alpha-to-coverage. cost of leaving it: the consumer's live tier is 30 device passes instead of 25 and offline 38 instead of 25, near 1 ms of GPU live (weakly measured). wanted: a fixture that reproduces it, the cause, then group or say why not. CONSUMER DATA POINT (shaderloom-f1, in the app at 1280×720, documents back to back, twice, a loaded machine): five casting lights + 4× MSAA 26–30 fps; two casting + MSAA 34–42; two, no MSAA 45–54; one, no MSAA 52–58; no shadow, no focus, no MSAA 55–60. MSAA on this geometry was the LARGEST single cost, larger than any one shadow, so the live tier is now `antialias: "none"` with only `light_body` casting and offline keeps MSAA with everything casting. how much of that is the pass per draw this row leaves and how much is 4× raster of 645,000 triangles is not separated; the consumer re-measures MSAA when this row lands.|T1604b,T1561b

T1600b|.|**A VALUE LOOP WITH A DELAY IN IT IS LEGAL, AND A REFUSED LOOP NAMES ITS PATH (from §T1561b, shaderloom-f1).** "an integrator whose rate depends on its own output" is every speed that depends on position, and it has no stock spelling: `rate → lag → speed → expression → rate` is dropped whole by the value graph (`valueGraph.cycle`: every member emits nothing), and a `valueDelay` in the loop does not break it.
