T1681b|.|**A CAMERA'S CHANNELS ARE NOT IN THE LISTS THAT ENUMERATE VALUE BAGS (left by §T1674b).** the agent tool `get_channels` and the inspector's channel pickers list the value graph's bags, and `parameterChannels` are not in them; the Camera's description names the read and expression completion offers the names. wanted: one enumerator of what `op('x').chan` can answer, read by both. also untested: a camera inside a component read by a sibling inside it.|T1674b,T1146
T1680b|.|**A READ THAT MEANS THE OFFSET IS WARNED FOR AS LONG AS IT STANDS (left by §T1674b).** `parameter.reference.notComposed` cannot tell a read of `par.lookAt.y` that MEANS the stored offset from a mistake (sentinel-bot's `flownReachExpression` divides by a length made of the stored offsets and will keep one such read). fix when a second document needs it: a third namespace beside `par` and `chan` for "as stored", or the finding passes an expression that reads no world value of the same camera.|T1674b,T1641b
T1679b|.|**A TEXTURE PASS TAKES A CAMERA INPUT (the second form in §T1674b's row; ruled unnecessary once the channels exist).** Custom WGSL and its multi form gain a camera port; wired, the pass's uniforms carry eye, basis and field of view from the payload. waits for a second consumer: with the channels, a pass needs one expression a uniform (sentinel-bot's haze reads six).|T1674b
T1678b|.|**A PRESET THAT WRITES A VECTOR BY ITS BARE KEY, ON A NODE WHERE A CHANNEL OF THAT VECTOR HAS ITS OWN STORED KEY, WRITES A VALUE THE READ NEVER USES, AND NOTHING SAYS SO (found by shaderloom-f1 pressing sentinel-bot's `reset_camera` through the real bus, fixed there in `411c03d5`).** the gizmo writes a partly driven vector channel by channel (`lookAt.x`, never the bare key, §B219); a preset authored in a document source held `lookAt` whole; pressed after a flight, the recall left the flown `lookAt.x` standing and the camera did not come back. the benign half holds: the recall of the bare key did NOT take the expressions on `lookAt.y` and `lookAt.z` with it; the component key wins over the bare vector, as it should. Store captures the right keys; an authored preset can get it wrong silently. this is §T1641b's class (a value that is never effective): a finding on such a preset at the checked save, and the recall saying what it did not move. the same for a cue and for `control.reset` on a partly keyed vector.|T1641b,T970,B219
T1677b|.|**FINGER TO PICTURE, END TO END, IS UNMEASURED (from §T1669b).** finger to the door is 14 ms on loopback; door to document is the editor's NEXT animation frame; document to picture is the frame after: one to two app frames on top of the network, 17 to 34 ms each on the owner's file. wanted: measured with the helper, the bridge and a second machine or a camera on the real phone over the real wifi; then whether a value from the door should be written when it arrives and not at the next frame (the values lane, §T1652b, makes such a write cheap), which is half a frame of latency for every remote control.|T1669b,T1652b,T1666b
T1676b|.|**EVERY VALUE WRITTEN ECHOES THE WHOLE SNAPSHOT TO EVERY PHONE (from §T1669b).** 15 KB on the owner's file, at the rate the finger moves: about 0.9 MB a second down the wifi. the page now ignores what did not change but still receives and parses it. a values-only delta on the wire is a protocol change (phone-protocol, the door, the publisher); not measured on real wifi; measure there first. **the owner, 2026-10-06: *"1mb/s for values to phone sounds inefficient. we should probably improve that. but if its filed thats okay for now"*. so: wanted, after the pause.**|T1669b
T1675b|.|**THE PHONE PAGE'S SLIDER, FADER AND PAD STILL MOVE BY GEOMETRY (from §T1669b).** fill width, thumb left, puck left/top: 0.6 ms of layout and one small full update a move at 4x CPU in Chromium. left alone on purpose: the Touch trial (§T1647b) is live and any change there is a change of look on the phone. measure on a real phone (Safari) before doing anything.|T1669b,T1647b
T1673b|.|**A POINT OF A POINTSET CANNOT BE READ BY A PARAMETER OR BY A TEXTURE PASS, SO EVERYTHING THAT IS NOT A KERNEL SAYS AGAIN WHERE THE RIG IS (row text by shaderloom-f1, 2026-10-06; the class the owner reported on the searchlight: *"the body sway and what not is not translated to the spot light and thus it suddenly floats"*).** sentinel-bot's rig places each robot in a point kernel (weave, bank, the head's turn, lunge, drift, rearing). a second kernel reads that as Points In: the searchlights and the eyes' light do since `9db66c1f` and `af18b571`, and there the cure was one source. but five consumers are NOT kernels and still repeat the rig as expressions (`document.ts`: glow, core, followers[].at, eye, aim): the air pass's glow round the face (`wgsl_haze` eyesAt, a customWgslMulti), `light_body` and `light_follower1/2` (Single mode, they cast), `material_hall` / tower robotAt, and `camera_rig`. each stands off the body by whatever the expressions do not repeat. WANTED, DESIGN FIRST, against TouchDesigner (a CHOP from a POP or SOP point) and Notch: one of (a) a pointset's point as channels (the readback question §T970's design names for a point as a camera's parent: a frame late, or composed on the GPU); (b) a texture pass and a material binding a pointset's buffer and reading a point by index; (c) a Single-mode Light standing on one point of a pointset and still casting (§T1623b's later slices: a casting Light of a pointset). consumer: shaderloom-f1, sentinel-bot.|T1561b,T970,T1623b,T1656b
T1672b|.|**THE EDITOR QUEUES A GESTURE'S WRITES ONE BEHIND ANOTHER (seen by §T970 slice 1, unmeasured).** on a loaded machine the document trails a flight after the key comes up (seen with six specs in parallel). wanted: measured on the owner's file (how many writes a second a flight makes, how long the tail is at 30 fps), then the cure by cause: a gesture's writes coalesced to the frame, the newest winning. the same question for a slider drag and a gizmo drag; read with §T1668b.|T970,T1668b
T1670b|.|**FLY A DRIVEN RIG BY DISPLACING IT.** a camera whose Eye and Look At are all driven and whose Origin is free could be flown by writing Origin (a translation added to the rig, no orbit). it would make a file like the owner's flyable as it stands, without moving the rig's expressions. not built in §T970 slice 1: the designed road is the rig on Origin and Heading with Eye and Look At as free offsets, and two roads to one gesture need a ruling on which the button means.|T970,T1656b
T1665b|.|**ROPE: THE BEND LIMIT ON A STRAND TOO FINE FOR ITS STEP.** a resting joint gives under the strand's own weight; at 1,024 points and Update Rate 960 that is 1.5 of the hinge's yield, so its limit opens and a loop holds 0.096 m where slice 4 held 0.118 (0.15 asked); 500 points at 240 goes from 1.52 to 2.35 of the limit on the reference; 250 points is clear at both rates. wanted: a mark that tells a strand's own weight from a pose that cannot be met. measured NOT to be one: the give's size, the tension beside the joint, whether the step finished, how fast the joint turns, whether the give falls when the limit opens. (§T1663b may be the way: a softness sized to the strand.)|T1585b
T1585b|.|**A ROPE / CHAIN SOLVER NODE (from §T1583b's assessment; not started).** Notch ships Rope and Cloth Deformers and TouchDesigner has a known gap (staff: "roll your own"); neither treats rope as a user kernel with a number turned up. wanted: a Rope node over a grid-topology pointset (cols = links, rows = strands) with Notch's vocabulary — Update Rate, Min/Max Update Steps, Gravity, Damping, Stiffness, Spring Damping, Bend Stiffness, Rest Length Scale, Anchor First/Second/Last, Collision Thickness — plus Iterations (Flex). anchors pin to the incoming animated position; collision from the field texture now and from a second pointset with §T1582b. inside: distance and bend constraints by red/black passes on kernel steps (§T1583b), long-range attachment to anchors, its own `simPosition`/`prevPosition` state. cloth as a later sibling on the same solver. design doc with the TD/Notch comparison first. citations (`docs/td-notch-mechanisms-2026-10-05.md`): Notch Rope Deformer's fixed-rate steps with min/max clamps and Hard | Soft anchors; TD ships no rope (Flex in TD is fluids only and ends at RTX 40). **NOW THE CONSUMER'S FIRST NEED (owner on the tentacles, relayed 2026-10-05: "very stiff and not floppy ropey", then "flight mode still looks too stiff").** the closed-form trail (`d2b1d34a`) has no inertia: nothing lags, whips or collides. consumer case: 10 strands × 54 links, pinned at the socket always and at the claw while it holds, colliding with a bore. kernel steps (§T1583b) and strips (§T1586b) are on main. DESIGN IN PROGRESS. **DESIGN LANDED `559efc51` (`docs/rope-solver-design-2026-10-05.md`), RULED BY THE LEAD as recommended, pending the consumer's review.** D1 THE METHOD IS NOT THE ROW'S SKETCH: red/black relaxation on kernel steps leaves the worst segment 51% long at 16 dispatches a frame on the consumer's motion (31% with long-range attachments — which are also patented, US 9,070,220 B2 — and follow-the-leader keeps length but gains energy, tip 88 m/s against 41). chosen: XPBD in small steps with each strand's stretch constraints solved TOGETHER — the system XPBD relaxes one constraint at a time is tridiagonal on a chain, and one GPU thread per strand solves it exactly in a walk like Curve Frames' (Han & Harada 2013, Goldenthal 2007): worst segment 0.012% at 16, 8 and 4 dispatches; exact when hanging; momentum-conserving. its one limit: a step shorter than a transverse wave's crossing of one segment (54 links: 2 substeps at 1 g, 12 at 55 g), with Notch's Max Stretch as a positions-only guard past it. figures from a float64 CPU model written for the design (`scratchpad/rope-model/`), nothing measured on a device yet. NODE `pointRope` ("Rope", kind `rope`): strips in, the same strips out, `position` replaced, `velocity` published; Notch's vocabulary (Update Rate 240, Min/Max Update Steps 1/16, Iterations 4, Gravity, Damping, Force, Mass, Rest Length Scale, Stretch as a compliance, Max Stretch 2%, Bend, Collision Thickness, Friction); anchors First / Second / Last as weights 0–1 with Map mode plus a per-point pin attribute, each pinning to the INCOMING point interpolated across the frame's steps (a 3 s quintic grab moves a claw 46.8 mm a frame; a stepped weight would move it 4,172 mm — the pop); two anchors out of reach: the earlier holds; Teleport Distance with Carry or Reset; time by Notch's rule `steps = clamp(round(delta × rate), min, max)`, no accumulator; collision with a floor, a second pointset (spheres, capsule chains, Inside for a tube), a height field, a WGSL distance function. its own shader module, one dispatch per update step on the kernel-steps region. D3 needs two small changes in `compiler/substeps.ts` (a rate form on the steps declaration; one unstepped dispatch beside the stepped one). slices: 1 strand and time, 2 anchors, 3 colliders, 4 bend, 5 distance function, 6 height field; follow-ups R1–R17 (long strands, cloth, self and strand-strand collision, twist, pre-roll). FOUND: sentinel-bot's world jumps 960 m once a lap (`speed_travel` loops), which any stateful rope will see — Teleport Carry is exact for it. **CONSUMER'S REVIEW (shaderloom-f1, 2026-10-06): NO OBJECTION to the method or the rulings; one requirement and an order.** (R1, REQUIRED) A BEND LIMIT: its rings are rigid pieces at a 0.06 m pitch (shell radius 0.049 m on a 0.036 m spine) and intersect once a joint turns past about 0.4 rad; its rig test holds every bend to a radius of 0.15 m or more. Bend Stiffness 0 lets a slack chain fold flat (a slack loop's bottom, the socket when the claw is close, a tail piled on the deck), and a spring toward straight gives no bound. wanted: a LIMIT, "no joint turns more than this angle" (a minimum bend radius), as a guard after the solve like Max Stretch, with Bend Stiffness as the soft part under it; test: 54 links, both ends pinned 0.5 m apart, 3.2 m of rope, the largest turn at any joint. goes with slice 4. (R2) SLICE ORDER for this consumer: 1, 2, 4 (with the limit), 5, then 3 (the body capsule); 6 never. (R3) slice 2 must measure a FAST MOVING PIN at weight 1: the claw's target crosses rung to rung at about 4 m/s every stride and about 8 m/s in the attack. (R4) TWO COLLISION SOURCES AT ONCE: the bore as a WGSL distance function with the deck in it AND the robot's body as one capsule (about 1.7 m by 0.45 m) from a colliders pointset; the doc must say one node takes both. no strand-strand in v1. (R5) A WINCH: `segmentLength` mapped on the first segments, changing about 1 m/s (the reach runs 1.5 m to 3.5 m a stride); measure paying out and reeling in before the description promises it. (R6) a FRACTIONAL weight under Hard must be a blend toward the target (a perched tentacle feeling about at 0.3–0.5), else Anchor Mode has to be mappable per strand. (R7) Teleport Distance 100 with Carry for the 960 m lap, as a test. (R8) HARNESS: step a document N frames headless and read the rope's points EVERY frame (`renderHeadless` with `probeBuffers` gives the last frame only, as far as the consumer knows). all eight sent to the rope worker, to fold into the doc before slice 4. **SLICE 1 LANDED `33e9e6ef` (one squash; verified on main: typecheck, `rope.test`, `point-rope.test`, `kernel-steps.test`, `substeps.test`, `animate-parameters.test` 101; on Dawn `point-rope`, `rope-steps`, `harness-probe-frames` and both `kernel-steps` files 54; the 26 catalogue walkers 444; the worker ran 22 named files 563, the gates 3547, the build).** `pointRope` ("Rope", kind `rope`): strips in, strips out, `position` and `velocity`; Update Rate, Min/Max Update Steps, Iterations, Simulation Speed, Gravity, Damping, Mass, Rest Length Scale, Stretch, Max Stretch, Anchor First, Reset, Teleport Distance, Teleport (Carry | Reset). `src/points/rope.ts` is the CPU reference in single precision and the oracle; `rope.wgsl.ts` is the same step operation for operation, one invocation a strand. BIT-EXACTNESS SURVIVED THE DEVICE everywhere the design claimed it; device against reference in general motion 1.04e-5 m after 640 steps on a 1 m strand. HARNESS: `probeFrames` on `renderHeadless` gives `bufferFrames`, a buffer read at EVERY frame (the consumer's ask, R8). AS BUILT DIFFERS FROM THE DESIGN (doc section 14.1), RULED AS BUILT: the step COUNT is derived by the BACKEND from each frame's own delta (`rateSubsteps`, `plan.ts`; a `loopRates` map and five lines in `render()`), not by the compiler — the structural compile has no frame and a host rendering a static document never compiles again (D23); the step is two loops, not three to five (the four-loop version measured 3–4× Curve Frames, the design's stop condition, so it was restructured); rest lengths and the anchor's history live in a separate `kept` buffer (128 B a point); Carry is dead reckoning on a kept anchor speed; drag is `v ÷ (1 + damping·h)`; the seed is THE INCOMING POINTS AS THEY ARE, slot for slot — the node builds no pose and holds no reference axis, so there is no hand to choose (the consumer's flip finding; tested over 256 directions on the reference and 128 strands on Dawn). MEASURED (Dawn on Metal, wall ms per step less the same graph without the node; the machine was shared, small layouts ±2×; taken BEFORE §B260's reference-pass rule): one 55-point strand 0.03–0.05 ms against Curve Frames' 0.03 (D1 stands); the consumer's 10 × 55: 0.35 ms a frame at 4 steps, 1.2 ms at 16; 400 × 250: 0.38–0.40 a step; 98 × 1,024: 1.41–1.43; 18,181 × 55 (a million points): 1.43–1.50 against 0.44 for a plain kernel — many short strands are throughput-bound (§T1637b). the design's ranges were LOW for long strands by 1.5–3×. a step past the step limit runs all four Newton steps and costs 4×. fast pin on the reference: 4 m/s 0.017% at 2 steps; 8 m/s 21% at 2 steps, 0.013% at 4, so the default Update Rate 240 holds the attack. FOUND BY A TEST: the backend writes `iterations`, `substep`, `seed` and others BY NAME into any member of a stepped dispatch's uniform block; the Rope's Newton cap was called `iterations` and read 1 always (renamed `solves`); every other node is unguarded (§T1636b). **SECTION 15 OF THE DOC (after the consumer's review; model only, not built), RULED BY THE LEAD D16–D23, the consumer to confirm D17 and D21:** D16 THE BEND LIMIT IS A CONSTRAINT IN THE SOLVE, one-sided rows between second neighbours in a banded system with the stretch rows — a positions-only guard like Max Stretch TEARS the strand on the consumer's own rest test (1,400% stretch, 210 m/s: gravity keeps pushing into the limit and the velocity never learns); no limit reads 50.5° (2.22× the limit), a Gauss–Seidel sweep 1.06–1.10×, the banded solve 1.001× at rest and 1.003–1.065× moving at 4–8 m/s with Iterations 8. D17 its parameter is Min Bend Radius in metres behind a structural switch, Iterations defaulting to 8 while on. D18 slices 1, 2, 4, 5, 3; no 6. D19 an anchor's stiffness is scaled by the STRAND's mass (by the point's own, a 55-point strand hangs 3.4 m below a half-weighted anchor; by the strand's, 62 mm at 0.5). D20 Anchor Mode stays one parameter; a fractional Hard weight is a blend. D21 THE WINCH IS `lengthOut` WITH PARKED POINTS and Segment Length is read at seeding only — the promise that Segment Length could be mapped every frame is WITHDRAWN (driven toward zero the step limit `√(m·l ÷ T)` goes to zero with it: a still strand is thrown 1.4 m at 4 m/s). D22 collision sources act together in the order colliders, field, floor, distance function, the last exact; one node takes all. D23 as above. not verified: the bend limit and the winch on a device, their cost, a strand seeded short between two pins. slice 2 (anchors, the second pin, the fast-pin measurement) NEXT. **THE CONSUMER CONFIRMS (shaderloom-f1, 2026-10-06):** D16 agreed; D17 Min Bend Radius in metres confirmed (its rig test holds every bend wider than 0.15 m); D21 `lengthOut` with parked points confirmed — it is the shape the rig has today (the rings nearest the body stowed at the socket, the claw always out; its Geometry already groups on a kind attribute, so a Group on `live` is a rename). TWO THINGS IT RELIES ON, to be held by tests in the winch slice: (1) a point keeps its IDENTITY whatever the length — ring k is always ring k (lit segments, the meter and the chase are indexed by ring and must not slide along the strand as it winds); (2) the parked end is the ANCHOR FIRST end and the last point is the free or second-pinned one. D18–D20, D22 no objection. the walk's legs wait on slice 2 — IN BUILD. **SLICE 2 LANDED `c8ef9905` (one squash; verified on main beside the buffer seam: typecheck; `rope.test`, `point-rope.test`, `kernel-steps`, the V1029 gate, `buffer-write.test` 140; on Dawn `point-rope-anchors`, `point-rope`, `rope-anchors`, `rope-steps`, `buffer-write` 52; the 26 catalogue walkers 444; the worker ran the gates on its merged tree, 58 files / 3,574, and the build).** Anchor Second, Anchor Last, Map mode on all three (a mapped weight replaces the parameter, read at the strand's own station), Anchor Mode (Hard | Soft), Anchor Strength, Anchor Damping, Pin Attribute (a weight on every point), the reach rule (the earlier pin holds), softened pivots with two or more stations, D19 and D20 as ruled, and Segment Length as a number (unasked; the consumer's seed pose has its last point already at the claw's target). NO ENGINE FILE TOUCHED. a sheeted grid input works as N strips (rows × sheets). THE FAST FAR PIN ON DAWN (60 fps, per frame through `probeFrames`, 54 segments, the target on a rung 70% and crossing 2 m in 30%): 4 m/s at 4 steps a frame worst segment 0.0072%, held points on target to the bit; 8 m/s at 4 steps 0.0125%; 8 m/s at ONE step 177% on the last segment; 8 m/s at 2 steps 0.0125%; 16 m/s at 4 steps 0.0130%. so THE ATTACK NEEDS MIN UPDATE STEPS 2, and Update Rate 240 (4 steps) holds 16 m/s. D19 closed form on the consumer's 55 points: 62.12 mm at weight 0.5, 144.95 mm at 0.3, on the reference and on Dawn. feeling about: the tip trails its target by 23–44 mm at 0.3, 10–22 mm at 0.5. Teleport 100 with Carry over 960 m with both pins: pins exact on every frame, interior within 2⁻¹⁴ m. COST, BY THE REFERENCE-PASS RULE (span ÷ reference, five variants alive in one process, visited in turn): one 55-point strand's calm step is 0.83 of Curve Frames' two walks (D11 stands, re-taken); anchors at the three stations cost nothing measurable, mapped or not; a PIN ATTRIBUTE DOUBLES A STEP (every point follows its target every frame); 250-point strands are 2.1× Curve Frames. Metal refused more than about 30 timer query sets in one process. WHAT THE DEVICE CHANGED: the hanging strand is no longer bit-exact on Dawn at 4 and 8 steps — the same arithmetic in a larger program reads 128.00009 N for 128, one last place of a square root, Metal's fast math again (§B260); that one test uses the design's fallback tolerance, the reference stays exact, and every pin, fall, tow, lap and seed is still exact on Dawn. RULED BY THE LEAD (doc 16.10): D24 THE STRETCH GUARD FAILS WITH A FAR PIN past the step limit (it holds every segment but the one before the far pin, which takes everything: the 177% above) — between two hard pins it walks back from the later pin and then out from the earlier; BUILD IT with slice 4. D25 a target's history is kept at any weight (without it a weight rising from 0 kicks the tip at 46 m/s; with it 2.1): as built. D26 a teleport is judged on the first point's incoming position: as built. D27 Segment Length as a number: stays. D28 a Pin Attribute follows every point every frame and costs a step twice: as built, said in its description. D29 a strand seeded short EXACTLY along gravity stays straight while its neighbours at 1.8° fall into a loop: left as it is, NO HAND, said in Segment Length's and Rest Length Scale's descriptions. for the winch: both of the consumer's reliances hold as built (point k is slot k; the parked end is the Anchor First end); open there: Anchor Second reads the second SLOT, which will be parked, so the leave direction must be held on the first live segment. slice 4 (the bend limit in the solve, Min Bend Radius, with D24's guard) NEXT. **THE FIRST CONSUMER IS ON MAIN (shaderloom-f1, `697f33f7`, behind a panel switch that ships off): 30 strands of 54 through Topology (Strips) → `rope_legs` → Curve Frames (Seed: Orient Attribute) → the ring and claw draws; measured frame by frame on Dawn through `probeFrames` with the robot travelling at 3.2 m/s.** HELD: length 0.014% at worst over twelve seconds of walking with hand-overs; Anchor First exact every frame; a claw at Anchor Last weight 1 exact; Reset to the bit; a swimming tentacle drawn to the rig's shape by Pin Attribute at 0.4 with the last 16 rings free, 8° between rings at the sharpest. DID NOT HOLD — THE CASES SLICE 4 IS HELD AGAINST: (1) A STRAND HELD AT BOTH ENDS WITH SLACK FOLDS FLAT (socket to rung 2.3 m, strand 3.18 m, all three anchors at 1, gravity 1.5): 2,576 of 109,200 joints turned more than 40°, up to 179°, HALF OF THEM AT RING 1 right after Anchor Second where the leave direction and the chord disagree, the rest in the last fifteen rings — so a tentacle on a rung is not rope in the consumer's file today, every ring is pinned to the rig's arc; (2) a PARTIAL Anchor Last kinks the end, 60–90° between the last three rings for a third of the frames (the pull is on one point and nothing spreads it); (3) a strand drawn by Pin Attribute to a curve 2.5% shorter than itself buckles (31° at weight 0.95); (4) for the winch: a hand-over with wound-in rings parked on the socket tore (30% long) and folded (167°). THREE THINGS ABOUT THE ROPE, sent to the worker for slice 4: (a) a Pin Attribute at exactly 1 trails its target by up to 3.5 mm while an Anchor at 1 is exact — a weight of 1 under Hard is to be a hard pin wherever it comes from, or the worker says why not; (b) Anchor Second's description must say the earlier pin holds; (c) a mapped weight a rounding short of 1 is a stiff pull, not a pin — a tolerance at the top. cost in the app not measured yet. consumer's in-app figures (same method, one clean visit each): the rope's chain built and held off about 0.1 ms; running (30 strands of 54, 2–8 steps, Iterations 8, Pin Attribute on) about 0.5 ms. **SLICE 4 STOPPED BY ITS OWN STOP CONDITION AND RULED (2026-10-06; work in progress on the worker's branch: D24's guard, the bend limit behind its switch, the weight fixes).** THE BEND LIMIT AS FIRST BUILT (a raised diagonal as its softening) cost 3.30× on 400 × 250 at rest (1.34× on the consumer's 10 × 55) — a banded Newton step is 1.35–1.45× a tridiagonal one and the rest is the Newton COUNT: a resting bend's multipliers are a smooth mode whose share of the diagonal falls with the fourth power of the joints at the limit together, so a 250-point loop never converged (8 steps, the Iterations cap, against 4 unlimited) — AND IT COULD THROW THE ROPE: at 8 m/s the worst turn 1.655× the limit on Dawn, stretch at the 2% guard, on the reference a point moving 0.78 m in a frame (where the rows cannot all be met a raised diagonal has no fixed point). D30 RULED (B): THE SOFTENING IS A TRUE COMPLIANCE, 2^-10 on the diagonal with its multiplier on the right-hand side, as the stretch rows carry Stretch — measured by the reference-pass rule 1.12–1.25× on 10 × 55 and 1.81× on 400 × 250 at rest; the consumer's loop at rest 1.0001× the limit with 5 joints at it; a 250-point loop 1.030×; swept at 4 m/s at Update Rate 240 1.146×, at 960 1.004×; at 8 m/s at 240 1.155× with stretch 0.12% and NO guard hit in any run. the limit is therefore met at rest and exceeded in fast motion by a stated margin: an author whose geometry breaks at the limit sets the radius with that margin or raises the Update Rate. DEVICE RESULTS as first built (54 links, pins 0.5 m apart, R 0.15 m, limit 23.07°): off 2.188× the limit, on 1.0001×; the active rows' switching at rest does not show (3.7 µm a frame against 4.5 with no limit). THE CONSUMER'S CASES ON THE REFERENCE: case 1 (held at both ends with slack) off 82–137° at joint 1, ON 23.1° at joints 1–6 — THE LIMIT HOLDS AT RING 1, across a pinned pair the row is still there and the strand leaves inside a cone about the socket's direction; case 2 (a partial Anchor Last) off 46–145°, on 23.1° everywhere, the end not kinked in any frame (with the limit on a station's pull need not be spread; a direction at the end is the Pin Attribute's job); case 3 (pinned to a curve 2.5% shorter) on 23.2°, finite, and THE PINS GIVE (55 mm against 20). T950|.|**§T942's BRIDGE PLAN — 8 GAPS FOUND BY §T947, & 3 ARE SAFETY ∴ ⊥ DEFERRABLE.** (1) ⊥ STREAMING message shape — the protocol union is request/response w/ a numeric id, **⊥ server-push, ⊥ subscription**; (2) ⊥ BACKPRESSURE — Ether Dream is a CREDIT system (`buffer_fullness` ∈ every status, NAK-Full on overflow) & nothing ∈ the model has a shape for a device pushing back; **(3) ⊥ DEAD-MAN/WATCHDOG concept**; **(4) ⊥ LIFECYCLE for an ARMED, EXCLUSIVE, STATEFUL resource — & Ether Dream itself allows only ONE host, which composes awkwardly w/ the bridge's own one-page rule: 2 exclusivity claims needing 1 story**; **(5) ⊥ SIDE-EFFECT story for offline/headless**; (6) ⊥ DATAGRAM semantics — for IDN/LaserCube the helper can report *sent*, never *arrived*, & request/response framing IMPLIES a reliability UDP lacks; (7) **WebUSB is ⊥ ∈ the ranked list despite being the ONLY helper-free output path**; **(8) ⚑THE CHANNEL SEAM DOES ⊥ FIT — `channels?: (name) => number` is SCALARS & `laserOut` consumes a POINTSET ∴ THIS IS THE FIRST I/O CONSUMER THAT FALSIFIES *one seam for all I/O***, & the seam it DOES fit (the readback budget, §V185) is ⊥ mentioned. ⚠the plan was mid-write & ends @ §2 w/ §§3–11 referenced but absent ∴ re-check each against the finished doc|V185,T942,T947 ⟶ **FIRST 2 COMMITS ∈ (peer). (1) protocol core, EMULATOR-GATED: `ether-dream.ts` (codec + client state machine) + `ether-dream-emulator.ts` — THE DAC'S OWN STATE MACHINES, ⊥ A MOCK (real playback/light-engine/buffer state, full status on every response, incremental TCP chunk parse, a LATCHED e-stop that refuses to clear w/ NAK `!`). 15 gates: hand-laid byte vectors for the 18-byte point struct, 7 client-vs-emulator CONVERSATIONS (credit streaming that never trips NAK-Full, in-flight accounting, device refusal on overflow, drain/underflow, out-of-sequence NAKs, the e-stop latch/refuse/clear arc, chunk splitting). **the credit model NEEDS NO CLOCK & that is its correctness argument.** (2) `laserOut` + its pump — & §T1005 FORCED EXACTLY WHAT IT WAS BUILT TO FORCE: `emits` required the pump row & the refusal call ∈ ONE commit. **⊥ `armed` PARAMETER EXISTS (G1: arming is NEVER document state); host empty = ⊥ device ever; the pump derives its types from `EMISSION_PUMPS` (§T1006 honoured from line one), consults `emissionRefusal`, & CONSTRUCTS NO SENDER — one mechanism on every path (§V840), held by a test reading the stripped source.** ledger rows carry arguments (§V841): the reproducibility row explains why *safe to run headless* is RIGHT ABOUT PIXELS & WRONG ABOUT LIGHT. shipped state = a transport that CANNOT FIRE, saying so per node|V840,V841,T949,T1005,T1006 ⟶ **COMMIT 3: the helper-side laser service ∴ ALL 3 NON-DEFERRABLE SAFETY GAPS NOW HAVE MECHANISMS.** **G2 DEAD-MAN**: injected clock, helper-side, fires the protocol module's FIXED sequence (darkness @ last position → Stop → E-Stop) when blocks stop arriving FOR ANY REASON — **the service decides WHEN, never WHAT**;
