V966|⚑⚑**A *COUNT* IS 1 FOR EXACTLY ONE FRAME ∴ ANYTHING IT DRIVES STEPS ∈ ONE FRAME — A BLINK BY CONSTRUCTION, WHATEVER IT IS ATTACHED TO. GAIN & DECAY SHAPE THE *RELEASE*; NEITHER TOUCHES THE *ATTACK*.** measured (§T1301, E57 frames 60–180, WORST SINGLE-FRAME STEP ∈ mean luma — **& the choice of instrument is half the finding: PEAK-TO-PEAK CANNOT TELL A SWELL FROM A STROBE, same travel, different time**): shipped worst step 11.40 (18.4 %); **moon frozen — worst step LARGER**; beat off the moon — 17.57 (25.9 %), i.e. **WORSE**; all three lanes frozen 1.82 (2.7 %) ∴ the lanes are the whole of it; **band ENVELOPES instead of counts — 2.72 (4.3 %), a 4.2× smaller worst step, & IT STILL LANDS.** ⚑**THE MOON DIP & THE SHAFT FLASH WERE PARTLY *CANCELLING*: shafts on `snareCount` is an 18-unit INSTANTANEOUS JUMP UP (67.97 → 85.95 ∈ one frame), LARGER than the moon's 12-unit drop ∴ REMOVING ONE OF TWO OPPOSED STEPS LEAVES THE BIGGER STEP NAKED** — which is why \"take the beat off the primary light\" (the orchestrator's recommendation) MEASURED WORSE THAN THE DEFECT. **THE FIX IS THE SIGNAL, ⊥ THE TARGET: use `kick`/`snare`/`onset` — the band ENVELOPES, the SAME EVENTS carrying the transient's OWN rise & fall.** ⚠**& A `valueLag` ON A COUNT IS ⊥ THE ANSWER: a count is 1 for one FRAME while lag is ∈ SECONDS ∴ the peak the lag reaches is FRAME-RATE DEPENDENT & the piece would land differently @ 30 & 60 fps.** COROLLARY, & d0 said it against its own work: **§T1304c's two-number blink fix (gain 1.5 → 0.7, decay 250 → 420 ms) was INCOMPLETE — it sufficed on E68 only because those lanes move a SMALL SHARE OF THE PIXELS; on E57 they move the WHOLE FRAME.** a release-shaped fix hides an attack-shaped defect exactly as long as the defect is small|T1301,T1304c,T1279,T1234,V903,V147
V967|⚑⚑**DO ⊥ FRAME AN *ART-DIRECTION* CHOICE AS A *COST* CHOICE — & ⊥ W/ NUMBERS NOBODY MEASURED.** §T1310b: the orchestrator put three E70 directions to the owner w/ an ms ESTIMATE attached to each as the headline discriminator. the owner's answer: *"stop tripping about costs. you did that last time and it turned out to be totally unnecessary since we had plenty of budget. i did not tell you to judge all my example requests at your wild and often wrongly estimated performance budget caps."* **THEY ARE RIGHT & IT IS A REPEAT: §V963 EXISTS BECAUSE THE SAME THING HAPPENED ON §T1283 — an unmeasured 25–35 ms estimate chose a direction, set a ceiling, designed an abort & asked the owner to accept a price, & THE PIECE SHIPPED @ 4.76 ms. the orchestrator then did it AGAIN ∈ the NEXT ROW, after the owner had ALREADY said \"go all out\".** ⇒ **V963 was ⊥ enough because it said MEASURE BEFORE QUOTING; the missing half is WHERE A NUMBER BELONGS @ ALL.** THE RULE: **a LOOK question is answered w/ LOOKS — what the thing IS, what it reads as, what it resembles. cost is an ENGINEERING constraint & belongs ∈ the BUILD, ⊥ ∈ the CHOICE — & it belongs there as a MEASUREMENT taken per stage, which is what the staged discipline is FOR.** ⚠**& NOTE THE ESTIMATES WERE WRONG ∈ THE *PESSIMISTIC* DIRECTION BOTH TIMES: the damage is ⊥ overspending, it is TALKING THE OWNER OUT OF AN AFFORDABLE IDEA.** a guess presented beside a real choice is an ARGUMENT, ⊥ information — & the owner has ⊥ asked for a budget cap on ANY example request|V963,T1310b,T1283,T1304b
V968|⚑⚑**A NULL RESULT FROM A DETECTOR YOU HAVE ⊥ VALIDATED AGAINST A KNOWN POSITIVE IS ⊥ A NULL RESULT.** measured (§T1306c): a bisect hunting E68's blown-white artefact reported **0.00 % for EVERY ARM INCLUDING THE UNMODIFIED ONE** — because the \"blown\" threshold was 245 & the offending pixels measure **(237, 233, 243)**. **THE INSTRUMENT COULD ⊥ SEE THE DEFECT ∴ IT REPORTED THAT NOTHING CAUSED IT, & the author nearly concluded THE ARTEFACT WAS GONE.** a detector that returns zero on the POSITIVE CONTROL returns zero on everything, & every arm then looks exonerated. **THE RULE: BEFORE TRUSTING ANY PASS/FAIL MEASUREMENT, RUN IT AGAINST A CASE YOU KNOW IS POSITIVE & CONFIRM IT FIRES.** ⚑**SECOND TRAP ∈ THE SAME BISECT & IT IS A DIFFERENT LESSON: AN ARM CAN FAIL TO ISOLATE WHAT ITS *NAME* SAYS.** `keyIntensity = 0` ALSO read 0.00 % & looked like a SECOND INDEPENDENT CAUSE — it was ⊥: **that parameter scales the BACKDROP as well as the surface term ∴ the arm was never isolating what it claimed to.** ⇒ an arm ! remove ONE idea & ⊥ two; check what a knob ACTUALLY multiplies before attributing a result to it. **COMPANION TO §V964** (a statistic through the WRONG WINDOW gives a plausible wrong answer) & §V959 (a red-verify that does ⊥ go red means THE EDIT DID ⊥ REACH THE CODE) — three members of one family now: **THE MEASUREMENT APPARATUS IS AS FALSIFIABLE AS THE THING IT MEASURES, & ⊥ ONE OF THE THREE WAS CAUGHT BY A GATE**|T1306c,V964,V959,V147 ⚑**CONFIRMED INDEPENDENTLY BY THE AUTHOR OF THE BISECT (§T1306c, reported again 2026-09-12): the blown-pixel threshold was 245 & the pixels measure 237 ∴ EVERY ARM INCLUDING THE UNMODIFIED ONE READ 0.00 %. "validate the detector against a known positive before trusting a null result" is now stated by BOTH the session that hit it & the one that recorded it**
V969|⚑**A DISTANCE ESTIMATOR IS A *PAIR* — THE MAP & ITS DERIVATIVE — & CHANGING ONE W/O THE OTHER PRODUCES *A PICTURE*, ⊥ AN ERROR.** §T1310b: E70's affine step ran `p = p*scale + juliaC` (a JULIA iteration: adds a CONSTANT) beside `dr = dr*abs(scale) + 1.0` (**the MANDELBOX derivative, which assumes the added term differentiates to 1 w.r.t. the ray's START; a CONSTANT differentiates to 0**) ∴ `dr` ran systematically LARGE & the estimate systematically SMALL — **conservative rather than dangerous, so it did ⊥ crash ∨ artefact, IT JUST CREPT**; & the set itself was ⊥ there (a Mandelbox-Julia @ that scale is A THIN DUST: **86.1 % of the frame near-black, mean luma 7.53, a scatter of specks & no object**). **NEITHER HALF RAISES AN ERROR ANYWHERE: a wrong derivative is a SLOW MARCH & a wrong map is A DIFFERENT SHAPE, & both look like \"the art direction is ⊥ working yet\".** THE RULE: **when either half of a DE changes, CHANGE BOTH & SAY WHICH DERIVATIVE FORM THE MAP EARNS** — & prefer a form whose derivative is EXACT (the true Mandelbox's `+1` is exact for the ray's own start plus a drifting offset, which is why E70 ships that rather than the Julia constant it was designed around, & the topology-evolution axis survives)|T1310b,V147,V968
V970|⚑**THE SHADER IS EMBEDDED ∈ THE `.loom.json` ∴ EDITING THE `.ts` & RE-RUNNING A PROBE RENDERS *STALE WGSL*. `--only <E>` AFTER EVERY SHADER EDIT, ∨ THE ARM IS A LIE.** measured (§T1310b): THREE arms were run against the OLD shader before an IMPOSSIBLE result surfaced it — **`detail: 6`, a SIX-FOLD change to every ray's stopping point, returned a mean IDENTICAL to `detail: 1`.** that is §V968's shape w/ a different cause: the instrument could ⊥ see the change ∴ it reported that nothing caused it, & three measurements were silently measuring a file nobody had edited. ⚑**THE TELL IS AN *IMPOSSIBLE* RESULT, ⊥ A WRONG ONE: a plausible-but-wrong number would have been believed & shipped.** & note the generated JSON is the RENDERED artefact for EVERY probe, gate & claim — so this applies to anything that reads a document rather than a source|T1310b,V968,B197,T1267
V971|⚑**ON A SHARED WORKING TREE, ONE SESSION'S MID-EDIT STATE REDDENS EVERY OTHER SESSION'S LADDER STEP — & THE READER CANNOT TELL A TRANSIENT FROM A REAL BREAK.** measured (§T1312b): the §T1310b agent ran `pnpm typecheck` & correctly saw `use-audio-input.ts:254 — ParameterValue not imported`, reported it as a red @ HEAD, & the orchestrator RELAYED IT AS SUCH. it had NEVER REACHED A COMMIT: 72 added `syncLeadOf` & its import ~2 MINUTES APART, & the window between the two edits is what the other session typechecked. **VERIFIED AFTERWARDS BY BOTH: `git show HEAD:<file>` carries the import, `syncLeadOf` is @ line 255 ⊥ 254, & `pnpm typecheck` exits 0.** ⇒ **THE FIX IS A HABIT ON THE *REPORTER*, ⊥ A RESTRICTION ON THE EDITOR — nobody should stop editing: (a) ATTRIBUTE A LADDER RED TO *HEAD* BEFORE REPORTING IT — `git show HEAD:<file>` ∨ simply RE-RUN AFTER A BEAT; (b) TREAT A RED ∈ A FILE YOU DO ⊥ OWN AS *SUSPECT-UNTIL-RE-RUN*.** the line number is itself a tell: a stale reading is often OFF BY A LINE from the committed file. **SAME \"WHOSE RED IS THIS?\" TAX AS §B201/§B203 FROM A DIFFERENT CAUSE — there the red was real & uncommitted; here it was real & TRANSIENT. both cost every other session the same attribution work, & the orchestrator paid it forward by relaying without checking**|T1312b,T1310b,B201,B203

A HUE SPRAYED OVER GEOMETRY THAT ALREADY HAS A COLOUR IS A *TINT*; A HUE CARRIED BY AN OBJECT THE EYE CAN POINT AT IS A SECOND LIGHT.** measured across SIX passes of §T1304b/§T1306b/§T1309c: every attempt put the second colour on a LIGHT — a warm rake, a daylight shaft, the vein junctions — & **every one was invisible ∨ read as a wash; the rake measured on the rubble @ (70, 42, 57), blue over green, A MAUVE SLAB OF PAINTED STONE.** what fixed it ∈ ONE pass, after six tuning passes could ⊥: **A HASH PER COLUMN — the hue belongs to a THING, & the thing is what the eye resolves.** ⇒ when a frame reads as one hue family & the brief asks for contrast, **do ⊥ reach for another light; find ⊥ ∨ make an OBJECT to carry the second hue.** companion: §T1304c's finding that a warm wash W/ NO SOURCE ∈ FRAME cannot read as light — same failure from the other side (a light w/o a source, & a colour w/o an owner)|T1304b,T1306b,T1309c,T1304c
V973|⚑**\"THE VOLUME WANTS A *SMOOTHER* FIELD THAN THE SURFACE\" & \"THE VOLUME WANTS A *DIFFERENT* FIELD FROM THE SURFACE\" ARE ⊥ THE SAME REQUIREMENT — & §V962 WAS WRITTEN AS THE FIRST & IMPLEMENTED AS THE SECOND.** measured (§T1309c): E68's dust sampled a `(row, bay)` hash **that knows NOTHING about where a vein is** ∴ the hall carried TWO UNRELATED PATTERNS, & the owner's *\"⊥ shining out of the stone… cheaply slapped on, sprite like\"* WAS LITERALLY TRUE — the light ∈ the air & the light on the stone were ⊥ the same light. **the old docblock ARGUED the correct thing (a volume wants a smoother field, because sparse samples through a near-binary field are a SPECKLE GENERATOR) & THEN TOOK A DIFFERENT FIELD, & the author DOCUMENTED THAT AS A FEATURE.** ⇒ **SMOOTHER = THE SAME FIELD @ A COARSER SCALE. IoU against the 512 reference DOES see it (0.837 @ 256, 0.163 @ 128) ∵ it is a PER-PIXEL agreement, ⊥ an aggregate. ∴ **§T1024's `<name>:coverage` separates *ran & found nothing* from *did ⊥ run* — which is what it was built for — & ⊥ANYTHING about whether the matte is GOOD.** ⚑the general form, & it is §V854's family from the other side: **an aggregate answers *how much*, never *where* — & every quality question about a mask, a segmentation, a depth map ∨ a point set is a WHERE question.** ∴ ⊥ let a scalar published for a LIVENESS claim be read as a QUALITY claim; if quality ! be gated, gate it per-pixel against a reference|V838,V842,V854,V856,T1024,T1044 ⚑**CONFIRMED AGAIN & BACKWARDS, §T1040: @ RVM ratio 0.25 THE PICTURE BREAKS WHILE **COVERAGE RISES** (0.199 vs ratio 0.5's 0.164) — the extra *coverage* IS BACKGROUND SPECKLE.** ∴ the aggregate moved in the GOOD direction while quality collapsed, which is §V839's sign-error & §V864's blindness ARRIVING TOGETHER — & it is why a coverage floor would have PASSED the worse setting
V859|**SEGMENT A DOWNSCALED COPY — A MODEL THAT WORKS @ A FIXED INTERNAL SIZE UPSAMPLES ITS OWN OUTPUT, SO A BIGGER INPUT BUYS ⊥ DETAIL & COSTS A BIGGER READBACK.** muse's `env.ts:62-70`, verbatim: *MediaPipe's selfie segmenter works @ 256x256 internally & then UPSAMPLES its mask to whatever input size it was given — so handing it a 1080p frame buys ⊥ detail & costs a 1080p mask readback every time. Segmenting a downscaled copy cuts that cost QUADRATICALLY w/ ⊥ loss of information the model ever had.* measured @ `inputScale01 = 0.35` (252×448 of 720×1280) = **8× less readback, ⊥ information lost** — & the full-frame figure they avoided is **3.5 MB, almost exactly ours**. ∴ ! know the model's INTERNAL size & feed it that, ⊥ the display size. ⚑corollary from the same repo, measured & counter-intuitive: **their research doc said *always use the GPU delegate* & THE MEASUREMENT OVERRULED IT** — MediaPipe's GPU mask is a `WebGLTexture` ∈ MediaPipe's own GL context, unreadable from a WebGPU renderer (peak sample **0** across a 720×1280 frame) ∴ they deliberately request the CPU delegate & treat a GPU mask as a LOUD FAILURE|V838,V849,T1039,T976
V860|⚑**DELAY THE COLOUR, DON'T SMEAR THE MATTE — the right fix for a late mask, & it is ⊥ an EMA.** muse's `colorDelay.ts` keeps a RING OF COLOUR FRAMES & composites **the frame the mask was ACTUALLY COMPUTED FROM**, chosen by `bundleTimestamp − maskTimestamp` measured PER FRAME rather than a constant (default 8 frames ≈ 133 ms @ 60 fps); when the mask is older than the ring reaches it reports `clipped` & `residualMs` **rather than quietly compositing a mismatch**. their header states the problem exactly: *the silhouette lags the body — it eats into arms exactly when they move, which is when anyone is looking*. ∴ an EMA HIDES the lag by blurring 2 wrong answers together; a delay line MAKES THE ANSWER RIGHT by pairing mask & frame. ⚠ **BUT IT ONLY BECOMES AVAILABLE ONCE INFERENCE IS FAST: @ 24 Hz their mask is ~42 ms old & a 133 ms ring covers it; OURS IS ~1 s OLD ∴ BOTH their fix & ours are unusable @ our rate.** ∴ FIX THE RATE FIRST & the smoothing question DISSOLVES — do ⊥ engineer smoothing around a slow model|V856,T976,T1024,T1039

T986|.|**DRAG A NODE INTO AN EXPRESSION FIELD TO WRITE ITS REFERENCE. owner: *being able to drag a node from the preview while another is selected, to then drop it into the expression field for this to write out the handle to get to the value of it, would be so neat*.** ⚑**THE REFERENCE SYNTAX IS THE THING NOBODY CAN GUESS & THE ONE THING A DRAG CAN SUPPLY**: `op('<label>').chan.<field>` — & 2 details make it unguessable, BOTH of which a drag would get right by construction: **the name is the node's *LABEL*, ⊥ its id** (§B170: ids are EDGE ADDRESSES, & that exact confusion left 2 shipped drives dead for months), & **the FIELD is a channel of the node's published BAG**, which is invisible until something consumes it (§T982's finding). ∴ a drag writes `op('midiin1').chan.` & — since the source node's bag is KNOWN at drop time — ? offer its fields, turning the least discoverable syntax ∈ the app into a gesture. ⚠**INSERT AT THE CARET & ⊥ REPLACE**: the owner's phrasing (*write out the handle to get to the value*) is a REFERENCE dropped INTO an expression, ⊥ an expression replaced ∴ `op('lfo1').chan.value * 0.5 + 0.2` ! be reachable by dropping then typing. related surface: §T935's gizmos & §T968's arm-&-capture — all 3 are *the app knows the answer & the user is retyping it*|B170,T897,T901,T935,T968,T982

V836|**THE PANEL'S LIVE READOUT COSTS THE WHOLE INSPECTOR SUBTREE PER SAMPLE ∴ THE INTERVAL IS THE WRONG KNOB.** measured w/ a React `Profiler` over 20 live samples: 21 commits / 20 samples (clean, ⊥ cascade) but each commit is the ENTIRE Inspector — `useLiveFrame`'s `setFrame` lives ∈ `Inspector` — plus **2 full `resolveParameters` passes per render** (`resolved` + `live`). jsdom: **3.89 ms/commit** small panel, **8.28 ms/commit** realistic (12 numeric params, 3 driven) ∴ @ 10 Hz = **83 ms/s ≈ 8% of the main thread, continuously, while the inspector is open on an animated node**; @ 30 Hz ≈ 25% & an 8.3 ms stall every 33 ms = half a 60 fps frame lost every other frame. ∴ **RAISING `LIVE_VALUE_INTERVAL_MS` SCALES THE WHOLE PANEL LINEARLY & IS THE WRONG FIX; NARROW *WHAT* RE-RENDERS** — land the sample ∈ a LEAF subscriber ∴ one sample repaints one field's text (~0.1–0.3 ms) & 30–60 Hz becomes free. 100 ms STAYS until then; 50 ms is the survivable stopgap. ⚑caveat stated by the measurer: **jsdom numbers, ⊥ a real browser** (real is likely 2–5× faster) — the SHAPE holds, the absolute % does ⊥|T988,V16,T714

V830|**`disabled` IS ⊥ THE WAY TO SAY *YOU ⊥ TYPE HERE*. a control the user may ⊥ EDIT but ! still READ is READ-ONLY, ⊥ DISABLED.** the 2 differ ∈ exactly the way that matters here: `disabled` means *inert & unimportant, skip me* — it dims the VALUE, drops the control from tab order & tells a screen reader to pass over it. but a driven parameter is the OPPOSITE of unimportant: it is the one moving number on the panel, & the user's whole question is *what is it right now*. ∴ ∀ non-static parameter (`expression|bind|driven|map`, whole-slot ∨ per-component §V113): ! REFUSE the edit, ! REMAIN LEGIBLE & FOCUSABLE, ! UPDATE LIVE, & ! CARRY A POSITIVE MARK saying WHAT drives it — ⊥ merely the absence of editability. **the mark ! be a positive signal, ⊥ a negation: *greyed out* is the same pixel as *broken*, *loading*, *unsupported* & *not licensed*, & the owner ! ⊥ have to disambiguate 5 states from 1 colour**|T988,V113,V811,V17

V879|⚑**ENUMERATE FROM THE SAME FUNNEL THE READER REFUSES THROUGH — an OFFER & a REFUSAL that consult different sources are 2 answers to one question, & the menu is the one that lies.** §T990: the enumerator lives ∈ `node-references.ts` **BESIDE THE READER** ∴ offer & refusal share the same 2 namespace constants, the same `schemaOf` funnel & the same `componentNamesFor`. & the gate is the shape worth copying: **`reference-completion.test.ts` WALKS EVERY OFFERED PATH BACK THROUGH THE REAL READER & FAILS IF ANY COMES BACK *there is no such thing*** ∴ **§V150 AS A PROPERTY RATHER THAN A PROMISE** — ⊥ a list of cases someone remembered, but *whatever you offer, you ! be able to read*. ∴ ∀ completion, palette ∨ picker: derive the offer from the CONSUMER's own resolution path, & gate the round trip rather than the contents|V150,V844,V848,B170,T990
V880|⚑**A MOTION PARAMETER ON A NODE THAT CANNOT MOVE IS A DEAD CONTROL W/ A CLOCK — the knob is accepted, the value is stored, & ⊥ONE READS IT.** measured @ §T1029/E52: the haze was a `simplex3d`, **which HAS ⊥ TIME AXIS**, & its `speed` parameter was INERT — **a static picture WEARING A MOTION KNOB.** the owner sees a control, sets it, & nothing happens; every downstream claim about *animation* is then false while every gate about *parameters* passes. ∴ §V146's dead-control family w/ the aggravating factor that **the affordance ITSELF is the lie**: a disabled control says *⊥ here*, an ignored one says *yes* & means *⊥*. ! a parameter whose whole job is to drive TIME be declared only where a time axis exists — & the cheap check is the one that caught it: **ADD THE AXIS & WATCH A LIVENESS GATE FAIL ON `t = 0`**|V146,V830,V876,T1029 ⚑**2ND & 3RD INSTANCES, both from the author's side: §T1037's `hueoffset: 0.55` (degrees, ∴ 0.0015 turns, invisible — §T1069) & the E52/E53 washes, where **hsv-SATURATING A MULTI-HUE NOISE AVERAGES TO WHITE-GREY PASTEL** ∴ a saturation knob @ 0.85 was TURNED HARD & DID VISIBLY NOTHING. ∴ the family is wider than *a node w/ ⊥ time axis*: **a control ? be inert ∵ THE OPERATION IS A NO-OP ON THIS INPUT** — saturating what has no single hue, offsetting a cyclic value by a normalised fraction. the fix ∈ both cases was to change THE INPUT (a MONO cloud tinted w/ solid ink), ⊥ the knob
V881|**A SPANNING REGEX OVER INTENTIONAL NEAR-DUPLICATES IS THE WRONG TOOL FOR REMOVING THEM.** §T1063: the first consolidation of the 5 instance-shape chains used a DOTALL match that ran **from the canonical const through 700 LINES & GUTTED THE FILE** — caught by a SYMBOL COUNT, restored, redone w/ anchored indices. ⚑the trap is structural, ⊥ careless: **de-duplication targets text that LOOKS THE SAME BY DESIGN, so the pattern that finds copy 1 also finds the boundary of copy 5 & everything between** — & a greedy match over near-identical regions is maximally dangerous exactly where duplication lives. ∴ anchor by INDEX, ⊥ by pattern; & **verify a consolidation by COUNTING SYMBOLS BEFORE & AFTER**, ∵ a gutted file still parses & its tests still import|V870,T1063
V882|⚑⚑**MAKE THE SEAM *REQUIRED* — an optional prop plus a self-supplying test is EXACTLY how a feature stays green while dead, & a required one turns that regression into a COMPILE ERROR.** §T1065's construction & the structural answer to §V272/§V844, which we have now hit SEVEN times ∈ one day: the predecessor pane was optional-prop'd & its 8 tests HANDED THEMSELVES the prop ∴ **had the app quietly stopped passing it, every test would have stayed green** — which is precisely how it sat dead. ∴ `InspectorPane`'s `components` prop is now REQUIRED & **the app-level threading is THE TYPE CHECKER'S PROBLEM**, ⊥ a gate's. ⚑the general rule: **a test CANNOT guard a supply it provides itself** (§V844) ∴ where the supply is structural, ENCODE IT ∈ THE TYPE rather than asserting it — a compile error is the only gate that ⊥ be satisfied by the test's own fixture. & the corollary: **⊥ make a prop optional ∵ *some callers might ⊥ have it* — that is the sentence that ships dead seams**; find out whether a caller genuinely lacks it, & if ⊥ one does, it is ⊥ optional|V272,V844,V855,T1065
V883|⚑**A DERIVED COMPANION ! TRAVEL W/ ITS SOURCE — IF A CALLER *CAN* RE-DERIVE IT, ONE EVENTUALLY WILL, & WRONGLY.** §T1066: `runExample` returned `document` & `components` while the COMPONENT-AWARE node view stayed inside; the oracle re-derived a bare registry & **severed every component instance ∈ the plan w/o throwing.** the fix is ⊥ *remember to pass the registry* — it is that **the runner now HANDS BACK the aware view beside the components: SPLITTING THAT PAIR *IS* THE BUG.** ⚑& the reason it went unnoticed for so long is the aggravating half: **A DEGRADED COMPILE IS ⊥ A FAILED ONE.** `unknown-node-type` is a DIAGNOSTIC, the edge severs as endpoint-missing, & the result is a VALID EMPTY PLAN — so every downstream assertion runs happily against a black rectangle. ∴ ∀ harness that compiles: **ASSERT THE DIAGNOSTIC SET IS EMPTY & THE PASS COUNT IS NON-ZERO** before asserting anything about pixels — a plan that compiled is ⊥ the same as a plan that compiled WHAT YOU MEANT|V844,V854,V877,T1066

## §P PARALLEL PLAN

wave = barrier. tracks ∈ wave run concurrent. track owns disjoint paths → ⊥ write collision.
rule: track ⊥ edit file outside owned paths. shared contract frozen @ wave 0.
cross-track need → raise, ⊥ patch other track path.
**⊥ transient probe files ∈ `src/`. an audit that writes `zz-probe.ts` & self-cleans still breaks `pnpm typecheck` for EVERY other session ∈ the window it exists. probe ∈ the scratchpad — it audits identically & is invisible to the shared tree.

**THE INDEX IS SHARED. `git add <path> && git commit` is ⊥ SAFE.**
`git add` ADDS to an index other sessions are also staging into; `git commit` then commits
the WHOLE index. staging explicitly protects nothing — the sweep happens on the COMMITTER's
side & takes whatever anyone else left staged.
**`git rm` STAGES.** a staged deletion sits ∈ the shared index & rides the next bare commit
from ANY session. for deletions: plain `rm`, then name the path ∈ `git commit -- <paths>`.
that is the door the path rule ⊥ cover.

**`git diff HEAD` before committing catches a STALE EDITOR BUFFER too.** an Edit wrote back a
buffer that predated another session's committed line & silently reverted it; the diff caught it
& the line was restored. the tool-level hazard is the same shape as the index one: what you are
committing is ⊥ only what you typed.

**READ THE INDEX BEFORE COMMITTING: `git diff --cached --stat`.** ⊥ after — printing it ∈ the
same command as the commit shows you the contamination ∈ the output of the thing that already
happened. that is how HEAD got a dangling export: another track's STAGED DELETIONS rode a commit
whose author had named 4 explicit paths of their own.

**PATH SCOPING IS FILE-LEVEL.** `commit -- <paths>` protects against the INDEX; it ⊥ split
co-resident HUNKS inside a file 2 tracks are both editing. the 4th "sweep" was ⊥ a rule breach
— the committer used the correct form & the file was legitimately theirs to commit while ALSO
carrying another track's uncommitted hunks. I diagnosed it as a breach & was wrong.
∴ before committing a SHARED file: `git diff HEAD -- <file>`, eyeball for foreign hunks, &
either coordinate the land order | accept & NOTE the rider ∈ the message.
NUANCE: `-- <paths>` ⊥ reference UNTRACKED files (`pathspec did not match`). for NEW files:
`git add <the new files ONLY>` then `git commit -- <all paths>` — the scoping still holds.
! `git commit -- <paths>` (| `git commit <paths>`): commits ONLY those paths, whatever else
sits ∈ the index.
3 incidents ∈ 1 session. the 3rd was MINE, & my own rule was the insufficient one: I wrote
"explicit paths ∈ `git add`" & then swept 968 lines of a track's staged work into a SPEC
commit while following it. a rule that names the wrong command trains people to feel safe.
⊥ `git add -A` | `git add .` | `git commit -a` while tracks live.** explicit paths ONLY. a track swept 7 files of another session's uncommitted work into its commit; repaired w/ `git restore --staged` (index only, ⊥ worktree) & disclosed. `-A` is ⊥ a convenience here, it is a cross-session data hazard — the sweeping track cannot know what it took. HAPPENED TWICE: the 2nd time a `commit -a` swept another track's STAGED diff into an unrelated spec commit. stage explicit paths, ∀ time.

**GATES THAT LIE — ! know which command actually checks:**
- bare `tsc --noEmit` @ root checks NOTHING & exits 0 (references-only tsconfig, `files: []`). ! `pnpm typecheck`.
- `vitest` ⊥ typecheck. a suite is green while the types are red.
- a unit test on shader SOURCE (`toContain("frameU.time")`) is ⊥ evidence a pixel moved (V147, B15).
∀ 3 have already produced a false green this project. a gate you ⊥ verified is a gate you ⊥ have.

⊥ `git stash` | `git checkout` | any tree-wide git op while tracks live — stash cycles OTHER tracks' uncommitted work. blame a file w/ `git diff HEAD -- <path>`, ⊥ tree-wide state changes.

B264|2026-10-06|**FIXED `71be6d69` (§T1641b slice 2: an error at the write and at rest, with the colour rule said): A PARAMETER SLOT UNDER A KEY THE NODE DOES NOT DECLARE IS A WARNING, AND THE VALUE IS SILENTLY NOT DRIVEN (found by shaderloom-f1; the same family as §B262).** repro: a Custom WGSL (or a Point Kernel) whose Params has `eyeColor: vec3f`; store `"eyeColor.x"`, `"eyeColor.y"`, `"eyeColor.z"` as expression slots. a vec3f whose name looks like a colour is a COLOUR parameter (`params-reflection.ts`, `looksLikeColour`), so its parts are r, g, b and `.x` is not a key. observed: `compiler/parameter-unknown` as a WARNING ("Node \"wgsl_haze\" carries parameter \"eyeColor.x\", which \"customWgslMulti\" does not declare."), the save path wrote it, and every frame rendered with the static colour — the robot's light in the air stayed red whatever its lenses did, for a day; a position-like vec3f beside it (`eyesAt.x`) worked, which is why it read as right. two things wanted: (1) §T1641b's question — a slot nobody reads is refused where the document is built; (2) THE NAMING RULE IS INVISIBLE FROM THE WGSL: nothing in `struct Params { eyeColor: vec3f }` says its parts are r, g, b, and the diagnostic does not say "this is a colour; its parts are r, g, b" nor name the declared keys — it must (a suggestion naming the nearest declared keys). the consumer's own guard: `director.test.ts` fails on any `compiler/parameter-unknown`, and its `render.ts` stops on it.|T1561b,B262,T1641b
B263|2026-10-06|**FIXED `4d8687b0` (a workaround and a warning; the bug is Apple's): AN UNSIGNED `/` OR `%` OF A VALUE THAT CAME OUT OF A WRAPPING MULTIPLY AND A SHIFT RETURNS GARBAGE IN A MATERIAL · WGSL (found by shaderloom-f1, Dawn on Metal, M3 Max; `ac5040c9`).** repro, inside a Material · WGSL `surface()` with `pair` a whole-valued f32 from a point attribute: `let a = u32(pair + 0.5); let m = ((a + 2931u) * 2654435761u) >> 16u;`, written to emissive and the byte read back. for pair 5 (m = 35899 on the CPU): `m & 255u` = 59 correct; shifts correct; `(m * 100u) >> 16u` = 54 correct; BUT `m / 97u` came back 386 (true 370), `m % 97u` and `m % 100u` came back at or over 255 (true 9 and 99), and `m - (m / 100u) * 100u` the same; pairs 13–16 each give a different wrong quotient (not one wrong divisor). `(a + 2931u) % 100u`, with no multiply before it, is correct. so multiply, shift and mask agree with the CPU to the bit and only divide and modulo after them do not. NOT TRACED: whether it is Tint's output (its divide and modulo helpers) or Apple's compiler; whether a compute kernel shows it as well as a fragment program. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE CONSUMER: an integer hash followed by `% n` is the obvious way to draw a lot per instance or per cell, and here it silently disagrees with the same line on the CPU — the stock WGSL (hash and random modules, `// @use` snippets, kernels, the Group predicate) must be searched for the same pattern. wanted: a minimal repro on Dawn in a fragment AND a compute program with exact expected values; the cause named from the generated MSL and Apple's compiler output (as §B260 was read); every stock use found; then a fix at the source (a safe helper the generators emit, or a refusal), and a gate. the consumer scales by multiply and shift instead (`fixtureLot`), held by its `fixtures.gpu.test.ts`. **REPRODUCED THROUGH THE REAL STACK IN BOTH STAGES AND THE CAUSE NAMED (2026-10-06; M3 Max, macOS 26.3.1, one machine, one driver).** a Point Kernel (compute), sixteen points: `m` matches the CPU on all sixteen and `m / 97u`, `m % 97u`, `m % 100u` are wrong on all 48 (m = 35899: 386 for 370, 63993 for 9, 59035 for 99); a Material · WGSL (fragment): the same wrong values. THE CAUSE IS IN APPLE'S DRIVER BACKEND, not Tint and not Apple's front end: Tint's Metal source is right and unsigned; Apple's front end (`xcrun metal -S -emit-llvm`) legally narrows the divide to 16 bits because the value fits (`lshr i32 …, 16` → `trunc … to i16` → `udiv i16 …, 97`), and that IR is still correct; the device returns garbage for exactly that shape. THE SHAPE, pinned by 45 lines on the raw device (512 inputs each): the WHOLE HIGH HALF of a 32-bit value used directly as the dividend of `/` or `%` by a CONSTANT that is not a power of two — `(x >> 16u) / C` and `% C` for C = 3, 10, 97, 100, 255, 1000, `(x / 65536u) % 97u`, `((x >> 8u) >> 8u) % 97u`, the signed and vector forms. the multiply is not needed. RIGHT: a power-of-two divisor, a divisor the shader cannot know, the whole word, a shift by 15, 17, 20, 24 or 25, the low half, a byte or 12 bits of the high half, ANYTHING between the shift and the divide (`((x >> 16u) + 1u) % 97u`), `extractBits(x, 16u, 16u) % 97u`, float, multiply and shift. (the machine code is not visible: "the backend takes the wrong half-register in its divide-by-constant sequence" is a hypothesis; with the high half zero, `/ 3` returns the LOW half over 3.) NO STOCK OR SHIPPED WGSL HAS THE SHAPE: all 9 shifts by 16 in `src/` and all 74 in shipped documents are the xor fold `x ^ (x >> 16u)`, a whole word; the 85 unsigned divides or modulos by a literal in stock sources have vertex indices, faces, cells, ids and float conversions as dividends. not tested: a vertex stage, a browser, another Apple GPU; not searched: author WGSL outside the repository. LEAD'S RULING ON THE FIX (to build after §T1623b slice 2): (a) a stock helper in the hash module for what people want — a lot in 0..n−1 from a hash, `((h >> 16u) * n) >> 16u`, exact against the CPU and a multiply cheaper than a divide — named in the Point Kernel's and Material · WGSL's descriptions; (b) a named WARNING through the Problems registry when an author's WGSL divides a bare high half by a constant (text-level, same function; it says what to write instead; a warning and not a refusal because the WGSL is valid and right on other GPUs; no rewriting of author text — there is no parser to do it safely); (c) a text gate that the shape is absent from both generators' output and every shipped document, a Dawn test that the helper equals the CPU on 512 inputs, and the driver canary kept as a committed tool script to run on an OS or browser bump, not as a gate; (d) the evidence written to `docs/` with a 12-line shader, ready for the OWNER to file with Dawn and Apple (nothing filed). **FIXED AS RULED `4d8687b0` (verified on main: typecheck; both `wgsl-high-half` test files with the generated-text gates and `light-points` 119; on Dawn `hash-lot` and `light-points` 21; the 26 catalogue walkers 444; the gates 59 files / 3,586).** THE BUG IS APPLE'S, NOW PROVEN RATHER THAN INFERRED: a Metal kernel with no Dawn and no Tint returns the same wrong value (`(x >> 16u) % 97u` gives 15872 for x = 96, where the answer is 0), and the Metal source Dawn dumped, run by Metal alone, returns Dawn's wrong values. THE QUOTIENT IS WRONG ONLY THROUGH TINT'S ZERO-DIVISOR GUARD: plain Metal `(x >> 16u) / 97u` is right (Apple's front end folds it into `udiv i32 %x, 6356992`, no 16-bit divide exists); as `a / select(b, 1u, b == 0u)` it is not folded, a `udiv i16` is emitted and the device returns 512 for x = 96; the remainder is wrong in both forms. the trigger read from Apple's compiler output: a `udiv i16` or `urem i16` by a constant that is not a power of two whose dividend is `trunc(lshr i32 x, 16)`; the mechanism inside the driver stays a hypothesis. BUILT: (a) a shared module `lot` (`// @use lot`) with `hashLot(h, n) = ((h >> 16u) * n) >> 16u` and its CPU twin `hashLotReference` (`shared-modules.ts`) — its own module, not part of `hash`, because `WGSL_HASH` is embedded in every Noise shader and adding to it would move every shipped text that includes it; named in the Point Kernel's and Material · WGSL's descriptions. (b) the warning `compiler/wgsl-high-half-divide` (`src/compiler/wgsl-high-half.ts`), delivered at ONE site in the compiler after the plan is read: it reads every pass's text and maps a hit through the pass's source map to the author's node, parameter and line (a kernel, a Material · WGSL named once on the material, a Custom WGSL, a Group predicate; a Geometry's Group has no source map, so its warning lands on the Render with the expression quoted). (c) `wgsl-high-half.cases.ts` is the MEASURED table, 43 lines, 14 wrong and 29 right, and the detector's verdict must equal the device's on every line both ways; `src/examples/wgsl-high-half.test.ts` on `test:gates` holds the shape absent from every pass of every shipped example, every string of all 112 shipped documents, the shared modules and the two lit generators (red with the shape planted in the stock hash module: 45 example passes); `hash-lot.gpu.test.ts` holds `hashLot` equal to its twin for 512 hashes in a kernel and in a Custom WGSL. NOT GATES, tools to run on an OS, driver or browser bump: `tools/apple-gpu-divide-canary.mjs` (today 14 of 14 wrong lines wrong, every right line right) and `tools/apple-gpu-divide-metal.swift`, the pure-Metal reproduction (today 4 of 8 kernels wrong). (d) `docs/apple-gpu-divide-high-half-2026-10-06.md`: the evidence and TWO READY-TO-FILE TEXTS, one for Apple (a Metal kernel) and one for Dawn (a WGSL shader; Tint's guard is what exposes the quotient), each with expected and observed values — NOTHING FILED: the owner's to send. THE WARNING CANNOT SEE a high half that arrives as a function's result or argument, a `var`, or a divisor the compiler folds to a constant itself. not checked: another Apple GPU or macOS version, Safari (its own WGSL compiler), a vertex stage, a fragment function in pure Metal.|T1561b,B260

B260|2026-10-06|**THE RENDER'S COST GROWS FASTER THAN ITS LIGHT COUNT: 37 LIGHT NODES ARE 24 ms OF GPU AND 1.2 s OF COMPILE (found by §T1589b's design, on sentinel-bot's live tier with shadows off, lights added by script).** GPU per render 6.75 ms at 5 lights, 7.54 at 13, 10.75 at 21, 24.05 at 37 (+0.8, +4.0, +17.3 ms for +8, +16, +32); `backend.compile` 157 ms → 803 → 906 → 1,227 ms. a raw probe of the same unrolled blocks shows the same shape (0.72 / 1.38 / 9.31 ms at 16 / 64 / 256) and pipeline creation of 3 / 9 / 34 ms. cause not found: candidates are the unrolled text's size against the shader compiler's register or inlining limits, and uniform block growth. §T1589b's grid removes the need for many Light nodes but not the cliff for a document that has them (§T1623b moves named Lights with a Range into the grid). wanted: the cause named, and either a fix or a diagnostic at the count where the cliff starts. **OWNER, 2026-10-06: "this here needs urgent investigation much more than any e2e". IN INVESTIGATION**: a minimal engine scene first (a floor and N Light nodes), the factors one at a time, the generated WGSL at 4 and 32 lights, compile time by call, then the cause PROVED by a change that removes the growth; a structural cure stops for the lead's ruling because §T1589b slice 1 is in the same generators. **CAUSE FOUND AND PROVEN ON A MINIMAL ENGINE SCENE (interim report, 2026-10-06; one 16×16 floor grid, PBR, N point lights with no shadow, 1280×720, no MSAA, Dawn on Metal, M3 Max, medians of 30 frames with a fixed reference compute pass timed beside every frame).** THE LIT SUM OVER LIGHTS IS ONE STRAIGHT CHAIN OF `lit +=` ACROSS N UNROLLED BLOCKS, and Apple's Metal compiler restructures it (read from `xcrun metal -S -emit-llvm` on the MSL Dawn generates for our text): fast math is on (`reassoc` on every op), so it pulls all 2N per-light terms out of their blocks and sums them in two chains at the END of the fragment function, then SINKS every light's GGX lobe below every light's kind and range branches — the program becomes all branches for all lights, then all lobes, then the sums, and each light's toLight, attenuation and colour stay live across everything. past the register file the fragment program falls off a cliff (that last step is a hypothesis: the machine code is not visible). UNROLLED AS TODAY: 0.05 / 0.13 / 0.33 / 0.39 / 1.51 / 2.88 / 8.52 / 18.7 ms at N = 1 / 8 / 16 / 20 / 24 / 32 / 48 / 64 — linear at 0.018 ms a light to 20, ×3.8 between 20 and 24, then faster than N. PROOF: the same blocks, each block's work under `if (lightMeta.y != 0.0) { … }`: 64 lights 18.7 → 1.31 ms, 24 lights 1.50 → 0.46; a loop over an array of rows in the same uniform block: 64 lights 1.11 ms and cold pipeline creation 119 ms against 572. per fragment (64 lights: 2.1 / 5.2 / 19.1 ms at 320 / 640 / 1280 wide). RULED OUT, each by one change at 64 lights: the uniform block's size (the same floats read with trivial code: 0.19 ms), the branches on kind and range (straight-line blocks: 14.0), inlining (a function call per block: 10.6), named members against an array; MSAA, overdraw, mesh and draw count are not needed. A MEASUREMENT TRAP FOUND WITH IT: THE GPU CLOCK FOLLOWS RECENT LOAD — the same 16-light draw took 1.245 ms on an idle GPU and 0.328 ms right after a heavy run, and under contention raw samples go bimodal (19 and 44 ms for one draw); raw milliseconds without a reference pass beside them are not comparable between variants, which bends figures in `docs/lights-from-pointset-design-2026-10-06.md` and may be §B251. COMPILE TIME, first look: Metal caches compiled shaders on disk between processes — a text seen before is 30 ms, a new one 60 ms plus about 8.5 ms a light per distinct lit shader; the 157 → 803 ms above is very likely warm against cold. LEAD'S RULING: (1) a STOPGAP now — each light block's work under the light-is-on test, emitted only when a Render lists more lights than a threshold (8 unless a shipped Render has more), so every shipped text and picture holds byte for byte; gated on the cause (no run of unguarded blocks above the threshold), not on a clock. PROJECTORS add into the same `lit` (found by the audit) but do NOT lengthen the chain: their addition already sits under two branches on the fragment's own position, so `lit` is a merge after each (8 lights + 0 / 8 / 16 / 24 projectors: 0.131 / 0.262 / 0.328 / 0.459 ms, flat 0.014 ms a projector); the gate counts a projector as a source so one written without its tests fails.
